BUG-2026-06-013: gradmoa() pressure perturbation halos use scalar
copy/Neumann behavior at all non-cyclic side boundaries

• MOA.F90
 – gradmoa
• Related:
 – update.F90
 – small_implicit_forcings in force.F90, through the call to gradmoa()

Summary
gradmoa() computes the pressure perturbation pr, updates its horizontal halos, and then differentiates it
to form the pressure-gradient contribution to forceSI_xv.
The relevant code is:

call update(pr,pr,np,mp,l,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,0,0,0,0)

Because both mirror-parity flags are passed as zero,

topbot = 0
leftright = 0

pr is treated as a scalar/even quantity at symmetric boundaries. For all non-cyclic physical boundaries,
including relaxation/open/environmental boundaries, update() effectively copies the nearest physical
edge value into the ghost cells.
For example, at the right boundary:

a(nxp+i,j,k)=ae(nxp,jref,k)

so for pressure perturbation:

pr(np+1,j,k) = pr(np,j,k)
pr(np+2,j,k) = pr(np,j,k)
...

Then gradmoa() computes the pressure gradients with centered differences:

px(i,j,k)=0.5*(pr(i+1,j,k)-pr(i-1,j,k))*dxi
py(i,j,k)=0.5*(pr(i,j+1,k)-pr(i,j-1,k))*dyi

At the right physical boundary this gives:

px(np,j,k) = 0.5 * (pr(np,j,k) - pr(np-1,j,k)) / dx

rather than a fully one-sided derivative, a zero wall-normal gradient, or a derivative based on an
environmental/open-boundary pressure state.

 101

For a purely scalar field at a reflective wall, copying the scalar into the ghost cell can be a reasonable
Neumann-like condition. Therefore this is not automatically a confirmed bug.
However, it is suspicious because gradmoa() applies the same pressure-halo treatment for all non-cyclic
side boundary types. It does not distinguish between:

symmetric/mirror side boundaries,
relaxation/open/environmental side boundaries,
inflow/outflow-like side boundaries,
ordinary copied scalar boundaries.

This means the pressure perturbation used by the pressure-gradient force may not be consistent with
the velocity boundary condition or with the intended open/environmental pressure behavior.
This is especially relevant when the velocity boundary is reflective or mirror-like. The velocity update
may be trying to impose no-normal-flow behavior, while the pressure perturbation halo is simply
copied. Near a side wall, that can produce a boundary-adjacent pressure-force stripe even if the velocity
ghost-cell parity is otherwise correct.
At xmax, the most relevant path is:

call update(pr,pr,...,topbot=0,leftright=0)

followed by:

px(np,j,k)=0.5*(pr(np+1,j,k)-pr(np-1,j,k))*dxi

with:

pr(np+1,j,k) = pr(np,j,k)

so the edge pressure gradient is determined by a half-width copy condition rather than by a boundary-
condition-specific pressure treatment.

This can produce or amplify boundary-aligned pressure-gradient artifacts near physical side boundaries.

a pressure-force stripe near xmax or xmin,
spurious acceleration adjacent to reflective or open side boundaries,
red/blue velocity structures aligned with a side wall,
pressure-gradient forcing inconsistent with the velocity wall condition,
artifacts that appear in forceSI_xv before large-step advection,
artifacts that are strongest in the boundary-adjacent cell or first few cells.

The most suspicious regions are:

right physical boundary:
i = np-2 : np+ih

left physical boundary:

 102

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log June 2026

i = 1-ih : 3

top physical boundary:
j = mp-2 : mp+ih

bottom physical boundary:
j = 1-ih : 3

For the observed xmax issue, inspect:

pr(np-2:np+ih,j,k)
px(np-2:np,j,k)
forceSI_xv(np-2:np,j,k,iuvel)

If the visible artifact aligns with a pressure-gradient stripe in px or in the iuvel component of forceSI_xv,
this issue is likely contributing.

Suggested diagnostic
Add temporary diagnostic output in or immediately after gradmoa() for the right boundary:

write(*,*) ’gradmoa␣right␣boundary␣diagnostic’
write(*,*) ’pr:’, pr(np-2:np+ih,j,k)
write(*,*) ’px:’, px(np-2:np,j,k)
write(*,*) ’forceSI_xv␣u:’, forceSI_xv(np-2:np,j,k,iuvel)

A more useful diagnostic is to output the pressure-gradient contribution before other small-step forcings
are added. In gradmoa(), the relevant x-momentum pressure term is:

-(px(i,j,k)+c13(i,j)*gmul(k)*pz(i,j,k))

So outputting a separate diagnostic array such as:

pgfx(i,j,k)=-(px(i,j,k)+c13(i,j)*gmul(k)*pz(i,j,k))

would help separate pressure-gradient artifacts from gravity, Coriolis, relaxation, drag, heat-source,
and fire-related forcings.
Recommended fields to inspect:

pr
px
py
pz
c13*gmul*pz
c23*gmul*pz
-(px+c13*gmul*pz)
-(py+c23*gmul*pz)
forceSI_xv(:,:,:,iuvel)
forceSI_xv(:,:,:,ivvel)

For the xmax artifact, specifically check whether the red structure is collocated with:

px stripe near i = np

 103

or

-(px+c13*gmul*pz) stripe near i = np

Suggested fix or test
The correct fix depends on the intended pressure boundary condition.

Option 1: Keep scalar copy behavior, but document it
If the intended pressure perturbation boundary condition is zero-normal-gradient at all non-cyclic side
boundaries, then the current behavior should be documented explicitly in gradmoa().
Add a comment such as:

! Pressure perturbation pr uses scalar zero-normal-gradient/copy halos
! at all non-cyclic horizontal boundaries before computing px and py.
! This is intentional for the current pressure-gradient formulation.
call update(pr,pr,np,mp,l,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,0,0,0,0)

This does not remove the artifact risk, but it makes the assumption explicit.

Option 2: Use a boundary-condition-specific pressure halo routine
A cleaner fix would be to avoid using one generic scalar-copy update for pressure perturbation and
instead fill pressure halos according to the actual side boundary type.
For example, introduce a pressure-specific halo update:

call update_pressure_perturbation(pr,np,mp,l)

Inside that routine, handle different side-boundary types explicitly:

cyclic boundary:
  use MPI/periodic exchange

symmetric/mirror wall:
  use appropriate scalar pressure condition, likely zero-normal-gradient

relaxation/open/environmental boundary:
  either relax pressure perturbation toward zero,
  extrapolate pressure from the interior,
  or impose the environmental pressure perturbation expected by the formulation

For open/environmental boundaries, since pr is a perturbation relative to pre, one possible test condition
is:

pr ghost = 0

or a tapered blend toward zero, rather than:

pr ghost = pr edge

However, this should be checked against the intended pressure formulation before being made permanent.

 104

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log June 2026

Option 3: Test a one-sided derivative at physical side boundaries
As a diagnostic, replace the boundary-adjacent centered derivative with a one-sided derivative at
physical side edges.
For example, at the right edge:

  do k=1,l
 do j=1,mp
      px(np,j,k)=(pr(np,j,k)-pr(np-1,j,k))*dxi
 enddo
  enddo
endif

and at the left edge:

  do k=1,l
 do j=1,mp
      px(1,j,k)=(pr(2,j,k)-pr(1,j,k))*dxi
 enddo
  enddo
endif

Similarly for py at bottom/top boundaries.
This is not necessarily the final correct discretization, but it is a useful A/B test. If the boundary stripe
changes substantially, then the artifact is sensitive to the pressure-gradient boundary discretization.

Option 4: Test forcing the pressure perturbation halo to zero for open/relaxation sides
For relaxation/open/environmental side boundaries, test whether the artifact is reduced by forcing
pressure perturbation ghost cells toward zero instead of copying the edge value.
Conceptually:

if(rightedge.eq.1.and.ibc_right.ge.1.and.ibc_right.lt.5)then
  pr(np+1:np+ih,:,:) = 0.0_prec
endif

and similarly for other physical sides.
This should be treated as a diagnostic first, not an automatic final fix, because it changes the pressure
boundary condition.

Run the same case with diagnostics enabled and compare:

original scalar-copy pressure halos,
one-sided pressure-gradient edge derivative,
pressure perturbation ghost cells forced toward zero for open/relaxation sides,
flat terrain,
tapered terrain near the boundary,
reflective versus relaxation side BCs.

BUG-2026-06-014: Mirror Radiation Boundary Conditions Let
Photons Leave the Domain

Summary
The mirror/symmetric radiation boundary-condition handling in shoot_photons does not actually keep
photons in the computational domain after they cross a lateral boundary. The routine updates the
photon cell index first, which can move i1 or j1 outside the valid range, and only later flips the direction
vector for mirror boundary conditions. Because the main photon-transport loop requires i1 and j1
to be in range at the top of each iteration, the reflected photon exits the loop before it can continue
propagating.
This means mirror radiation boundary conditions can behave like absorbing/leaking boundaries for
photons that cross left, right, top, or bottom boundaries.

Affected file and routine
• File: monteCarlo_rad.F90
• Routine: shoot_photons
• Relevant boundary-condition values:
 – ibc_* == 0: cyclic boundary
 – ibc_* == 5: mirror/symmetric boundary

Evidence from current implementation
The photon-transport loop only continues while the current cell index is in range:

          do while(i1.ge.1.and.i1.le.n.and.j1.ge.1.and.j1.le.m.and. &
            k1.ge.1.and.k1.le.lmc.and.lopt.gt.0)

When the next event is an intersection with an x or y cell face, the routine immediately increments the
corresponding cell index:

 if(abs(t-tx).lt.tolerance)then
                 i1=i1+int(sign(one,dir(1)))
 elseif(abs(t-ty).lt.tolerance)then
                 j1=j1+int(sign(one,dir(2)))
 else
                 k1=k1+int(sign(one,dir(3)))
 kt=int(sign(one,dir(3)))
 endif

For cyclic boundaries, the code repairs the index and position before the next loop iteration:

 ! Cyclic boundary conditions implementation
 if(ibc_left.eq.0.and.i1.lt.1) then
 i1=i1+n
 xf=xf+n*dx
 endif
 if(ibc_right.eq.0.and.i1.gt.n) then
 i1=i1-n
 xf=xf-n*dx

 108

 endif
 if(ibc_bot.eq.0.and.j1.lt.1)then
 j1=j1+m
 yf=yf+m*dy
 endif
 if(ibc_top.eq.0.and.j1.gt.m) then
 j1=j1-m
 yf=yf-m*dy
 endif

However, the mirror/symmetric boundary handling only flips the direction vector:

 ! Mirror / symmetric boundary conditions
 if(ibc_left.eq.5.and.xf.le.tolerance) dir(1) = -dir(1)
 if(ibc_right.eq.5.and.xf.ge.(n*dx-tolerance)) dir(1) = -dir(1)
 if(ibc_top.eq.5.and.yf.le.tolerance) dir(2) = -dir(2)
 if(ibc_bot.eq.5.and.yf.ge.(m*dy-tolerance)) dir(2) = -dir(2)

There is no corresponding restoration of i1 or j1 to a valid in-domain cell. Therefore, if a photon
crosses the left boundary, i1 becomes 0; if it crosses the right boundary, i1 becomes n+1; if it crosses
the low-y boundary, j1 becomes 0; and if it crosses the high-y boundary, j1 becomes m+1.
The direction may be reflected, but the next evaluation of the do while condition terminates the loop
because the cell index is out of range.

Impact
This bug can cause photon leakage through mirror boundaries. Consequences may include:

• Under-counting photon residence/absorption near mirror boundaries.
• Incorrect radiation energy deposition near domain edges.
• Loss of the intended symmetry/no-flux behavior for radiation transport.
• Boundary-condition-dependent bias in Monte Carlo radiation results.

Mirror boundaries should be handled similarly to cyclic boundaries: after a crossing moves i1 or j1 out
of range, the code should restore the index to the adjacent in-domain cell, reflect the position across
the boundary plane, and flip the appropriate direction component.

 ! Mirror / symmetric boundary conditions
 if(ibc_left.eq.5.and.i1.lt.1) then
 i1=1
 xf=max(tolerance,-xf)
                dir(1)=-dir(1)
 endif
 if(ibc_right.eq.5.and.i1.gt.n) then
 i1=n
 xf=min(n*dx-tolerance,2.0_prec*n*dx-xf)
                dir(1)=-dir(1)
 endif
 if(ibc_bot.eq.5.and.j1.lt.1) then
 j1=1
 yf=max(tolerance,-yf)
                dir(2)=-dir(2)

 109

 endif
 if(ibc_top.eq.5.and.j1.gt.m) then
 j1=m
 yf=min(m*dy-tolerance,2.0_prec*m*dy-yf)
                dir(2)=-dir(2)
 endif

BUG-2026-06-015: Top/bottom symmetric-boundary checks are
reversed in ray-tracing mirror logic

Summary
The ray-tracing mirror/symmetric boundary checks for the y-direction appear to use the wrong
boundary-condition variables in both:

• Monte-Carlo radiation photon tracing, in shoot_photons
• Solar shade/heating ray tracing, in solarHeating

The current logic checks:

if(ibc_top.eq.5.and.yf.le.tolerance) dir(2) = -dir(2)
if(ibc_bot.eq.5.and.yf.ge.(m*dy-tolerance)) dir(2) = -dir(2)

This is reversed. In the rest of the codebase, the convention is:

• Bottom y-boundary: yf <= 0
• Top y-boundary: yf >= m*dy

Therefore the mirror checks should be:

if(ibc_bot.eq.5.and.yf.le.tolerance) dir(2) = -dir(2)
if(ibc_top.eq.5.and.yf.ge.(m*dy-tolerance)) dir(2) = -dir(2)

The x-direction checks appear consistent.

Affected code
Both shoot_photons and solarHeating contain the same reversed y-direction mirror boundary conditions.

Impact
This bug is masked when both top and bottom boundaries are symmetric, but if the user configures
asymmetric y-boundaries, for example:

ibc_bot = 5
ibc_top = 1

then rays hitting the bottom boundary will not be reflected as intended, while top-boundary behavior
may be incorrectly controlled by the bottom setting.
This can affect:

• Radiative absorption/distribution from Monte-Carlo photons
• Solar shading/insolation calculations
• Vegetation heating rates
• Any cases using symmetric/mirror boundary conditions only on one y-boundary

- if(ibc_top.eq.5.and.yf.le.tolerance) dir(2) = -dir(2)

BUG-2026-06-016: shoot_photons bottom-surface quadratic branch
tests acoeftop instead of acoefbot

Summary
In the Monte Carlo radiation photon-tracing routine shoot_photons, the bottom-surface intersection
logic computes bottom-face quadratic coefficients:

• acoefbot
• bcoefbot
• ccoefbot

but then incorrectly tests acoeftop when deciding whether the bottom-surface equation is linear or
quadratic.
The bottom branch should test acoefbot, not acoeftop.

Current buggy code

if(kt.le.0)then
  if(abs(acoeftop).lt.tolerance)then !a.eq.0
 if(ccoefbot*bcoefbot.lt.0.) tz=-ccoefbot/bcoefbot
  else
 delta=bcoefbot**2-4*acoefbot*ccoefbot
 if(delta.gt.0.)then
 tz1=-0.5*(bcoefbot-sqrt(delta))/acoefbot
 tz2=-0.5*(bcoefbot+sqrt(delta))/acoefbot
      if(tz1.gt.0.)then
 tz=tz1
        if(tz2.gt.0.) tz=min(tz1,tz2)
 elseif(tz2.gt.0.)then
 tz=tz2
 endif
 endif
  endif
elseif(abs(acoeftop).gt.tolerance)then
  if(bcoefbot*acoefbot.lt.0) tz=-bcoefbot/acoefbot
endif

Why this is incorrect
The top and bottom cell faces may have different bilinear surface shapes, especially in terrain-following
grids, fuel-zone AZ layers, or non-planar cells.
The a coefficient determines whether the ray/surface intersection should be solved as a linear equation
or a quadratic equation.
For the top face, the correct coefficient is acoeftop.
For the bottom face, the correct coefficient is acoefbot.
Using acoeftop in the bottom branch can cause the code to:

• Treat a genuinely quadratic bottom surface as linear.

 114

• Treat a nearly linear bottom surface as quadratic.
• Divide by a near-zero acoefbot in the quadratic formula.
• Skip valid bottom intersections.
• Choose the wrong photon exit face.
• Produce incorrect absorption locations and radiative energy deposition.

- if(abs(acoeftop).lt.tolerance)then
+ if(abs(acoefbot).lt.tolerance)then

...

- elseif(abs(acoeftop).gt.tolerance)then
+ elseif(abs(acoefbot).gt.tolerance)then

Impact
This bug affects photon transport in the Monte Carlo radiation model.
Potential consequences include:

• Incorrect photon crossing distance tz
• Wrong face selected as the next photon exit face
• Incorrect movement between AZ cells
• Incorrect photon absorption counts
• Incorrect radiative heating/cooling
• Possible numerical instability

The issue is likely hidden for flat or nearly planar cells. It is more likely to matter for non-flat
topography, terrain-following distorted cells, and complex fuel-zone structures.

Git evidence: 5e20226 (2026-06-15, radiation acoefbot typo fix); 869ead7 (2026-06-25, boundary-error
pass).
The bottom-surface photon branch in CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90 was changed from acoeftop
to acoefbot; the later boundary-error pass carried the corrected branch forward.

BUG-2026-06-017: Missing cyclic-pair validation allows inconsistent
MPI/domain boundary state

Summary
Removing cyclic-pair validation allows one-sided periodic boundaries that conflict with MPI halo
topology and domain physics.
The previous validation required cyclic boundary conditions to be paired by direction. Those checks
were removed. As a result, invalid asymmetric configurations such as:

ibc_left = 0
ibc_right = 1

are now accepted.
However, setup_MPI still constructs MPI neighbors using periodic wraparound in both horizontal
directions. That means halo exchange remains toroidal even if only one side is declared cyclic. The
resulting configuration is internally inconsistent: one global edge wraps periodically while the opposite
edge is treated as a physical/non-cyclic boundary.

Why this is a real bug
setup_MPI always builds wraparound neighbors.
For x-direction:

peleft=mpi_rank-1
if (peleft<((mpos-1)*nprocx)) peleft=mpi_rank+(nprocx-1)

peright=mpi_rank+1
if (peright>(mpos*nprocx-1)) peright=mpi_rank-(nprocx-1)

So the MPI topology is always periodic/toroidal.
But physical edge flags are set independently:

if((ibc_right.gt.0).and.(mod((mpi_rank+1),nprocx)==0)) rightedge=1

if((ibc_left.gt.0).and.(mod((mpi_rank+1),nprocx)==1.or.nprocx==1)) &
  leftedge=1

This means ibc_left = 0, ibc_right = 1 creates behavior where the left global boundary is treated as
cyclic, the right global boundary is treated as physical, and MPI halo exchange still wraps left/right
processors.

Impact
This can cause silent numerical/physical errors, including:

• Wrong halo values near one boundary
• Inconsistent gradients near lateral edges
• Non-conservative or asymmetric transport

 117

• Incorrect advection near boundaries
• Incorrect radiation ray wrapping
• Incorrect firebrand wrapping/removal behavior
• Inconsistent topography/metric ghost cells
• Hard-to-debug boundary artifacts

The issue is especially dangerous because the simulation can continue without crashing.

Expected behavior
The code should reject configurations where only one side of a horizontal pair is cyclic.
Valid examples:

ibc_left = 0
ibc_right = 0

ibc_left = 1
ibc_right = 5

Invalid examples:

ibc_left = 0
ibc_right = 1

ibc_bot = 0
ibc_top = 3

The key rule is: For each horizontal direction, cyclicity must be paired. Either both sides are 0, or
neither side is 0.

Restore validation in setup_MPI after MPI initialization:

  if ((ibc_left.eq.0) .neqv. (ibc_right.eq.0)) then

 print*,’BOUNDARY␣CONDITION␣ERROR’
 print*,’ibc_left␣and␣ibc_right␣must␣both␣be␣cyclic␣or␣both␣non-cyclic’
 print*,’Cyclic␣boundary␣condition␣value␣is␣0’
 print*,’ibc_left␣=’,ibc_left,’␣ibc_right␣=’,ibc_right
 endif
 call mpi_finalize(ierror)
 STOP
  endif

  if ((ibc_bot.eq.0) .neqv. (ibc_top.eq.0)) then

 print*,’BOUNDARY␣CONDITION␣ERROR’
 print*,’ibc_bot␣and␣ibc_top␣must␣both␣be␣cyclic␣or␣both␣non-cyclic’
 print*,’Cyclic␣boundary␣condition␣value␣is␣0’
 print*,’ibc_bot␣=’,ibc_bot,’␣ibc_top␣=’,ibc_top
 endif
 call mpi_finalize(ierror)
 STOP
  endif

BUG-2026-06-019: Symmetric BC support for radiation/solar is
broken, and firebrands are not safe enough

Summary
Removing the input guards that disallowed radiation and firebrands with symmetric boundary conditions
introduces a real regression.

• Radiation / solarHeating: symmetric reflection is currently incorrect.
• Firebrands: reflection is closer to correct, but exact-boundary handling can still produce invalid
  processor assignment.

Actual behavior
1. Radiation / solar rays do not properly reflect
Both shoot_photons and solarHeating only flip direction at symmetric boundaries but do not reset i1 /
j1 or move xf / yf back inside the valid domain.
Result: symmetric boundaries behave like leaky/absorbing boundaries rather than mirrors.

2. Top/bot checks are reversed in radiation/solar
Current code:

if(ibc_top.eq.5.and.yf.le.tolerance) ...
if(ibc_bot.eq.5.and.yf.ge.(m*dy-tolerance)) ...

But geometrically:

• yf <= 0 is the bottom
• yf >= m*dy is the top

So those conditions are reversed.

3. Firebrand reflection still has unsafe exact-boundary cases
evolveFB does perform a real reflection, but it still allows exact-boundary values to persist. If xvbrand
,→ (it,ix) == n*dx, then after reflection it is still n*dx. Later processor ownership computation can
produce an invalid mpi_rank_fb.

4. Firebrand feature maturity concern
The igniteFB() subroutine is empty/stubbed out, indicating the feature is not fully implemented.

Immediate safe fix
Restore the removed input guards for:

• radiation with symmetric BCs

 122

• firebrands with symmetric BCs

This is the safest short-term fix and matches current implementation reality.

Follow-up fix
If symmetric support is intended to remain enabled:

• fix ray reflection in shoot_photons
• fix ray reflection in solarHeating
• clamp reflected firebrands strictly inside the domain
• clamp processor assignment inputs
• add targeted tests before removing guards again

Git evidence: 070ccdf (2026-06-08, firebrand reflection boundaries); 3a1258c (2026-06-08, firebrand
mirror-boundary fixes); dc9c30c (2026-06-08, radiation/firebrand mirror-boundary enabling); 6102606
(2026-06-04, cyclic/symmetric boundary support).
Symmetric/mirror behavior was added across radiation, solar heating, cyclic boundaries, and firebrands.
The later firebrand commits split boundary checks and made the mirror paths safer before the old
stops were removed.

BUG-2026-06-020: Bottom-right corner uses topedge instead of
botedge

Summary
The bottom-right corner logic in update.F90 checks topedge in two places where it should check botedge.

Affected locations
• update.F90:592
• update.F90:636

Current code

if(topedge.eq.1.and.rightedge.eq.1) then ! Domain bot right corner

and later in the same bottom-right block:

else if(topedge.eq.1) then

This block is explicitly handling the bottom-right corner. The comment says Domain bot right corner,
the write indices are bottom ghost/corner cells:

a(nxp+i,1-j,k)

and the branch uses bottom-boundary logic:

ibc_bot

Therefore the edge test should use botedge, not topedge.

Impact
On processors that are on the physical bottom boundary but not the top boundary, the intended
bottom-right corner boundary logic will not run. Conversely, processors on the top-right boundary
may incorrectly enter bottom-corner handling. This can corrupt ghost/corner cells near a(nxp+i,1-j,k).

BUG-2026-06-021: Upper-left corner send omits i0/j0 staggered-grid
offsets

Summary
The upper-left corner send buffer in update.F90 omits the iperiod-dependent staggered-grid offsets i0
and j0.

Affected location
• update.F90:578

Current code

tmpcorsnd(ncount)=a(i,nyp-ih+j,k)

The other corner-send blocks apply the iperiod-dependent offsets i0 and/or j0 so that staggered variables
send the correct interior strip. For example, the other corner sends use patterns like:

a(nxp-i0-ih+i,nyp-j0-ih+j,k)
a(nxp-i0-ih+i,j+j0,k)
a(i+i0,j+j0,k)

The upper-left send should be symmetric with those blocks and should include both offsets:

a(i+i0,nyp-j0-ih+j,k)

Impact
For cell-centered variables this may be masked when i0 = 0 and j0 = 0. For staggered variables,
especially those using iperiod = 1 or iperiod = 2, the wrong strip of interior cells can be sent to the
diagonal neighbor. This affects corner ghost-cell values exchanged with perightbelow.

tmpcorsnd(ncount)=a(i+i0,nyp-j0-ih+j,k)

Git evidence: 0792741 (2026-06-15, mirrored-boundary corner rewrite); 23370e2 (2026-06-18, multi-halo
mirror reflection).
The upper-left and related corner sends were folded into the new corner-send logic that accounts for
staggered-grid offsets and multi-halo reflection.

BUG-2026-06-023: ibc=5 mirror/reflective boundary uses constant
extrapolation instead of true mirrored ghost cells

Summary
update.F90 currently treats ibc_* = 5 as a "Mirror Velocity" boundary condition, but the implementation
only mirrors the sign of the normal velocity component. It does not mirror the spatial index of the
interior field into the ghost cells.
As a result, for halo width ih > 1, every ghost layer is filled from the same boundary-adjacent interior
cell. This is equivalent to constant extrapolation, or zero-gradient fill, with a sign flip for the normal
velocity component. It is not a true reflective/mirrored extension of the interior state.
This can degrade or corrupt high-order stencils near reflective boundaries, because ghost cells beyond
the first layer do not contain the expected reflected interior values.

Current behavior
At the left boundary, for normal velocity iuv == 1 and ibc_left == 5, the code currently does:

a(1-i,j,k) = -a(1,j,k)

For ih = 3, this gives:

a(0,j,k) = -a(1,j,k)
a(-1,j,k) = -a(1,j,k)
a(-2,j,k) = -a(1,j,k)

All ghost layers are copied from the same boundary cell.
Similarly, for non-normal components or scalar fields, the current else branch does:

a(1-i,j,k) = a(1,j,k)

so all ghost layers are constant copies of the boundary cell.

Expected behavior
For a true mirror/reflective boundary, each ghost layer should map to the corresponding interior layer.
For the left boundary:

a(1-i,j,k) = +/- a(i,j,k)

For ih = 3, this gives:

a(0,j,k) = +/- a(1,j,k)
a(-1,j,k) = +/- a(2,j,k)
a(-2,j,k) = +/- a(3,j,k)

The sign should be negative for the velocity component normal to the reflective wall, and positive for
tangential velocity components and scalar fields.

 135

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log June 2026

Why this matters
With a one-cell halo, the current implementation and a true mirror implementation are identical for
the first ghost cell. The bug becomes important when ih > 1 or when high-order advection, diffusion,
filtering, pressure-gradient, or interpolation stencils use multiple ghost layers.
Example for a left reflective wall and interior values:

i = 1 2 3
u = 10 7 4

Current implementation:

i = -2    -1      0        1        2   3
u = -10   -10    -10       10       7   4

True odd reflection:

i = -2    -1       0       1        2   3
u = -4    -7      -10      10       7   4

These are not equivalent for any stencil that uses more than one ghost cell.
For scalars or tangential components, the same issue exists with even reflection.
Current implementation:

q = 10    10    10    10   7    4

True even reflection:

q =   4    7    10    10   7    4

The current ibc=5 logic only checks whether the field is the normal velocity component. If so, it flips
the sign. Otherwise, it falls through to the same Neumann/constant-extension logic used for all other
boundary types.
This means ibc=5 does not receive a distinct even-reflection path for non-normal components or scalar
fields.

Proposed fix
For physical boundaries where ibc_* == 5:

• use odd reflection for the velocity component normal to the boundary;
• use even reflection for all other variables;
• preserve the existing Neumann/constant-extension behavior for non-reflective boundary types.

Suggested test
A simple regression test would be to initialize a monotonic field near a reflective boundary with ih >= 3,
call update, and verify that the ghost cells are reflected by layer rather than copied from the first interior

 136

cell.
For example, at the left boundary with ibc_left = 5 and iuv = 1:

interior:
a(1) = 10
a(2) = 7
a(3) = 4

expected ghost values:
a(0) = -10
a(-1) = -7
a(-2) = -4

For a scalar or tangential component under the same boundary:

expected ghost values:
a(0) = 10
a(-1) = 7
a(-2) = 4

The current code would instead produce:

a(0) = +/-10
a(-1) = +/-10
a(-2) = +/-10

which demonstrates the bug.

Git evidence: 23370e2 (2026-06-18, multi-halo mirror reflection); 0792741 (2026-06-15, mirrored-
boundary corner rewrite).
The mirror-boundary implementation was changed from constant edge extrapolation to reflection over
the halo depth, including the corner cases introduced by multiple halo cells.

Overview

This list documents a broad precision-portability cleanup across the solver, physics modules, and
supporting utilities. The main issues were mixed use of configured-precision variables with default-real
literals, hard-coded floating-point kinds, duplicated single-versus-double precision branches, and a
handful of interface or MPI-related mismatches. The fixes standardize the implementation on real(prec),
_prec literals, and real(...,kind=prec) conversions so the same source behaves consistently in both
single- and double-precision builds.

BUG-2026-06-024: No proper build-time switch for precision mode

Summary
The source expected DBL_PREC-gated behavior, but the build system did not expose a clean CMake
option to explicitly enable or disable double precision.

• CMakeLists.txt

Without an explicit build-time switch, the selected floating-point mode is implicit and harder to
audit. That makes single- and double-precision builds less reproducible and increases the chance that
developers compile with the wrong precision configuration.

Impact
This can leave precision selection inconsistent across builds and make precision-sensitive debugging
harder.

Add a dedicated CMake option for DBL_PREC, define the compile macro when enabled, and emit a clear
status message indicating whether the build is using single or double precision.

precision datatype); a849341 (2026-06-24, precision and boundary follow-up fixes); 80d0a79 (2026-06-24,

BUG-2026-06-025: Mixed-kind numeric literals caused precision loss
and SP/DP inconsistencies

Summary
Many routines mixed real(prec) variables with default real literals such as 0., 1.!, 0.5, 1.e-6!, and 2./3..
This introduced implicit kind conversion into arithmetic that was intended to follow the configured
precision kind.

• Emissions/deposit_ems.F90
• Emissions/input_ems.F90
• MOA.F90
• advectionScheme.F90
• variables.F90
• many similar files in emissions, vegetation, radiation, and turbulence code

Default real literals are not guaranteed to match the configured prec kind. When they are combined
with real(prec) variables, compilers may insert implicit conversions or evaluate parts of the expression
at a different precision than intended.

Impact
These mixed-kind expressions can reduce numerical consistency, trigger compiler diagnostics, and
produce different behavior between single- and double-precision builds.

Convert default real literals to kind-safe forms such as 0.0_prec, 1.0_prec, 0.5_prec, and 2.0_prec/3.0_prec
throughout the affected formulas.

Git evidence: 5a8fd2e (2026-06-19, precision mismatch fixes); 6e086cf (2026-06-22, unified MPI
precision datatype); a849341 (2026-06-24, precision and boundary follow-up fixes); 80d0a79 (2026-06-24,

BUG-2026-06-026: Missing prec imports caused compile failures after
prec-suffix conversion

Summary
Several routines began using _prec-suffixed literals or real(...,kind=prec) conversions without importing
the prec kind parameter.

• Radiation/definearray_rad.F90
• Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
• domainUpdates.F90
• force.F90
• rinit.F90
• several additional files using _prec literals

If prec is not in scope, then literals such as 1.0_prec and conversions such as real(i,kind=prec) fail to
compile because the kind parameter is undefined.

Impact
This causes direct compile failures and blocks otherwise-correct precision-safe fixes.

literals, or conversions.

BUG-2026-06-030: MPI precision handling was fragile and sometimes
precision-truncating

Summary
MPI reductions and gathers were already split by precision mode where needed, but some local
scalars, temporary buffers, and diagnostics still used non-kind-safe reals or downcast results after
communication.

• rmaxmin.F90
• Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
• Radiation/rinit_rad.F90

Even when the MPI datatype is correct, storing communicated values in default-real temporaries or
printing a downcast copy can reintroduce precision loss.

Impact
This can truncate results, make diagnostics disagree with reduced values, and weaken cross-precision
reproducibility.

Retain precision-appropriate MPI datatypes, but standardize local storage and diagnostic intermediates
on real(prec) and precision-safe literals.

Git evidence: 5a8fd2e (2026-06-19, precision mismatch fixes); 6e086cf (2026-06-22, unified MPI

BUG-2026-06-031: Integer-to-real conversion logic in initialization
was not kind-safe

Summary
Several initialization and interpolation paths used separate dble(... ) versus real(... ) branches
depending on whether double precision was enabled.

• rinit.F90
• tinit.F90
• xeVariation/xevariation.F90

Branching between dble and default real duplicates conversion logic and still does not express the
intended target kind directly.

Impact
The conversion behavior can diverge across precision modes and is harder to maintain than a single
configured-kind conversion.

Replace split conversions with real(value,kind=prec).

BUG-2026-06-032: Numerically sensitive physics constants were not
precision-safe

Summary
Many empirical or physical constants in combustion, radiation, evaporation, solar, and thermodynamics
code were written as default reals instead of _prec-suffixed constants.

• Emissions/zBEST_ems.F90
• Vegetation/burn_veg.F90
• thermodynamics.F90
• Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
• additional radiation, vegetation, and variables modules

Physical constants are often used in numerically sensitive paths. If they are declared as default real,
the expression tree can inherit an unintended kind.

Impact
This can alter sensitive calculations, reduce consistency between precision modes, and make results
depend on implicit compiler conversions.

Convert such constants to precision-safe declarations using _prec consistently.

precision datatype); a849341 (2026-06-24, precision and boundary follow-up fixes); 80d0a79 (2026-06-24,

SP/DP branches

Summary
The central constants module defined key values such as pi, g, Rgas, pref, and other scientific constants
using duplicated single- and double-precision branches.

• variables.F90

Impact

Overview

This list documents a radiation-physics consistency bug in which the Stefan–Boltzmann constant was
both inaccurate in the shared constants module and duplicated with a different hardcoded value in the
Monte Carlo radiation module.

 184

BUG-2026-06-039: Incorrect and inconsistent Stefan–Boltzmann
constant values

Summary
The Stefan–Boltzmann constant was defined with an incorrect value in variables.F90 and was also
hardcoded with a different value in Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90. This created both a numerical
accuracy issue and an inconsistency between radiation modules.

• CODE-dev/variables.F90
• CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90

The codebase used two different values for the Stefan–Boltzmann constant:

! variables.F90
sigma = 5.678e-8_prec

! Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
5.67051e-8_prec

The value in variables.F90 was less accurate than the CODATA 2018 recommended value:

sigma = 5.670374419e-8_prec

Additionally, the Monte Carlo radiation module hardcoded its own value in multiple source-term
calculations instead of using the shared sigma constant from the constants module. This made
the radiation behavior inconsistent across modules and increased the risk of future divergence if the
constant were updated in only one location.

Impact
This bug affected radiation source calculations that depend on the Stefan–Boltzmann constant. The
numerical difference is small but systematic, and it could lead to inconsistent radiative heat transfer
results between simple radiation and Monte Carlo radiation paths.
The issue also reduced maintainability because the same physical constant was defined in one module
but duplicated as hardcoded literals elsewhere.

Changes made
Updated sigma in variables.F90
The Stefan–Boltzmann constant in the constants module was updated from:

real(prec) :: sigma = 5.678e-8_prec ! Stefan-Boltzmann constant (W/(m^2K^4))

to:

 185

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log June 2026

real(prec) :: sigma = 5.670374419e-8_prec ! Stefan-Boltzmann constant (W/(m^2K^4))

This updates the shared constant to the CODATA 2018 recommended value.

Imported sigma into Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
The main Monte Carlo radiation subroutine import was changed from:

use constants, only : pref

to:

use constants, only : pref,sigma

The nested source_defs() subroutine was also updated to import sigma:

use constants, only : sigma

Removed hardcoded Stefan–Boltzmann values from Monte Carlo radiation source terms
The hardcoded value

5.67051e-8_prec

was replaced with the shared sigma constant in all affected source calculations.
Examples:

sourcesol(ift,i,j,k)=4.0_prec*papvift(ift,i,j,k) &
  *(t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*sigma

sourcesol(ift,i,j,k+nfuel)=4.0_prec*papvift(ift,i,j,k+nfuel) &
  *(t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*sigma

sourcegas(i,j,k)=4.0_prec*papvgas(i,j,k+nfuel)* &
  (t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*sigma

Files changed
CODE-dev/variables.F90
Updated the shared Stefan–Boltzmann constant:

- real(prec) :: sigma = 5.678e-8_prec ! Stefan-Boltzmann constant (W/(m^2K^4))
+     real(prec) :: sigma = 5.670374419e-8_prec ! Stefan-Boltzmann constant (W/(m^2K^4))

CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
Imported sigma from the constants module:

 186

- use constants, only : pref
+ use constants, only : pref,sigma

Added sigma import to source_defs():

+ use constants, only : sigma

Replaced hardcoded Stefan–Boltzmann constant values:

-               *(t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*5.67051e-8_prec
+ *(t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*sigma

-                 *(t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*5.67051e-8_prec
+ *(t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*sigma

-             (t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*5.67051e-8_prec
+ (t4bar-tambient**2)*(t4bar+tambient**2)*sigma

Result
The code now uses a single shared Stefan–Boltzmann constant throughout the affected radiation
calculations. This improves numerical consistency, accuracy, and maintainability by avoiding duplicated
hardcoded physical constants.

Git evidence: 14164a2 (2026-06-22, Stefan-Boltzmann constant fix).
The Stefan-Boltzmann constant was made consistent in the shared variables/radiation code instead of
carrying mismatched values across modules.

BUG-2026-06-040: MPDATA y-face halo update appears to use
botedge instead of topedge when updating f2o

Summary
In advectionScheme.F90, near the end of mpdata(), the MPDATA/FCT path updates the y-face
flux-correction array f2o with an update() call whose y-extent is selected using botedge:

if(botedge.eq.0) then
  call update(f2o(:,:,:,kv), &
    np,mp,l,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
else
  call update(f2o(:,:,:,kv), &
    np,mp+1,l,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
endif

This appears inconsistent with the array geometry and with nearby MPDATA code. f2o is a y-face
array with an extra face on the high-y side, so the decision to include mp+1 should depend on topedge,
not botedge. The analogous x-face update uses rightedge to decide whether f1o should be updated
through np or np+1. The analogous y-face update should therefore use topedge to decide whether f2o
should be updated through mp or mp+1.

• CODE-dev/advectionScheme.F90
• CODE-dev/update.F90
• CODE-dev/msga.F90
• CODE-dev/variables.F90
• CODE-dev/force.F90

The suspect code is:

if(rightedge.eq.0) then
  call update(f1o(:,:,:,kv), &
    np,mp,l,1-ih,np+ih+1,1-ih,mp+ih,2,0,1)
else
  call update(f1o(:,:,:,kv), &
    np+1,mp,l,1-ih,np+ih+1,1-ih,mp+ih,2,0,1)
endif

if(botedge.eq.0) then
  call update(f2o(:,:,:,kv), &
    np,mp,l,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
else
  call update(f2o(:,:,:,kv), &
    np,mp+1,l,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
endif

The first block is structurally correct for f1o: f1o is an x-face array, so including the high-side x
face np+1 depends on whether this rank is on the right/high-x boundary. The second block appears

 189

inconsistent: f2o is a y-face array, so including the high-side y face mp+1 should depend on whether
this rank is on the top/high-y boundary.
Evidence from array allocation supports this interpretation:

allocate (v1mp(il:iu+1,jl:ju ,lls ,nvp)); v1mp=0.0_prec
allocate (v2mp(il:iu ,jl:ju+1,lls ,nvp)); v2mp=0.0_prec
allocate (v3mp(il:iu ,jl:ju ,lls+1,nvp)); v3mp=0.0_prec
allocate (f1(il:iu+1,jl:ju ,lls ,nvp) ); f1= 0.0_prec
allocate (f2(il:iu ,jl:ju+1,lls ,nvp) ); f2= 0.0_prec
allocate (f3(il:iu ,jl:ju ,lls+1,nvp) ); f3= 0.0_prec
allocate (f1o(il:iu+1,jl:ju ,lls ,nvp) ); f1o= 0.0_prec
allocate (f2o(il:iu ,jl:ju+1,lls ,nvp) ); f2o= 0.0_prec
allocate (f3o(il:iu ,jl:ju ,lls+1,nvp) ); f3o= 0.0_prec

That means f1o has the extra face in the x direction, il:iu+1, while f2o has the extra face in the y
direction, jl:ju+1. Therefore the special +1 extent for f1o is associated with the high-x/right side,
while the special +1 extent for f2o is associated with the high-y/top side.
Earlier in the same mpdata() routine, the code already uses topedge when deciding whether y-face
arrays should be updated through mp or mp+1. For v2mp:

if (topedge.eq.0) then
  call update(v2mp(:,:,:,kv),np,mp,l, &
              1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
else
  call update(v2mp(:,:,:,kv),np,mp+1, &
              l,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
endif

For f2:

if (topedge.eq.0) then
  call update(f2(:,:,:,kv),np,mp,l, &
              1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
else
  call update(f2(:,:,:,kv),np,mp+1,l, &
              1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
endif

These are direct precedents for how y-face arrays with jl:ju+1 should be handled. The later f2o block
differs from this pattern by using botedge.
msga.F90 also confirms the meanings of the edge flags:

! set up edge information (0=>not an edge, 1=>edge)
if((ibc_right.gt.0).and.(mod((mpi_rank+1),nprocx)==0)) rightedge=1
if((ibc_left.gt.0).and.(mod((mpi_rank+1),nprocx)==1.or.nprocx==1)) &
  leftedge=1
if ((ibc_bot.gt.0).and.((mpi_rank+1).le.nprocx)) botedge=1
if ((ibc_top.gt.0).and.(((numprocs)-(mpi_rank+1))<nprocx)) topedge=1

This confirms that botedge marks ranks on the low-y/bottom domain boundary, while topedge marks
ranks on the high-y/top domain boundary. There is no indication that botedge has a special meaning
related to the high-side y face.

 190

Impact
For flat terrain, equal grid spacing, symmetric lateral boundary conditions, and no directional forcing,
the horizontal parts of the numerical scheme should be structurally invariant under the coordinate
exchange

x <-> y
u <-> v
np <-> mp
dx <-> dy
left/right boundaries <-> bottom/top boundaries

The current code breaks this structural symmetry in the f2o update path:
• x-face f1o uses the high-side x boundary flag, rightedge, to decide whether to include np+1;
• y-face f2o should analogously use the high-side y boundary flag, topedge, to decide whether to
  include mp+1;
• instead, it uses the low-side y boundary flag, botedge.
This likely affects MPDATA/FCT runs where this later correction path is active, especially runs with
nfct > 1 and a y-direction MPI decomposition where botedge and topedge are not identical. It may
be masked or less visible when nfct = 1, when there is no y-direction MPI decomposition, or when a
single y rank is both bottom and top edge.

Express the fix as a minimal diff:

@@
- if(botedge.eq.0) then
+ if(topedge.eq.0) then
                 call update(f2o(:,:,:,kv), &
                    np,mp,l,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih+1,3,0,2)
 else

The fix is small and localized, but existing nfct > 1 results may change near y boundaries. That
result change would be expected if the current code is incorrectly updating the wrong y-face extent. A
targeted regression test should compare rotated x- and y-oriented cases and verify that mp+1 is selected
exactly when topedge = 1, not when botedge = 1.

Git evidence: ee83e79 (2026-06-09, zeta bug-list pass); 0325b25 (2026-07-14, MPDATA cleanup);
a849341 (2026-06-24, precision and boundary follow-up fixes).
The MPDATA y-face update calls were folded into the new staggered-boundary update interface
and later MPDATA cleanup. The current code uses side-specific update flags rather than the earlier
hand-written edge test pattern.

BUG-2026-06-041: MPI broadcast type mismatch in source_defs

Summary
The source_defs routine currently computes a global radiation energy total, Etot, using mpi_reduce
followed by mpi_Bcast. The code chooses the MPI datatype with #ifdef DBL_PREC, using either
mpi_double_precision or mpi_real depending on the configured precision.
The existing comment says:

! Workaround for a weird type mismatch bug in gfortran

That comment is misleading. The underlying issue is not specifically a gfortran broadcast bug. The
real issue is that the MPI datatype must match the Fortran kind of real(prec). If prec and DBL_PREC
ever get out of sync, the code can compile successfully but pass the wrong datatype to MPI at runtime.

• monteCarlo_rad.F90

The current pattern is effectively:

#ifdef DBL_PREC
  call mpi_reduce(Etotlocal,Etot,1,mpi_double_precision,mpi_sum,0, &

#else
  call mpi_reduce(Etotlocal,Etot,1,mpi_real,0,mpi_comm_world, &
 ierror)
#endif

! Workaround for a weird type mismatch bug in gfortran
#ifdef DBL_PREC
  call mpi_Bcast(Etot,1,mpi_double_precision,0,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
  papvthresh=2.0_prec*min_rhoFuel/(maxval(sizeScale)*rhoMicro)
#else
  call mpi_Bcast(Etot,1,mpi_real,0,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
  papvthresh=2.0_prec*min_rhoFuel/(maxval(sizeScale)*rhoMicro)
#endif

Etotlocal and Etot are treated as real(prec), but MPI does not understand real(prec) directly.
It only sees a memory buffer and an MPI datatype, such as mpi_real or mpi_double_precision.
Therefore this mapping must always be correct:

real(prec) <--> matching MPI datatype
real(4) / single precision <--> mpi_real
real(8) / double precision <--> mpi_double_precision

If Etot is an 8-byte real but the code passes mpi_real, MPI will reduce or broadcast it as if it were a
4-byte real. That can corrupt the value, produce incorrect totals, or cause compiler/MPI-dependent
behavior.

 194

The broadcast exists because mpi_reduce only makes the reduced value valid on the root rank, rank 0,
while Etot is later used on all ranks in logic such as if(Etot.LT.Emin)then and in photon allocation
calculations involving EAZ(i,j,k)/Etot.

Impact
This communication pattern is valid but more verbose than necessary. It duplicates precision-specific
code, carries a misleading compiler-specific workaround comment, and increases the risk of MPI
datatype mismatches at runtime if precision selection and datatype selection ever diverge.

Replace the mpi_reduce plus mpi_Bcast pair with a single mpi_allreduce. This removes duplicated
communication, removes the misleading comment, and makes the intent clearer. The assignment to
papvthresh should also be moved outside the precision-dependent branch because it is identical in
both branches.
A representative diff is:

diff --git a/monteCarlo_rad.F90 b/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@
- call mpi_reduce(Etotlocal,Etot,1,mpi_double_precision,mpi_sum,0, &
+ call mpi_allreduce(Etotlocal,Etot,1,mpi_double_precision,mpi_sum, &

@@
- call mpi_reduce(Etotlocal,Etot,1,mpi_real,0,mpi_comm_world, &
+ call mpi_allreduce(Etotlocal,Etot,1,mpi_real,mpi_sum,mpi_comm_world, &
 ierror)
@@
- ! Workaround for a weird type mismatch bug in gfortran
-#ifdef DBL_PREC
- call mpi_Bcast(Etot,1,mpi_double_precision,0,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
- papvthresh=2.0_prec*min_rhoFuel/(maxval(sizeScale)*rhoMicro)
-#else
- call mpi_Bcast(Etot,1,mpi_real,0,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
- papvthresh=2.0_prec*min_rhoFuel/(maxval(sizeScale)*rhoMicro)
-#endif
+ papvthresh=2.0_prec*min_rhoFuel/(maxval(sizeScale)*rhoMicro)

Longer term, the project should define one project-wide MPI datatype alias for real(prec), for
example mpi_prec, so MPI communication does not have to repeat #ifdef DBL_PREC at each call site.

Git evidence: 6e086cf (2026-06-22, unified MPI precision datatype); a849341 (2026-06-24, precision
and boundary follow-up fixes).
The radiation source broadcast path now uses the shared MPI datatype tied to real(wp), avoiding the
old single/double precision mismatch.

BUG-2026-06-042: Non-portable precision definition in
gridlist_variables.f90

Summary
The prec parameter in gridlist_variables.f90 uses hardcoded kind values, 4 and 8, which are
compiler-dependent and non-portable. These should be replaced with selected_real_kind() for
Fortran 90+ compatibility.

• gridlist_variables.f90

The current module definition is:

#ifdef DBL_PREC
  integer,parameter :: prec = 8
#else
  integer,parameter :: prec = 4
#endif

Kind numbers such as 4 and 8 are not standardized in Fortran and may vary by compiler. As a result:
• some compilers may use different kind values for single and double precision;
• there is no guarantee that kind 4 represents a 32-bit real or that kind 8 represents a 64-bit real on
  all systems;
• the implementation violates Fortran portability best practices.
The impact is that the code may fail to compile on certain compilers, may select incorrect precision if
a compiler uses different numbering, and loses portability across HPC systems and compiler families,
including GNU, Intel, and Cray.

Impact
This issue directly affects portability and numerical configuration. The current implementation may
work on the compilers already tested, but it is not guaranteed to remain correct across all supported
systems or future compiler environments.

Use selected_real_kind() in diff form:

diff --git a/gridlist_variables.f90 b/gridlist_variables.f90
@@
 #ifdef DBL_PREC
- integer,parameter :: prec = 8
+ ! Double precision: ~15 decimal digits, exponent range ~10^307
+ integer,parameter :: prec = selected_real_kind(15, 307)
 #else
- integer,parameter :: prec = 4

 198

+ ! Single precision: ~6 decimal digits, exponent range ~10^37
+ integer,parameter :: prec = selected_real_kind(6, 37)
 #endif

After applying the fix, verify the selected precision with diagnostics such as:

if (mpi_rank == 0) then
  print*, ’Precision␣kind␣value:’, prec
  print*, ’Storage␣size␣(bits):’, storage_size(1.0_prec)
  print*, ’Decimal␣precision:’, precision(1.0_prec)
  print*, ’Exponent␣range:’, range(1.0_prec)
endif

 Expected results are approximately 32 bits / 6 digits / exponent range 37 for single precision and
 64 bits / 15 digits / exponent range 307 for double precision. Testing should include builds with
-DDBL_PREC=ON and -DDBL_PREC=OFF, ideally on GNU, Intel, and Cray compilers, with regression
 checks and restart compatibility review.

Git evidence: 5a8fd2e (2026-06-19, precision mismatch fixes); a849341 (2026-06-24, precision and
boundary follow-up fixes); 80d0a79 (2026-06-24, missed precision setting).
Precision definitions in gridlist and related modules were moved to the common precision scheme, with
a follow-up for a missed prec=4 location.

BUG-2026-06-043: Firebrand exact top-boundary handling writes the
x coordinate instead of y

Summary
The exact top-boundary equality case in Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90 checks iy, but modifies ix. A
firebrand exactly on the top domain boundary therefore has its x coordinate overwritten with a y
coordinate, while the y coordinate remains unchanged.

• Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90

The relevant code is:

else if(xvbrand(it,ix).ge.(n*dx))then ! Outside x domain on right
  if(xvbrand(it,ix).eq.(n*dx)) xvbrand(it,ix)=xvbrand(it,ix)-tolerance
...
else if(xvbrand(it,iy).ge.m*dy)then ! Outside y domain on top
  if(xvbrand(it,iy).eq.(m*dy)) xvbrand(it,ix)=xvbrand(it,iy)-tolerance
  if(ibc_top.eq.0)then
 xvbrand(it,iy)=xvbrand(it,iy)-m*dy

The top-boundary equality case checks iy, but modifies ix. A firebrand exactly on the top domain
boundary has its x coordinate overwritten with a y coordinate. The y coordinate remains exactly
m*dy, so mirror handling and later processor assignment can still see it as outside. In updateFB, the
destination rank is derived from floor(xvbrand(it,iy)/dy/mp), so exact iy = m*dy can map one
row past the valid processor range.

Impact
This can corrupt firebrand coordinates, leave a top-boundary brand still outside in y, and send it to an
invalid or unintended processor row during later processor assignment and boundary handling.

Correct the typo in diff form:

diff --git a/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90 b/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
@@
- if(xvbrand(it,iy).eq.(m*dy)) xvbrand(it,ix)=xvbrand(it,iy)-tolerance
+ if(xvbrand(it,iy).eq.(m*dy)) xvbrand(it,iy)=xvbrand(it,iy)-tolerance

A more robust follow-up would use a tolerance comparison instead of exact floating-point equality, but
the minimal fix is the index correction.

Git evidence: 0497645 (2026-06-15, split firebrand boundary checks); c8296c6 (2026-06-15, firebrand
edge tolerance); 869ead7 (2026-06-25, boundary-error pass).

 202

Firebrand boundary handling was split by side, edge tolerances were added for exact-edge landings,
and the later boundary pass removed the erroneous coordinate reuse in removal/landing logic.

BUG-2026-06-044: Radiation bottom-face intersection uses the
top-face coefficient

Summary
In Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90, the code computes the bottom-face quadratic coefficients, but
then decides whether the bottom-face equation is linear by checking acoeftop instead of acoefbot.

• Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90

The evidence is:

! Downward photon
acoefbot=(z1bot+z4bot-z2bot-z3bot)*dir(1)*dir(2)/(dx*dy)
bcoefbot=(-dir(3)+dir(2)/dy*(z3bot-z1bot)+dir(1)/dx* &
  (z2bot-z1bot)+(z1bot+z4bot-z2bot-z3bot)*(dir(2)/dy* &
  (xf/dx-(i1-1))+dir(1)/dx*(yf/dy-(j1-1))))
ccoefbot=(z1bot-zf+(z3bot-z1bot)*(yf/dy-(j1-1))+ &
  (z2bot-z1bot)*(xf/dx-(i1-1))+(z1bot+z4bot-z2bot-z3bot)* &
  (xf/dx-(i1-1))*(yf/dy-(j1-1)))

if(kt.le.0)then
  if(abs(acoeftop).lt.tolerance)then !a.eq.0
 if(ccoefbot*bcoefbot.lt.0.0_prec) tz=-ccoefbot/bcoefbot

On terrain-following or deformed cells, top and bottom faces can have different bilinear coefficients. If
the top face is effectively linear and the bottom face is not, the code incorrectly uses the linear formula
for the bottom face. If the top face is not linear and the bottom face is, the quadratic branch can
divide by a near-zero acoefbot.

Impact
This can produce incorrect bottom-face intersection behavior in the downward-photon branch of the
Monte Carlo radiation solver, especially on terrain/deformed cells where top and bottom geometry
differs.

Use acoefbot in diff form:

diff --git a/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90 b/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@
- if(abs(acoeftop).lt.tolerance)then !a.eq.0
+ if(abs(acoefbot).lt.tolerance)then !a.eq.0
 if(ccoefbot*bcoefbot.lt.0.0_prec) tz=-ccoefbot/bcoefbot

Git evidence: 5e20226 (2026-06-15, radiation acoefbot typo fix); 869ead7 (2026-06-25, boundary-error
pass).
The bottom radiation intersection branch now uses acoefbot rather than the top-face coefficient.

BUG-2026-06-046: radiationSink receives a fuel-depth gas-force slice
but loops over the full atmosphere depth

Summary
CODE-dev/force.F90 calls the simple radiation sink with a gas force slice whose third dimension is
restricted to 1:lfuel:

call radiationSink(forceSE_xv(:,:,1:lfuel,itheta), &
  forceSE_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies),xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
  xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhow),tempg,temps, &
  1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,1,np,1,mp,l,lfuel,nfuel)

However, the same call passes lls=l, and radiationSink declares and loops over the gas force
argument as if its third dimension has length lls:

real(prec),intent(inout) :: force(ilh:iuh,jlh:juh,lls)
...
do k=1,lls
  ...
  force(i,j,k)=force(i,j,k)+...
enddo

If lfuel < l, the actual argument has a third-dimension section of length lfuel, while the dummy
argument is declared with length l. That is a likely argument-shape mismatch and can lead to
out-of-bounds access or non-portable behavior.

• CODE-dev/force.F90
• CODE-dev/Radiation/sink_rad.F90

The current call site in CODE-dev/force.F90 is:

elseif(irad.eq.3)then ! Radiation Sink
  call radiationSink(forceSE_xv(:,:,1:lfuel,itheta), &
    forceSE_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies),xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
    xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhow),tempg,temps, &
    1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,1,np,1,mp,l,lfuel,nfuel)
endif

The relevant dummy argument and loop in CODE-dev/Radiation/sink_rad.F90 are:

real(prec),intent(inout) :: force(ilh:iuh,jlh:juh,lls)
...
do k=1,lls
  do j=jl,ju
 do i=il,iu
 ...
 force(i,j,k)=force(i,j,k)+firad_gas/cp_gas(i,j,k)* &
        (pref/pr(i,j,k))**(1.0_prec-cv_gas(i,j,k)/cp_gas(i,j,k))

 211

 enddo
  enddo
enddo

The call passes inconsistent information about the vertical extent of the gas force array:

actual gas force section: forceSE_xv(:,:,1:lfuel,itheta)
dummy gas force shape: force(ilh:iuh,jlh:juh,lls)
passed lls value: l

The code therefore tells radiationSink that force has l vertical levels even though the actual
section has only lfuel levels. This is especially suspicious because the other gas arrays passed to
radiationSink, such as tempg, pre, pr, cp_gas, cv_gas, and xe, are full gas-domain fields indexed
over k=1,lls. The gas-radiation loop is written to operate over the full lls gas column, while the
actual force argument is sliced to fuel depth only.

Impact
This mismatch is a code correctness issue independent of the radiation physics. Depending on compiler,
optimization level, bounds checking, and memory layout, it may fail with bounds or shape checking
enabled, silently write beyond the dummy argument’s actual section, rely on non-portable contiguous-
memory behavior, or accidentally update the intended full forceSE_xv field only because the underlying
storage happens to be laid out favorably.

If the simple gas radiation sink is intended to apply over the same full gas depth as the Monte Carlo
radiation call, pass the full gas potential-temperature force field:

@@
- call radiationSink(forceSE_xv(:,:,1:lfuel,itheta), &
+ call radiationSink(forceSE_xv(:,:,:,itheta), &
       forceSE_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies),xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
       xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhow),tempg,temps, &
       1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,1,np,1,mp,l,lfuel,nfuel)

If it is intentionally supposed to apply only to the fuel-depth gas levels, then the lls argument should

BUG-2026-06-047: Halo exchange MPI tags can exceed MPI_TAG_UB
after only a few timesteps

Summary
The update routine builds every MPI tag from the global timestep. MPI does not allow arbitrary
integer tags; every communicator has a finite MPI_TAG_UB, and portable MPI code can only rely on a
minimum upper bound of 32767.

• update.F90

The code uses:

95 itag=(timestep*10000)+1000
145 itag=(timestep*10000)+1100
197 itag=(timestep*10000)+1200
247 itag=(timestep*10000)+1300
300 itag=(timestep*10000)+1400
395 itag=(timestep*10000)+1500
490 itag=(timestep*10000)+1600
585 itag=(timestep*10000)+1700

Each tag is then used in MPI_Sendrecv calls for side and corner halo exchanges. On an implementation
that only guarantees the portable lower bound, the routine starts producing invalid tags at timestep
= 4:

timestep = 3 -> max update tag = 31700
timestep = 4 -> min update tag = 41000

That can make normal halo exchange fail with MPI_ERR_TAG or abort on MPI implementations with
a smaller tag range. On implementations with larger tag ranges, the same pattern can still fail in
long runs or restarted runs when default integer arithmetic overflows. With 32-bit default integers,
timestep * 10000 + 1700 overflows at about timestep = 214749.
The timestep component is not needed for correctness here. The routine uses blocking MPI_Sendrecv,
and the eight exchange phases already have distinct fixed offsets, 1000 through 1700. Reusing the
same small phase tags on later calls is safe once the previous blocking exchange has completed.

Impact
This can cause ordinary halo exchanges to fail after only a few timesteps on some MPI implementations,
and can produce restart- or run-length-dependent failures on others.

Use fixed, small phase tags for the eight exchange directions, or query MPI_TAG_UB and explicitly
validate any encoded tag scheme. The simplest fix is to remove timestep from the tag calculation and
remove the now-unused use gridsetup, only : timestep. In diff form:

 214

diff --git a/update.F90 b/update.F90
@@
- use gridsetup, only : timestep

@@
-    itag=(timestep*10000)+1000
+    itag=1000
@@
-    itag=(timestep*10000)+1100
+    itag=1100
@@
-    itag=(timestep*10000)+1200
+    itag=1200
@@
-    itag=(timestep*10000)+1300
+    itag=1300
@@
-    itag=(timestep*10000)+1400
+    itag=1400
@@
-    itag=(timestep*10000)+1500
+    itag=1500
@@
-    itag=(timestep*10000)+1600
+    itag=1600
@@
-    itag=(timestep*10000)+1700
+    itag=1700

Longer-term cleanup would define named tag parameters, for example tag_y_top = 1000 and
tag_y_bot = 1100, to make the communication phases easier to audit and to prevent future
reintroduction of unbounded runtime-derived tags.

Summary

BUG-2026-07-001: Firebrand Output Is Called With Time Instead
Of The Timestep

Source report: compressF90/COMPRESS-001.md

Files
• compress.F90
• Firebrands/io_fb.F90
• Firebrands/variables_fb.F90
• rinit.F90
• force.F90

! compress.F90
78 if(mod(it,frqoutput).eq.0)then
79 call binary_writeio(ittot)
80 if(ifbrand.ge.1) call writeio_fb(time)
81 endif

! Firebrands/io_fb.F90
4 subroutine writeio_fb(ittot)
...
14 integer,intent(in) :: ittot
...
43 call namefile(ittot,outname_fb,fname)

! rinit.F90 / force.F90
93 if(ifbrand.eq.1) call rinitFirebrands(irst)
...
154 if(ifbrand.eq.1) call firebrand(...)

Problem
writeio_fb expects an integer timestep and uses it to build the firebrand output filename. compress.F90
passes time, a real-valued simulation time. Because writeio_fb is an external subroutine with no explicit
interface at the call site, this mismatch can compile but the callee reads the real argument’s bytes as
an integer. The resulting firebrand filenames can be garbage or inconsistent with restart expectations.
The guard is also inconsistent: initialization and evolution only support ifbrand.eq.1, but output uses
ifbrand.ge.1. If a nonzero unsupported value is ever supplied, compress.F90 can call writeio_fb without
the firebrand arrays being initialized.

Pass ittot, not time, and use the same ifbrand.eq.1 guard used by initialization and physics.

BUG-2026-07-002: Restart At Or Beyond nt Runs One Extra Step

Source report: compressF90/COMPRESS-002 (decided no).md

Files
• compress.F90
• rinit.F90
• io.F90
• variables.F90

! compress.F90
31 call rinit

35 ittot=it+itrestart

! io.F90

! rinit.F90

...
79 time=itrestart*dts*nts

! variables.F90
247 integer :: itrestart=0 ! Iteration of restart
248 integer :: ittot=0

Problem
On restart, irstreadio updates itrestart, and rinit updates time, but ittot remains at its module
default of 0 until the first iteration of the loop. The loop condition therefore uses stale state:

do while(ittot.lt.nt)

If the restart file is already at the requested final timestep, for example restartfile = comp.out.10000 and
nt = 10000, the condition is still true because ittot is 0. The driver enters the loop, sets ittot = 10001,
and advances one unwanted extra timestep past nt.

After rinit, synchronize ittot with itrestart before testing the loop condition.

BUG-2026-07-004: NaN Guard Checks Only One Local Cell And
Can Strand MPI Ranks

Source report: compressF90/COMPRESS-004 (decided no).md

Files
• compress.F90
• rmaxmin.F90
• variables.F90

! compress.F90
41 call explicit_domain_updates ! Updates environmental variables (pressure, etc.)
42    do kv=1,nv-1
43      call rmaxmin_3D(xvrho(:,:,1:l,kv),xv_list(kv), &
44        1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,1,l)
45 enddo
46    call rmaxmin_3D(xv(:,:,1:l,nv),xv_list(nv), &
47      1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,1,l)
...
55    if(isnan(xvrho(1,1,1,1)).or.abs(xvrho(1,1,1,1)).gt.1e15) then
56 print*,’NaNs␣or␣Infinity␣in␣XV␣array’
57 call mpi_finalize(ierror)
58 STOP
59 endif

! rmaxmin.F90
52 rmax=maxval(array(:,:,:))
53 rmin=minval(array(:,:,:))
54 call mpi_reduce(rmax,xmax,1,mpi_wp,mpi_max,0, &
55 mpi_comm_world,ierror)
56 call mpi_reduce(rmin,xmin,1,mpi_wp,mpi_min,0, &
57 mpi_comm_world,ierror)

Problem
The driver prints min/max values for many fields, but the actual stop condition checks only xvrho
,→ (1,1,1,1) on each MPI rank. A NaN, Inf, or runaway value in any other cell, variable, halo, or fuel
field can continue into the next physics step.
The stop is also not collective. If one rank’s local (1,1,1,1) is bad and another rank’s is not, the bad
rank calls mpi_finalize and stops while the other ranks continue toward later collectives. That can lead
to a hang or an MPI abort rather than a clean diagnostic.
Finally, isnan is compiler-specific in this form. The codebase targets GNU, Intel, and Cray compilers,
so the standard ieee_arithmetic intrinsic is safer.

 230

Check the full local interior state with ieee_is_nan, reduce a bad-state flag across MPI ranks, and
finalize collectively when any rank reports a problem.

+ use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only : ieee_is_nan

- isensor,ifbrand,outname
+ isensor,ifbrand,outname,wp

- use msga_variables, only : mpi_rank,ierror
+ use msga_variables, only : mpi_rank,ierror,mpi_comm_world,mpi_integer, &
+ mpi_max
@@
- integer :: kv,it,ift
+ integer :: kv,it,ift

Problem
compress.F90 creates only the directory implied by the main outname. Sensor and firebrand outputs use
independent filename prefixes (sensorfile and outname_fb) that can include their own directories, but
those directories are not created before the files are opened.
This is especially visible for sensors because rinit calls rinitSense, and rinitSense opens the sensor
CSV files during initialization. A gridlist such as sensorfile = ’./sensors/sensor’ can fail immediately
unless ./sensors already exists, even though the driver already has a helper designed to create output
directories.

Create directories for each enabled output stream before rinit opens or writes those files. xvdataname is
already handled inside input_xevariation, so the missing pieces here are sensors and firebrands.

 237

Problem
xvpointers adds aerosol moment slots to xv when nAero > 0, but it never updates the global aerosol
moment pointers iM0 and iM1. Those pointers keep their module defaults of 1, which is also iuvel.
When iemissions == 3, ZBEST writes soot moment source terms through iM0 and iM1. With the current
pointers, those source terms are added to the u momentum component instead of the aerosol moment
fields. The aerosol fields remain unchanged, while the wind field receives non-momentum forcing.
The code also does not fail fast if ZBEST is enabled without at least one aerosol species and at least two
aerosol moments.

Set iM0 and iM1 when the aerosol block is appended, and validate the minimum aerosol configuration
needed by ZBEST.

Problem
xvpointers leaves iEmitStart and iEmitStop at their module defaults when iemissions == 0. If fire is
disabled, input.F90 does not force emissions on and input_emissions is not called, so cpEmit and mwEmit
can remain unallocated.
Both implicit_domain_updates and explicit_domain_updates always call updateGasThermProps with cpEmit,
mwEmit, and the iEmitStart:iEmitStop slice. In a no-emission run, that means an unallocated gas-property
table can be passed to a routine expecting arrays of size nEmit, while the default emission slice points
at transported variable 1 (u) rather than an empty gas-species list.
At best this relies on compiler- and interface-dependent behavior for zero-length explicit-shape dummies.
At worst it crashes under runtime checks or corrupts thermodynamic properties for wind-only/no-fire
configurations.

Make the no-emission state explicit and avoid passing unallocated emission arrays to updateGasThermProps.
Keep domainUpdates on a real zero-length array path when nEmit == 0.

BUG-2026-07-008: Aerosol xv_list Labels Can Be Wrong Or Crash
On Long Species Names

Source report: definearrayF90/DEFINEARRAY-003 (decided no).md

! variables.F90

! Emissions/variables_ems.F90

! compress.F90

! Sensors/rinit_sense.F90

52 write(unitnum,’(A8)’,advance=’no’) xv_list(ni)

! xeVariation/windfield.F90
137    write(48) xv_list

 246

Problem
The aerosol label builder searches for the first blank in spAero(i) and then writes spAero(i)(1:indx) plus
the moment number into a 12-character xv_list element.
This has two failure modes:

• If an aerosol species uses all 12 characters, index(spAero(i),’ ’) returns 0, so the species substring is
  empty and labels collapse to just the moment number.
• If the first blank is at the end of the 12-character field, or the species plus moment number is longer
  than 12 characters, the internal write target can be too short. That can raise an internal-file write
  error before the simulation starts.

Those labels are used in min/max diagnostics, sensor headers, and windfield output, so this can either
crash initialization or produce ambiguous output names for aerosol fields.

Build the label in a temporary string that is longer than xv_list, use trim(spAero(i)) instead of searching
for a blank manually, and then assign into xv_list. The assignment may truncate to the current 12-
character label width, but it avoids internal-write overflow and does not drop full-width names to an
empty substring.

@@
 ! Local Variables
 integer :: i,j
- integer :: indx
+ integer :: idx
+ character(len=32) :: aerosolLabel
@@
 if(nAero.gt.0)then
 do i=1,nAero
 do j=1,nMAero
- indx=index(spAero(i),’ ’)
-          write(xv_list(iEmitStart+nEmit+nMAero*(i-1)+j-1),"(A,I0)") &
-            spAero(i)(1:indx),j
+ idx=iEmitStart+nEmit+nMAero*(i-1)+j-1
+ write(aerosolLabel,"(A,’_’,I0)") trim(spAero(i)),j
+ xv_list(idx)=aerosolLabel
 enddo
 enddo
 endif

Git evidence: 91c2a57 (2026-07-22, aerosol merge fixes); a15c17e (2026-07-23, longer path variables).
Aerosol labels and path/name buffers were made safer through the aerosol merge and later lengthened
path variables, reducing the risk of truncation or label mismatch for longer species names.

Problem
xvpointers only creates the kb transported variable when iturb > 1. If a run uses fire, moisture, or
radiation-related solid energy (isies.ne.1) with iturb == 0, both ika and ikb remain at their module
default of 1, which is the u momentum field. If iturb == 1, ika is created but ikb still remains 1.
The vegetation routines then compute turbulent mixing from xvrho(...,ika) and xvrho(...,ikb). In
those configurations, they use wind momentum/velocity as turbulence energy. That can silently distort
convective heat transfer and burning rates, or produce sqrt of a negative value when u is negative.

Either implement non-kb formulas for these physics paths or reject the unsupported combination early.
With the current code, fail-fast is safer because the fire/moisture/solid-energy routines are written
around the two-equation turbulence indices.

+ STOP
+ endif

 ivvel = 2

Problem
definearray calls defineTurbArray for any iturb > 0, but defineTurbArray only allocates the Linn turbulence
arrays when iturb == 2. Later, rinit calls rinitSubTurb for iturb >= 1, and rinitSubTurb unconditionally
writes saxy, saz, sa, and sb.
For iturb == 1, those arrays were never allocated, so the run can crash during initialization before it
reaches the explicit Smagorinski Not implemented stop in calcForceTurb.

Reject iturb == 1 before allocation/initialization, or fully implement and allocate the arrays required
by that mode. Since calcForceTurb already says this mode is not implemented, the smallest safe fix is
an early stop.

+ print*,’iturb=1 is not implemented’
+ STOP
+ endif

and thermodynamics bug-list pass).

diation paths that require unallocated turbulence arrays. Later subgrid commits cleaned up the
remaining kernels.

Problem
implicit_domain_updates recomputes xvrho(:,:,1:l,:) from xvtmp, but it never recomputes the k=0 ground
ghost layer. explicit_domain_updates has custom bottom-boundary code for xvrho(:,:,0,:), so the model
clearly expects that layer to track the current normalized state.
During MOA, the small-step solution advances in xvtmp; each call to implicit_domain_updates refreshes the
interior normalized fields but leaves the ground plane from the previous large-step explicit update.
After MOA, large_explicit_forcings can call firebrand with xvrho(:,:,:,iuvel:iwvel) over 0:l. GetWind uses
km=k-1, so particles in the first cell can interpolate against stale ground velocities.
This can make near-ground firebrand transport inconsistent with the final implicit small-step state,
especially when pressure, drag, buoyancy, or relaxation changed the first-layer winds during MOA.

Move the bottom-boundary construction into a shared helper and call it from both implicit_domain_updates
,→ and explicit_domain_updates immediately after the xvrho(:,:,1:l,:) halo updates.

Problem
explicit_domain_updates updates lateral halos and corners for xvrho(:,:,1:l,:), then computes only the
interior k=0 bottom plane. The turbulence routines document that the velocity/scalar fields must be

 261

valid on [0,np+1]*[0,mp+1]*[0,l], and their k=1 stencils read bottom-layer halos such as xvrho(0,j,0,*),
xvrho(np+1,j,0,*), xvrho(i,0,0,*), and corners.
Those values are either left from an older time, left at allocation-time contents, or missing MPI-
neighbor/corner updates. That contaminates bottom-face gradients in stressrij and diffuse, directly
affecting near-ground turbulent momentum and scalar fluxes.

After computing the interior k=0 bottom boundary, run the normal halo exchange on the single bottom
plane with icorner=1. This fills lateral halos and corners consistently with the freshly computed interior
values. The same helper proposed in DOMAINUPDATES-001 can do this for both explicit and implicit updates.

Problem
temps and the solid internal-energy field isies are created whenever imoist.eq.1, ifire.eq.1, or irad.gt.0.
But both implicit_domain_updates and explicit_domain_updates recompute temps only when ifire.eq.1.
That means non-fire moisture or radiation configurations can evolve xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies) while temps
remains at its old value. Several physics routines use temps directly: solar heating computes outgoing
longwave radiation from temps**4, radiation sink uses temps**4, Monte Carlo radiation updates/uses
temps, and evaporation uses temps for saturation/boiling logic.
This is a state-consistency bug: xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies) is the transported/evolved quantity, but the
derived temps field is stale whenever solid energy exists without active burning.

Gate the solid temperature refresh on the existence of isies, not on ifire. The code already uses
isies.ne.1 as the allocation/physics guard elsewhere.

Problem
explicit_domain_updates refreshes the derived solid temperature field before calling updateHeatSourcePosition
,→ . Despite its name, updateHeatSourcePosition does not only update geometry: it directly burns fuel
by assigning xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof) to 0.01_wp in active heat-source cells.
temps is derived from rhoFuel, rhoWater, and sies in updateSolidThermProps. If the heat source changes
rhoFuel after temps has been recomputed, then temps no longer matches the fuel state for the rest of
that large timestep.
That stale value is consumed immediately. The timestep driver calls small_explicit_forcings after
explicit_domain_updates, where radiation and diffusesies use temps. It then calls large_explicit_forcings,
where firebrand generation also uses temps alongside the newly changed xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof). This can
produce inconsistent heat loss, spread, ignition, or firebrand-launch behavior in heat-source cells.

Apply the heat-source fuel-density update before recomputing solid thermal properties, so temps is
derived from the final xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof) for the timestep.
If DOMAINUPDATES-003 is applied, keep the solid-temperature guard as isies.ne.1. If this report is applied
by itself, the minimal fix is just to move the existing if(iheatsource.gt.0) block above the existing
temperature-refresh block.

! boundary.F90
25           force(i,j,k,kv)=force(i,j,k,kv)+relaxxv(i,j,k,min(kv,4))* &
26             (xe(i,j,k,kv)-xv(i,j,k,kv))/dt

Problem
domainUpdates.F90 calls xevariation every large timestep when ixevariation.ge.1, passing the local interior
xe(1:np,1:mp,:,:) with i and j bounds.
In the sensor-driven branches, xevariation computes a height factor with zcart(z(k),j,k). But zcart
expects horizontal indices (i,j) and indexes terrain as zs(i,j). The current call passes the loop’s
y-index as the terrain x-index and the vertical level k as the terrain y-index.
When the vertical level range extends beyond the allocated y-index halo of zs, this can address outside
the second dimension inside zcart. When it stays in bounds, it still samples terrain from the wrong
horizontal cell, so the sensor wind target uses the wrong vertical coordinate. The bad xe then feeds
boundary relaxation through boundary.F90, and can force the domain toward a sensor wind profile based
on unrelated terrain.
This affects ixevariation == 3 and ixevariation == 4; the existing completed v-ramp loop-bound bug
covers a different branch.

Pass the current horizontal cell indices to zcart in the sensor branches.

BUG-2026-07-016: FORCE-002: Density can be clipped to exactly
zero, then divided by on the next update

Source report: forceF90/FORCE-002 (changed).md

• force.F90
• MOA.F90
• rinit.F90
• domainUpdates.F90

! rinit.F90
210   xvLim(1,irho)=0._wp
211   xvLim(2,irho)=10._wp

! force.F90
60 xv(i,j,k,kv)=max(xvLimits(1,kv),min(xvLimits(2,kv), &
61              xv(i,j,k,kv)))

! MOA.F90
93 call forcingLimits(xvtmp,xvLim,1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,nv)

! domainUpdates.F90
52 xvtmp(i,j,k,iEmitStart:iEmitStop)/xvtmp(i,j,k,irho), &
53 cpEmit,mwEmit,nEmit,xvtmp(i,j,k,itheta)/xvtmp(i,j,k,irho), &
...
57 xvrho(i,j,k,kv)=xvtmp(i,j,k,kv)/xvtmp(i,j,k,irho)

Problem
The limiter permits irho to become exactly 0.0_wp. That can happen after either the MOA small-step
limiter or the final large-step forcing limiter.
The very next domain update divides by density to compute species fractions, actual potential
temperature, and every xvrho component. A density value clipped to zero therefore becomes a divide-
by-zero/NaN source. The limiter prevents negative density but does not preserve the stronger invariant
the rest of the code requires:

xv(:,:,:,irho) > 0

Use a positive density floor, not zero. The floor should be chosen as a model parameter if there is
already a preferred low-density cutoff; otherwise a small constant is safer than exact zero.

 279

+++ b/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
@@
- xvLim(1,irho)=0._wp
+ xvLim(1,irho)=1.0e-6_wp
   xvLim(2,irho)=10._wp

A more explicit variant is to define a named rho_floor constant in constants or gridlist_variables and
use that value in both the limiter and any diagnostics that check for invalid density.

Git evidence: c21d0ea (2026-07-08, broad bug-list cleanup); 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches
to reduce bad runs).
The July validation pass added guardrails around invalid states and input combinations that could
otherwise drive density or derived physics into bad values.

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log July 2026

BUG-2026-07-017: FORCE-003: iturb=1 bypasses the existing
unsupported-mode stop and leaves fire physics using the wrong field
as kb

Source report: forceF90/FORCE-003 (changed).md

• force.F90
• subGridTurb/force_turb.F90
• definearray.F90
• Vegetation/convection_veg.F90
• Vegetation/evaporation_veg.F90
• Vegetation/burn_veg.F90

! force.F90

! subGridTurb/force_turb.F90

! definearray.F90
