! Vegetation/convection_veg.F90
46 rktemp=xvrho(i,j,k,ika)+1.2_wp*xvrho(i,j,k,ikb)

! Vegetation/burn_veg.F90
47           rkctemp=0.2_wp*xv(i,j,k,ikb)/xv(i,j,k,irho)

 282

Problem
calcForceTurb already has an explicit stop for iturb=1, but force.F90 never calls it for that mode because
the call is guarded by iturb.eq.2.
That means an iturb=1 run can continue past the intended "not implemented" stop. In this mode
definearray.F90 assigns ika, but does not assign a real ikb; ikb remains its default value of 1, which
is the u momentum field. Fire and moisture routines then use xvrho(...,ikb) or xv(...,ikb) as if it
were turbulent kinetic energy. This can create bad heat-transfer rates, bad burn rates, or sqrt() of
nonsensical values.

Let calcForceTurb handle every nonzero turbulence mode so the existing iturb=1 stop is actually reached.
If iturb=0 with fire/moisture is intended to be supported, the vegetation routines also need a no-TKE
branch; if not, input should reject that configuration explicitly.

+++ b/CODE-dev/force.F90
@@
- if(iturb.eq.2) call calcForceTurb(xv,forceSE_xv, &
+ if(iturb.gt.0) call calcForceTurb(xv,forceSE_xv, &
     1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,nv)

Optional follow-up validation:

@@
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’iturb’,iturb,48)
+ if(ifire.eq.1.and.iturb.ne.2) then
+ print*,’ERROR: fire physics currently requires iturb=2 because kb is used’
+ STOP
+ endif
 if(iturb.gt.0) call input_subGridTurb(iturb)

That second guard is deliberately conservative. A better long-term fix is to make convection, evapBulk,
and burnFuel handle iturb=0/1 without reading a missing kb field.

Git evidence: c21d0ea (2026-07-08, broad bug-list cleanup); 27c7afa (2026-08-17, subgrid turbulence
and thermodynamics bug-list pass).
The unsupported iturb=1 path was blocked for coupled fire physics and later turbulence code was
cleaned up so kernels use their explicit arguments.

Problem
The atmospheric arrays passed from force.F90 have vertical extent 1:l for xv/force_xv, and 0:l for xvrho.
The fuel arrays have extent 1:lfuel, and lfuel is inferred from the vegetation file size.
There is no guard that requires lfuel to fit inside the gas column. Several fuel physics routines assume
it does:

• dragm loops k=1:lfuel and reads/writes gas fields at gas level k, so it needs lfuel <= l.
• convection and evapBulk read xvrho(i,j,k:k+2,...), so they need lfuel <= l-2.
• burnFuel, evapPDF, and ZBEST also write gas forcing at fuel index k, so they need at least lfuel <= l.

The shipped sample cases use l=20 and usually lfuel=1, so the bug stays hidden. A deeper vegetation
file or a shallower gas grid can turn this into an out-of-bounds read/write.

Validate the fuel/gas vertical compatibility before entering these force paths. Failing fast is safer than
silently clamping lfuel, because skipping upper fuel layers would change physics without telling the
user.

+++ b/CODE-dev/force.F90
@@
 ! Executable Code

+ if(lfuel+2.gt.l) then
+ print*,’ERROR: lfuel must be <= l-2 for convection/evapBulk xvrho stencils’
+ STOP
+ endif

A more polished version should validate this once after rinitVeg determines lfuel, and should include
mpi_rank/mpi_finalize to match the codebase’s MPI error handling style.

BUG-2026-07-019: FORCE-005: icorio > 2 can index outside the
vertical column

Source report: forceF90/FORCE-005.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/force.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/input.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.
 ,→ F90

In force.F90, the Coriolis branch accepts any positive icorio:

  !Coriolis Forces
  if(icorio.ge.1)then
 do k=1,l
 do j=1,mp
 do i=1,np
 kref = k+(l-k)*(icorio-1) ! k or l depending icorio=1 or 2
          uc=xe(i,j,kref,1)
          vc=xe(i,j,kref,2)
 forceSI_xv(i,j,k,iuvel)=forceSI_xv(i,j,k,iuvel)+xv(i,j,k,irho)*fcorio*vc
 forceSI_xv(i,j,k,ivvel)=forceSI_xv(i,j,k,ivvel)-xv(i,j,k,irho)*fcorio*uc
 enddo
 enddo
 enddo
  endif !icorio.ge.1

input.F90 reads icorio directly:

  call QueryGridlist_integer(’icorio’,icorio,1)

variables.F90 documents it only as a generic option:

  integer :: icorio = 0 ! Option fors coriolis effect

Problem
The inline comment says the expression is only intended for icorio=1 or icorio=2. However, the guard
is icorio.ge.1, and there does not appear to be validation that rejects larger values.
For icorio=3, the computed index is:

kref = k + (l-k)*2 = 2*l - k

That exceeds the valid 1:l range for most vertical levels. Larger icorio values move even farther outside
the column. This can read invalid memory from xe(i,j,kref,...), producing crashes or silently corrupt
Coriolis forcing.

 290

Make the accepted modes explicit in force.F90, keep the mode branch outside the inner loops, and fail
fast for unsupported positive values.

+ if(icorio.eq.1)then

-           uc=xe(i,j,kref,1)
-           vc=xe(i,j,kref,2)
+           uc=xe(i,j,k,1)
+           vc=xe(i,j,k,2)

+ do k=1,l

Problem
When iemissions=2, the model reads efAero, but the force path never applies it. The only call is to
efSource, which loops over nEmit gas species. Aerosol moment fields in iEmitStart+nEmit:iEmitStop receive
no emission-factor source.
That makes aerosol emission-factor inputs silently ineffective: users can configure aerosol factors and
get no particulate forcing from this path. Because the gas species are still emitted, the run can look
superficially successful while aerosol outputs are biased low or identically missing.

The best fix is to add an aerosol-aware emission-factor routine and call it after the gas source. The
exact mapping from efAero into aerosol moments is a model decision, so the placeholder below shows
the force-side wiring and makes that decision explicit.

  frhof(ift,i,j,k) = frhof(ift,i,j,k) - (fkpp*...)*dtinvinv
  fsies(ift,i,j,k) = fsies(ift,i,j,k) + fkpp*...*dtinvinv

Problem
idiffsies is not guarded by the conditions that actually create the solid internal energy field. If a
configuration sets idiffsies=1 while ifire=0, imoist=0, and irad=0, then:

 297

• isies remains at its default value, which aliases the first fuel variable.
• temps is not allocated.
• force.F90 passes forceSE_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies) anyway.
• diffusesies reads temps and writes the aliased forcing array.

This can crash on an unallocated array reference. Worse, if bounds/runtime checks are not catching it,
isies=1 makes the density forcing and solid-energy forcing actual arguments refer to the same memory,
so the routine mixes density and energy tendencies through overlapping dummy arguments.

Fail fast before calling diffusesies unless the solid internal energy field exists.

Problem
The point-source routine assumes both searches always succeed, but neither result is checked.

rather than a code change.

BUG-2026-07-023: Large-scale PGF mass-flux reduction uses
repeated scalar MPI_Allreduces

Source report: MPI_5.md

What it does now
The large-scale pressure-gradient forcing path computes a local massFluxTemp and then performs one
MPI_Allreduce per element:

do i=1,nMassFlux
  call mpi_allreduce(massFluxTemp(i),massFlux(i),1,...)
enddo

Why this is inefficient
This creates nMassFlux separate collective calls, each with its own latency and synchronization cost.
When nMassFlux is more than a handful, the collective startup overhead can dominate.
A single vector MPI_Allreduce would do the same work with one collective.

Code evidence
From largeScalePGF.F90:

• repeated scalar allreduces: lines 279–288

Priority: Medium Collapse the loop into one vector collective.

--- a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/largeScalePGF.F90
+++ b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/largeScalePGF.F90
@@
- do i=1,nMassFlux
-#ifdef DBL_PREC
- call mpi_allreduce(massFluxTemp(i),massFlux(i),1, &
- mpi_double_precision,mpi_sum,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
-#else
- call mpi_allreduce(massFluxTemp(i),massFlux(i),1,mpi_real, &
- mpi_sum,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
-#endif
- enddo
+#ifdef DBL_PREC
+ call mpi_allreduce(massFluxTemp,massFlux,nMassFlux, &
+ mpi_double_precision,mpi_sum,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
+#else
+ call mpi_allreduce(massFluxTemp,massFlux,nMassFlux,mpi_real, &
+ mpi_sum,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
+#endif

 305

Expected speedup
• Medium
• especially helpful when largeScalePGF is called often and nMassFlux is not tiny

Git evidence: c21d0ea (2026-07-08, broad bug-list cleanup); ae1a78e (2026-08-18, speedups part 2).
The LSPGF mass-flux calculation was changed from repeated scalar reductions to array-based collective
communication, and the later speedup pass kept that path in the optimized loop order.

BUG-2026-07-024: EMISSIONS-023: ZBEST can be selected without
fire-enabled fuel state

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/EMISSIONS-023.md

Files
• input.F90
• force.F90
• definearray.F90
• Vegetation/definearray_veg.F90
• Emissions/zBEST_ems.F90

The input path accepts any positive iemissions value independently of ifire:

call QueryGridlist_integer(’iemissions’,iemissions,48)
if(ifire.eq.1.and.iemissions.eq.0) iemissions=2

The solid internal-energy pointer and fuel temperature array are only created when the fuel heat/fire
paths are enabled:

if(imoist.eq.1.or.ifire.eq.1.or.irad.gt.0)then
  isies = nvfuel+1
  nvfuel = nvfuel+1
endif

  allocate(temps(nfuel,1-ih:np+ih,1-ih:mp+ih,lfuel))
endif

But small_implicit_forcings calls ZBEST for iemissions=3 regardless of ifire or whether temps exists:

case (3)
  call ZBEST(forceSI_xv,xvtmp,-forceSI_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
    temps(:,1:np,1:mp,:),xvfueltmp(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
 1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,1,np,1,mp,lfuel,nv,nfuel,dts)

Problem
A gridlist can set iemissions=3 while ifire=0. In that configuration, the fire burn path is skipped, temps
may never be allocated, and forceSI_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof) remains zero because burnFuel is not called.

 308

The ZBEST call still passes temps(:,...) and fuel-consumption forcing. Depending on compiler/runtime
checks, this can fail immediately on an unallocated array section or silently run a ZBEST mode that
has no physical fuel-consumption source.
ZBEST is a fire-dependent emissions model; it should be rejected unless the fire/fuel state it needs is
enabled.

Validate the option combination while reading the gridlist, before array layout and allocation depend
on it.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 ! Emissions
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’iemissions’,iemissions,48)
 if(ifire.eq.1.and.iemissions.eq.0) iemissions=2
+ if(iemissions.eq.3.and.ifire.ne.1)then
+ print*,’ERROR: iemissions=3 (ZBEST) requires ifire=1’
+ stop
+ endif

 call QueryGridlist_real(’relativehumidity’,relativeHumidity,48)

If ZBEST is later extended to work from an externally supplied burn-rate field, that mode should pass
an allocated temperature field and a validated fuel-consumption source explicitly instead of reusing the
fire-only arrays.

Git evidence: c21d0ea (2026-07-08, broad bug-list cleanup); 91c2a57 (2026-07-22, aerosol merge fixes).
ZBEST/emissions activation was tied to the fire-enabled fuel state through the July validation work
and the aerosol merge, so the mode no longer relies on absent fire arrays.

The input path accepts any positive iemissions value and initializes the emissions module:

call QueryGridlist_integer(’iemissions’,iemissions,48)
if(ifire.eq.1.and.iemissions.eq.0) iemissions=2

The force path implements only modes 1, 2, and 3:

select case (iemissions)
  case (1)
 call pointSource(forceSI_xv(:,:,:,iEmitStart:iEmitStop), &
 1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,nEmit,nAero,nMAero)
  case (2)
 call efSource(forceSI_xv(:,:,:,iEmitStart:iEmitStop), &
      -forceSI_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof),1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l, &
 1,np,1,mp,lfuel,nfuel,nEmit)
  case (3)
 call ZBEST(forceSI_xv,xvtmp,-forceSI_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
      temps(:,1:np,1:mp,:),xvfueltmp(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
 1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,1,np,1,mp,lfuel,nv,nfuel,dts)

Problem
Values such as iemissions = 4 are treated as active emissions during input and array definition, because
they are positive. input_emissions can read species and aerosol configuration, xvpointers can add
emission variables to xv, and rinitEmission can apply emission limits.
During time stepping, however, small_implicit_forcings has no matching case, so no emission source
routine runs. The model can therefore carry apparently configured emission fields that never receive a
source term. Negative unsupported values have the opposite silent failure: they skip initialization and
forcing without any diagnostic.
This is especially easy to miss because the valid modes are encoded only by convention in separate files.
A typo in the gridlist changes the transported variable layout or disables emissions instead of stopping
with a clear error.

 312

Validate the mode immediately after reading it, and add a defensive case default in the force path so
unsupported modes cannot silently pass through if the value is changed later.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 ! Emissions
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’iemissions’,iemissions,48)
+ if(iemissions.lt.0.or.iemissions.gt.3)then
+ print*,’ERROR: invalid iemissions value ’,iemissions, &
+      ’. Valid values are 0, 1, 2, or 3.’
+ stop
+ endif
 if(ifire.eq.1.and.iemissions.eq.0) iemissions=2

+++ b/CODE-dev/force.F90
@@
 case (3)
 call ZBEST(forceSI_xv,xvtmp,-forceSI_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
         temps(:,1:np,1:mp,:),xvfueltmp(:,:,:,:,irhof), &
 1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,1,np,1,mp,lfuel,nv,nfuel,dts)
+ case default
+ if(iemissions.ne.0)then
+ print*,’ERROR: unsupported iemissions value in forcing ’,iemissions
+ stop
+ endif

Combine this with the iemissions=3/ifire compatibility check so every implemented mode also has the
state it requires.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs); 91c2a57 (2026-07-22,
aerosol merge fixes).
The input-validation crutch pass added stops/warnings for unsupported mode values, and the aerosol
merge made the supported emission modes explicit in the forcing path.

BUG-2026-07-026: FIREBRANDS-009: Default firebrand restart file
points at an incompatible main-output file

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/FIREBRANDS-009.md

Files
• Firebrands/variables_fb.F90
• Firebrands/io_fb.F90

The default firebrand restart path is the main model output name:

character(len=257) :: restartfile_fb = ’comp.out.h5’ ! Name of restart file

The firebrand restart reader opens that file as a Fortran unformatted firebrand file:

open(48,file=restartfile_fb,form=’unformatted’,status=’old’)

Firebrand output is written in a different custom binary stream:

call namefile(ittot,outname_fb,fname)
open(48,file=fname,form=’unformatted’,status=’unknown’)
write(48) sum(totNumBrands)
write(48) xvtotBrands

Problem
If irst=1 and the user does not override restartfile_fb, the firebrand restart routine tries to parse
comp.out.h5 as the two-record firebrand binary format. That can fail immediately, read garbage into
numBrands, or attempt an enormous allocation.
The default should not point at an incompatible file type. It should either be blank and explicitly
required for firebrand restart, or point to a firebrand output file generated by writeio_fb.

Make the default empty and stop with a clear error when a firebrand restart is requested without a
firebrand restart file.

diff --git a/CODE-dev/Firebrands/variables_fb.F90 b/CODE-dev/Firebrands/variables_fb.F90

BUG-2026-07-027: FIREBRANDS-012: ifbrand > 1 writes
uninitialized firebrand arrays

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/FIREBRANDS-012.md

Files
• compress.F90
• rinit.F90
• force.F90
• Firebrands/io_fb.F90

Initialization and forcing only run for exactly ifbrand == 1:

if(ifbrand.eq.1) call rinitFirebrands(irst)

if(ifbrand.eq.1) call firebrand(...)

But output runs for any positive value:

if(ifbrand.ge.1) call writeio_fb(time)

writeio_fb assumes the firebrand array exists:

call mpi_gatherv(xvbrand(:,it),numBrands,mpi_wp, &
  xvtotBrands(:,it),totNumBrands,displs,mpi_wp,0, &

Problem
If a gridlist sets ifbrand=2 or any other positive unsupported value, Firebrands are never initialized or
evolved, but compress still calls writeio_fb. numBrands remains zero, yet xvbrand is unallocated, so taking
xvbrand(:,it) is illegal even with a zero MPI send count.
This turns an unsupported option value into a crash in the output path. The output condition should
match the initialization/forcing condition, and invalid options should be rejected during input.

Validate the option when it is read:

 320

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 ! Firebrands
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’ifbrand’,ifbrand,48)
+ if(ifbrand.lt.0.or.ifbrand.gt.1) &
+ STOP ’ERROR: ifbrand must be 0 or 1.’
 if(ifbrand.eq.1) call input_firebrands

The writeio_fb(ittot) part also fixes the real/integer argument mismatch described in FIREBRANDS-006.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs); 869ead7 (2026-06-25,
boundary-error pass); af8cb71 (2026-07-23, firebrand restart close).

BUG-2026-07-028: FIREBRANDS-019: Nonpositive firebrand
geometry inputs can produce divide-by-zero and NaNs

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/FIREBRANDS-019.md

Files
• Firebrands/input_fb.F90
• Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
• Firebrands/generation_fb.F90

User-provided geometry and density values are read without validation:

call QueryGridlist_real(’radiusFB’,radius,48)
call QueryGridlist_real(’heightFB’,height,48)
call QueryGridlist_real(’rhoFB’,rhoFB,48)

The evolution code divides by these dimensions and density:

sqrt(w_abs*nu/xvbrand(it,ihght))

rhog(i,j,k)/xvbrand(it,irho)* &
  sqrt(w_abs*nu/(xvbrand(it,irad)*pi))

The launch code also uses the values in volumes and forces:

force_grav=g*rhoFB*(pi*radius**2*height)

Problem

The default values are positive, but a bad gridlist value currently reaches the physics unchecked.

Reject nonphysical values immediately after reading the Firebrands gridlist inputs.

Problem
A gridlist can set ifbrand=1 while leaving ifire=0, imoist=0, and irad=0. In that configuration, isies
keeps its default value, temps is not allocated, and large_explicit_forcings still passes temps(:,:,:,:)
into the Firebrands driver.
That can crash on an unallocated allocatable array reference. If checks do not catch it, launchFB reads
undefined fuel temperatures to decide whether to create new firebrands.
Firebrand launch currently depends on the fire/fuel temperature machinery, so the input layer should
reject unsupported Firebrand-only configurations instead of letting the run fail later.

Require active fire physics before accepting ifbrand=1. This diff also uses the no-argument
input_firebrands call expected by the Firebrands input routine.

If Firebrands should support non-fire external heating in the future, then ifbrand also needs to
participate in the isies/temps allocation and temperature-refresh guards. With the current launch
model, failing early is the safer minimal fix.

BUG-2026-07-030: HEATSOURCE-001: Unsupported per-source
option values silently change or disable heat-source forcing

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/HEATSOURCE-001.md

Files
• HeatSource/input_heat.F90
• HeatSource/heatsource_heat.F90
• HeatSource/rinit_heat.F90

input_heat.F90 reads several option arrays but does not validate their values:

call QueryGridlist_real_array(’isource_function_hs’,tmp,nsource_hs,48)
isource_function_hs = nint(tmp)
...

imass_source_hs = nint(tmp)

call QueryGridlist_real_array(’MLRHRRinputs_hs’,tmp,nsource_hs,48)
MLRHRRinputs_hs = nint(tmp)

The forcing path only implements isource_function_hs cases 0 through 3:

source_function=0.0_wp
select case(isource_function_hs(itsource))
  case(0)
 source_function=1.0_wp
  case(1)

 source_function = 1.0_wp
 endif
  case(2)
 source_function = 0.5_wp* &
      (1.0_wp+sin(2.0_wp*pi*freq_hs(itsource)*time))
  case(3)
 if((freq_hs(itsource).gt.0.0_wp).and. &
 (freq_hs(itsource)*time.le.1.0_wp))then
 source_function = 1.0_wp
 endif

Mass source options other than 1 and 2 fall through with no mass forcing:

if(imass_source_hs(itsource).eq.1)then
  frho=coverfrac*energy/(hf/rnfuel)
  force(i,j,k,irho)=force(i,j,k,irho)+frho

  ...

MLR/HRR files are enabled only when the flag equals exactly 1:

if(any(MLRHRRinputs_hs.eq.1)) then
  ...
  if(MLRHRRinputs_hs(itsource).ne.1) cycle

Problem
Invalid per-source options are accepted during input and then interpreted as quiet no-ops or as a
different mode:

• isource_function_hs = 4 leaves source_function at zero, so the source is active by time window but
  injects no heat.
• imass_source_hs = 3 applies heat but no gas-phase mass source.
• MLRHRRinputs_hs = 2 does not read the MLR/HRR file path and falls back to the flux-based heat
  path instead.

These are configuration errors, but the simulation can continue without a diagnostic. Because the
arrays are per-source, a single typo can disable only one heat source in a multi-source setup, making
the result especially hard to spot.

Validate the option arrays immediately after converting them to integers, and add defensive defaults in
the runtime select case.

BUG-2026-07-031: HEATSOURCE-009: Heat-source geometry and
time inputs are not validated

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/HEATSOURCE-009.md

Files
• HeatSource/input_heat.F90
• HeatSource/heatsource_heat.F90

input_heat.F90 reads timing, heat, depth, and geometry arrays without sanity checks:

call QueryGridlist_real_array(’starttime_hs’,starttime_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’endtime_hs’,endtime_hs,nsource_hs,48)

allocate(freq_hs(nsource_hs),av_hs(nsource_hs),flux_hs(nsource_hs), &
  depth_hs(nsource_hs))
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’av_hs’,av_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’flux_hs’,flux_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’freq_hs’,freq_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’depth_hs’,depth_hs,nsource_hs,48)

Circle geometry is read directly:

allocate(xcen_hs(nsource_hs),ycen_hs(nsource_hs), &
  radius_hs(nsource_hs))
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’radius_hs’,radius_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’xcen_hs’,xcen_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’ycen_hs’,ycen_hs,nsource_hs,48)

Rectangle geometry is also read directly:

allocate(xl_hs(nsource_hs),xu_hs(nsource_hs), &
  yl_hs(nsource_hs),yu_hs(nsource_hs))
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’xl_hs’,xl_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’xu_hs’,xu_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’yl_hs’,yl_hs,nsource_hs,48)
call QueryGridlist_real_array(’yu_hs’,yu_hs,nsource_hs,48)

Downstream code quietly treats invalid values as no overlap or no active source. For example,
nonpositive circle radius returns zero area:

hs_circle_rect_area = 0.0_wp
if(r.le.0.0_wp) return

Inverted time windows are simply inactive:

 335

heatsource_active = time.ge.starttime_hs(itsource) .and. &
  time.lt.endtime_hs(itsource)

Problem
Several invalid or physically suspicious heat-source inputs are accepted and then become silent no-ops
or unintended sinks:

• radius_hs <= 0 makes circular sources produce no area and no heat.
• xl_hs >= xu_hs or yl_hs >= yu_hs makes rectangular sources produce no area and no heat.
• depth_hs <= 0 makes the heat volume zero.
• endtime_hs <= starttime_hs makes the source inactive for the whole run.
• negative av_hs or flux_hs turns a heat source into a heat sink.
• freq_hs <= 0 is incompatible with the single-pulse source function.

These are almost always gridlist mistakes. Continuing without a diagnostic wastes full simulations and
makes the output look like the heat source simply failed to ignite.

Validate source parameters after the relevant arrays are read. Keep the checks close to input_heat.F90
so bad configurations fail before the run starts.

+++ b/CODE-dev/HeatSource/input_heat.F90

+ STOP
+ endif

BUG-2026-07-033: INPUT-005: Cadence inputs are not validated
before being used as mod divisors

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/INPUT-005.md

Files
• input.F90
• compress.F90
• domainUpdates.F90
• xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90
• xeVariation/windfield.F90
• Sensors/input_sense.F90

input.F90 reads cadence values without range checks:

  call QueryGridlist_integer(’frqoutput’,frqoutput,48)
  ...
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’frqlspgf’,frqlspgf,48)

Those values are later used as divisors in mod:

  if(mod(it,frqoutput).eq.0)then

Child input routines read more cadence values that are also used as divisors:

  call QueryGridlist_integer(’itinterp’,itinterp,48)
  ...
  if(ittot.ge.itwindfield.and.mod(ittot,itinterp).eq.0)then

  call QueryGridlist_integer(’se_frq_write’,se_frq_write,48)
  ...
  if((isensor.eq.1).and.(mod(it,se_frq_write).eq.0))then

  call QueryGridlist_integer(’freqSensor’,freqSensor,48)
  ...
  if(mod(ittot,freqSensor).eq.0) then

 344

Problem
If any of these gridlist values are zero, Fortran evaluates mod(value,0), which is invalid and commonly
crashes at runtime. Negative cadence values are also nonsensical and can produce confusing scheduling
behavior.
These are user-input errors, so they should be caught in the input layer with a specific message. Waiting
until the time loop or xe-variation update makes the failure later and harder to connect back to the
bad gridlist key.

Validate cadence values immediately after reading them, and validate conditional cadences only when
their feature is enabled.

BUG-2026-07-034: INPUT-009: topofile is truncated to 60
characters before topo.F90 opens it

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/INPUT-009.md

Files
• input.F90
• variables.F90
• rinit.F90
• topo.F90

Most file-name inputs in gridlist_variables use 257 characters:

  character(len=257) :: outname = ’comp.out’
  character(len=257) :: restartfile = ’’

But topofile is only 60 characters:

  character(len=60) :: topofile = ’’ ! Name of topo file

input.F90 reads the gridlist value directly into that variable:

  call QueryGridlist_string (’topofile’,topofile,48)

rinit.F90 and topo.F90 then use the stored value:

  if(topofile(1:1)/=’*’.and.topofile/=’␣’) call topo

  open(25,file=topofile,form=’unformatted’,status=’old’)

Problem
An absolute topography file path can easily exceed 60 characters. For example, paths under the
versioned tree in this workspace already have long prefixes. Reading such a path into character(len=60)
truncates it before topo.F90 opens the file, so a valid gridlist path can become a nonexistent path at
runtime.
The rest of the I/O-related path variables already use 257 characters, so topofile is an inconsistent
and surprisingly short limit.

 348

Use the same length as the other major file-name inputs.

+++ b/CODE-dev/variables.F90
@@
- character(len=60) :: topofile = ’’ ! Name of topo file
+ character(len=257) :: topofile = ’’ ! Name of topo file

If longer paths are expected, define a shared path-length parameter and use it consistently for all
path-like gridlist variables.

The topography file path is now opened with the full trimmed topofile string, and the shared filename
buffers were cleaned up so valid long paths are not truncated at the old short limit.

BUG-2026-07-035: INPUT-010: Relaxation inputs can trigger
divisions by zero in tinit

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/INPUT-010.md

Files
• input.F90
• tinit.F90
• variables.F90

input.F90 reads relaxation controls without checking their ranges:

  call QueryGridlist_integer(’nr’,nr,48)
  ...
  call QueryGridlist_real (’zab’,zab,48)
  call QueryGridlist_real (’tow’,tow,48)

tinit.F90 allocates relb from nr, writes the first two columns, and divides by expressions involving nr:

  allocate(relb(4,nr+1)); relb = 0.0_wp
  ...
              real(nr-1,kind=wp)**2.0_wp))
  ...
 real(nr-1,kind=wp))
  ...
              (0.5_wp*real(nr,kind=wp)-1.0_wp))**2.0_wp))
  ...
  relb(:,1:2)=1.0_wp

The top absorber also divides by tow:

  relaxxv(i,j,k,:)=t1/((zb-zab)+1.e-10_wp)/tow**2.0_wp
  ...
  relaxxv(i,j,k,1:3)=0.66_wp*0.25_wp*(1.0_wp-cos(pi*(zl-zab)/(zb-zab)))/tow

Problem
Several invalid gridlist values fail inside tinit instead of at input time:

• nr=0 allocates only one relb column, then relb(:,1:2)=1.0_wp writes beyond the allocation.
• nr=1 makes real(nr-1) zero in relaxation cases 1, 3, and 4.
• nr=2 makes (0.5*nr - 1) zero in relaxation case 2.
• tow=0 makes top absorber formulas divide by zero.

 351

The defaults are safe, but a bad gridlist can create invalid relaxation coefficients or crash later in
initialization.

Validate the absorber controls after resolving per-side defaults.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 if(ibc_top.eq.7825) ibc_top = ibcy
 if(ibc_bot.eq.7825) ibc_bot = ibcy

 if(ibc_right.eq.7825) ibc_right = ibcx
+
+ if(nr.lt.1)then
+ print*,’ERROR: nr must be at least 1’
+ STOP
+ endif
+ if((ibc_top.ge.1.and.ibc_top.lt.5 .or. &
+      ibc_bot.ge.1.and.ibc_bot.lt.5 .or. &
+ ibc_left.ge.1.and.ibc_left.lt.5 .or. &
+ ibc_right.ge.1.and.ibc_right.lt.5) .and. nr.lt.3)then
+ print*,’ERROR: nr must be at least 3 for relaxation boundary options 1-4’
+ STOP
+ endif

Parentheses can be adjusted to match the project’s style; the key point is to reject invalid relaxation
inputs before tinit allocates or divides.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs); a8b1c58 (2026-08-17,
tinit/topo/variables bug-list pass).

BUG-2026-07-036: INPUT-011: Unsupported iheatsource values are
accepted as enabled heat sources

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/INPUT-011.md

Files
• input.F90
• HeatSource/input_heat.F90
• HeatSource/heatsource_heat.F90
• domainUpdates.F90

input.F90 treats any value greater than or equal to 1 as enabled:

  call QueryGridlist_integer(’iheatsource’,iheatsource,48)
  if(iheatsource.ge.1) call input_heatsource(iheatsource)

input_heatsource only allocates geometry arrays for modes 1 and 2:

  if(iheatsource.eq.1)then
 allocate(xcen_hs(nsource_hs),ycen_hs(nsource_hs), &
 radius_hs(nsource_hs))
 ...
  elseif(iheatsource.eq.2)then
 allocate(xl_hs(nsource_hs),xu_hs(nsource_hs), &
 yl_hs(nsource_hs),yu_hs(nsource_hs))
 ...
  endif

The heat-source implementation also only handles modes 1 and 2:

  if(iheatsource.eq.1) then ! Circular
 ...
  elseif(iheatsource.eq.2) then ! Rectangular
 ...
  endif

  if(iheatsource.eq.1)then !Circular source
 ...
  elseif(iheatsource.eq.2)then !Rectangular source
 ...
  endif

 355

Problem
A gridlist value like iheatsource=3 is accepted and causes heat-source input arrays to be allocated,
rinitHeatSource to run, domainUpdates to call updateHeatSourcePosition, and force.F90 to call heatSource.
But no geometry is read and the heat-source routines do not apply any source for that mode.
That is a silent no-op for a user who explicitly enabled heat sources. It should fail during input parsing
instead of running a simulation with the requested source absent.

Validate iheatsource before calling the heat-source input routine, and validate nsource_hs when the
feature is enabled.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 !Heat source
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’iheatsource’,iheatsource,48)
+ if(iheatsource.ne.0.and.iheatsource.ne.1.and.iheatsource.ne.2)then
+ print*,’ERROR: iheatsource must be 0, 1 circular, or 2 rectangular’
+ STOP

BUG-2026-07-037: INPUT-012: Xe-variation input ranges can cause
divide-by-zero or out-of-bounds windfield access

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/INPUT-012.md

Files
• input.F90
• xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90
• xeVariation/rinit_xeVar.F90
• xeVariation/xevariation.F90
• xeVariation/windfield.F90

input_xevariation reads windfield and sensor dimensions without range checks:

 call QueryGridlist_integer(’windspeedupfactor’,windspeedupfactor,48)

Those values are later used as divisors and array bounds:

  if(npos.eq.1) xvdatanew(1:ibcells,:,:,:)= &
    indatai(1:ibcells,mp*(mpos-1)+1:mp*mpos,:,:)
  if(npos.eq.nprocx) xvdatanew(np-ibcells+1:np,:,:,:)= &
 indatai(ibcells+1:ibcells*2,mp*(mpos-1)+1:mp*mpos,:,:)

Sensor mode also divides by sensor heights:

  (zcart(z(k),j,k)/SensorZ(kv))**(1.0_wp/7.0_wp)

Problem
Several invalid xe-variation inputs are accepted until they fail later:

 359

• windspeedupfactor=0 causes integer division by zero in rinit_xeVar and xevariation.
• ibcells > np or jbcells > mp causes out-of-bounds slices in windfld_read; np and mp are n/nprocx and
  m/nprocy.
• nSensors <= 0 allocates empty sensor arrays and can silently zero the velocity fields in sensor-driven
  xe-variation modes.
• SensorZ <= 0 causes division by zero or invalid fractional powers in sensor interpolation.

INPUT-005 covers cadence divisors like itinterp and freqSensor; this issue covers the other xe-variation
dimensions and divisors.

Validate windfield dimensions against the configured domain decomposition and validate sensor arrays
after reading them.

BUG-2026-07-038: RADIATION-007: icallrad is not validated
before use as a MOD divisor

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/RADIATION-007.md

Files
• Radiation/input_rad.F90
• Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90

input_radiation reads icallrad directly from the gridlist:

call QueryGridlist_integer(’icallrad’,icallrad,48)

  call QueryGridlist_real (’crad’,crad,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’irandseed’,irandseed,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’iseed’,iseed,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’isootmodel’,isootmodel,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’iradeastflux’,iradeastflux,48)
endif

The Monte Carlo radiation driver uses it as the divisor in mod:

  call papv_defs ! define papvtotAZ,papvgas,papvtot
  call source_defs ! define sourcegas, sourcesol, EAZ, Etot, and lmc
  if(Etot.ge.Emin) call montecarlo

Problem
A gridlist value of icallrad=0 causes an immediate integer divide-by-zero in mod(ittot,icallrad). Negative
values do not crash consistently, but they make the call-frequency semantics ambiguous and can suppress
or mis-schedule Monte Carlo updates.
This is a configuration error that should fail at input time with a clear message.

Validate icallrad as soon as it is read. Since it only controls the Monte Carlo path, the validation can
be limited to irad=2; accepting it for all radiation modes is also fine if the gridlist always contains it.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/input_rad.F90
@@
 ! Executable Code
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’icallrad’,icallrad,48)

 363

+ if(irad.eq.2.and.icallrad.le.0)then
+ print*,’ERROR: icallrad must be greater than zero for Monte Carlo radiation’
+ STOP
+ endif

It would also be useful to validate irandseed, isootmodel, and iradeastflux as enumerated options in the
same routine so typos do not silently choose unintended model branches.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs); 9ce10f9 (2026-08-13,
radiation bug-list pass); 46f574d (2026-07-29, custom firerad gridlist argument).
Radiation mode validation was tightened and the Monte Carlo implementation was substantially
reworked in the August radiation pass, including cleaner source selection and firerad gridlist handling.

BUG-2026-07-039: RADIATION-010: Invalid radiation modes and
options are silently accepted

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/RADIATION-010.md

Files
• input.F90
• force.F90
• Radiation/input_rad.F90
• Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90

The main input routine reads irad and accepts any positive value:

! Radiation
call QueryGridlist_integer(’irad’,irad,48)
if(irad.gt.0) call input_radiation(irad)

The forcing routine only handles modes 1, 2, and 3:

if(irad.eq.1)then ! Diffusive Radiation Scheme
  if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’Diffusive␣Radiation␣Not␣implemented’
  call mpi_finalize(ierror)
  STOP
elseif(irad.eq.2)then ! Monte-Carlo Radiation Scheme
  call firerad_MC(forceSE_xv(:,:,:,itheta), &
    forceSE_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies), &
    xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof)+xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhow), &
    1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,1,np,1,mp,l,nfuel)
elseif(irad.eq.3)then ! Radiation Sink
  call radiationSink(forceSE_xv(:,:,:,itheta), &

For Monte Carlo radiation, several option values are read without validation:

  call QueryGridlist_real (’crad’,crad,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’irandseed’,irandseed,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’iseed’,iseed,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’isootmodel’,isootmodel,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’iradeastflux’,iradeastflux,48)
endif

isootmodel treats every value except 1 as the alternate model:

if(isootmodel.eq.1)then
  ...
else

 366

  ...
  papvgas(i,j,k)=crad*aemit*absemis*0.25_wp

Problem
Invalid radiation settings can silently produce the wrong behavior:

• irad=4 or any other unsupported positive value calls input_radiation and rinitrad, but no radiation
  branch runs in force.F90. The user gets no radiation and no error.
• invalid isootmodel values fall into the else branch and select the non-soot-model formula.
• invalid irandseed values behave like "do not randomize".
• invalid iradeastflux values behave like "do not output east flux".
• negative crad makes papvgas negative in the non-soot-model branch, which can create negative gas
  emission/absorption terms and nonsensical Etot.

These are gridlist mistakes that should fail before the simulation starts.

Validate the mode and enumerated options at input time.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 ! Radiation
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’irad’,irad,48)
+ if(irad.lt.0.or.irad.gt.3)then
+ print*,’ERROR: irad must be 0, 1, 2, or 3’
+ STOP
+ endif

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/input_rad.F90
@@

 call QueryGridlist_integer(’isootmodel’,isootmodel,48)

+ if(irandseed.lt.0.or.irandseed.gt.1)then
+ print*,’ERROR: irandseed must be 0 or 1’
+ STOP
+ endif
+ if(isootmodel.lt.0.or.isootmodel.gt.1)then
+ print*,’ERROR: isootmodel must be 0 or 1’
+ STOP
+ endif

+ print*,’ERROR: iradeastflux must be 0 or 1’
+ STOP
+ endif

 367

+ if(isootmodel.eq.0.and.crad.lt.0.0_wp)then

+ endif

BUG-2026-07-040: SUBGRIDTURB-006: Invalid isa leaves

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/SUBGRIDTURB-006.md

Files
• subGridTurb/input_turb.F90
• subGridTurb/rinit_turb.F90

isa is read from the gridlist without range checking:

rinitSubTurb only assigns saxy and saz for isa=1:5, but it always uses those values afterward:

the simulation can proceed with arbitrary eddy length scales.

bypass the check.

BUG-2026-07-041: SUBGRIDTURB-009: Negative rturbprandtl
turns scalar turbulence diffusion into anti-diffusion

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/SUBGRIDTURB-009.md

Files
• subGridTurb/input_turb.F90
• subGridTurb/force_turb.F90
• subGridTurb/diffuse_turb.F90
• subGridTurb/variables_turb.F90

rturbprandtl is read directly from the gridlist without a range check:

! subGridTurb/input_turb.F90
13 if(iturb.eq.2)then ! Rod Linn subgrid Turbulence Model
14 call QueryGridlist_integer(’isa’,isa,48)
15 call QueryGridlist_real (’rturbprandtl’,rturbprandtl,48)
16 endif

The variable is documented as the scalar diffusion multiplier:

! subGridTurb/variables_turb.F90
10 real(wp) :: rturbprandtl = 2.0_wp ! Inverse of turb prandtl number for scalar diffusion

calcForceTurb applies it to every non-TKE scalar in the turbulence diffusion loop:

! subGridTurb/force_turb.F90
46 ! turbulent diffusion of all non-wind fields
47 do kv=itheta,nv-1
48 if(kv.eq.ika.or.kv.eq.ikb)then
49         call diffuse(force_xv(:,:,:,kv),xvrho(:,:,:,kv), &
50            1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,one)
51 else
52         call diffuse(force_xv(:,:,:,kv),xvrho(:,:,:,kv), &
53 1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,rturbprandtl)
54 endif
55 enddo

Inside diffuse, cdiff multiplies the divergence of the turbulent flux directly:

! subGridTurb/diffuse_turb.F90
40 real(wp),intent(in) :: cdiff ! ratio between vt of variable iv and simple vt (ie rturbprandtl
 ,→ for theta and o2)
...
142         r=cdiff*gi(i,j,k)*(dxi*(hxc(i+1,j,k)-hxc(i,j,k))+dyi*(hyc(i,j+1,k)-hyc(i,j,k)) &
143           +dzi*(hzc(i,j,k+1)-hzc(i,j,k)))

 374

144         fphi(i,j,k)=fphi(i,j,k)+r

Problem
A negative rturbprandtl is accepted and passed straight into diffuse as cdiff. Since cdiff is a direct
multiplier on the scalar diffusion tendency, a negative value reverses the sign of the operator for theta,
emissions/species, water vapor, oxygen, mixture fraction, and other non-TKE scalars.
That turns turbulent diffusion into anti-diffusion: gradients are sharpened instead of smoothed. The
failure can look like a numerical instability in thermodynamics, emissions, or fire coupling even though
the root cause is a bad turbulence input value.
The default value is positive, so normal cases are unaffected. The bug is that an invalid gridlist value
is not rejected before it reaches the physics.

Reject negative scalar diffusion multipliers when reading the turbulence inputs.

diff --git a/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/input_turb.F90 b/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/input_turb.F90
--- a/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/input_turb.F90
+++ b/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/input_turb.F90
@@

+ use gridlist_variables, only : wp

@@
 if(iturb.eq.2)then ! Rod Linn subgrid Turbulence Model
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’isa’,isa,48)
 call QueryGridlist_real (’rturbprandtl’,rturbprandtl,48)
+ if(rturbprandtl.lt.0.0_wp)then
+ print*,’ERROR: rturbprandtl must be non-negative for scalar turbulence diffusion’
+ STOP
+ endif
 endif

If zero is not intended to mean "disable turbulent scalar diffusion," tighten this to rturbprandtl.le.0.0_wp
instead.

subgrid turbulence and thermodynamics bug-list pass); 44f9732 (2026-08-25, subgrid diffusion cleanup
and small bug fix).

BUG-2026-07-042: TINIT-003: Invalid top-absorber settings silently
disable or corrupt damping

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/TINIT-003.md

Files
• tinit.F90
• input.F90
• variables.F90

input.F90 reads the top absorber controls without checking their ranges:

call QueryGridlist_integer(’ibctopopen’,ibctopopen,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’iab’,iab,48)
call QueryGridlist_real (’zab’,zab,48)
call QueryGridlist_real (’tow’,tow,48)

tinit.F90 has no case default for a bad iab value. In the June 26 tree only iab=1:3 do anything in the
closed-top branch:

  case(1)
    relaxxv(i,j,k,:)=t1/((zb-zab)+1.e-10_wp)/tow**2.0_wp
  case(2)
    relaxxv(i,j,k,:)=0.05_wp*exp(-t1/(-(zb-zab)/log(tow**(-2.0_wp))))
  case(3)
    relaxxv(i,j,k,1:3)=0.66_wp*0.25_wp*(1.0_wp-cos(pi*(zl-zab)/(zb-zab)))/tow

The open-top branch still divides by tow:

relaxxv(i,j,k,3)=0.66_wp*0.25_wp*(1.0_wp-cos(pi*(zl-zab)/(zb-zab)))/tow

Problem
Several invalid settings survive input and fail later in less obvious ways:

• Any iab value without an implemented branch silently leaves the closed-top absorber unset because
  the select case has no default.
• tow=0 divides by zero in options 1 and 3, the open-top branch, and lateral boundary option 2.
• tow<0 can produce negative damping for /tow branches and NaNs in tow**(-2.0_wp) because that
  expression uses a real exponent.
• iab=2 with tow=1 evaluates log(1) in the denominator, causing division by zero.

 378

Older 1.5.x trees also had an iab=4 scalar/theta top-damper path using zabt. If that path is restored as
in TINIT-004, iab=4 should be treated as valid. If it is not restored, iab=4 should be rejected instead of
silently doing nothing.
The result is either no top damping, invalid relaxation coefficients, or damping with the wrong
sign. Because boundary.F90 applies relaxxv every small step, these bad coefficients directly affect the
momentum and scalar forcing.

Fail early in input.F90, while the bad values are still clearly tied to the gridlist.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@

BUG-2026-07-043: TINIT-008: Over-wide lateral sponge regions can
cover the whole domain

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/TINIT-008.md

Files
• tinit.F90
• input.F90
• variables.F90

nr is the lateral relaxation width:

integer :: nr = 5 ! Number of cells for lateral relaxation (irlx, irly)

tinit.F90 applies the bottom/left sponge to cells whose global index is at most nr:

if(ja.le.nr)then
  relaxxv(i,j,k,it)=max(relaxxv(i,j,k,it),relb(2,ja))
endif
...
if(ia.le.nr)then
  relaxxv(i,j,k,it)=max(relaxxv(i,j,k,it),relb(3,ia))
endif

It applies the top/right sponge to cells whose global index is within nr cells of the far side:

if(ja.gt.m-nr)then
  relaxxv(i,j,k,it)=max(relaxxv(i,j,k,it),relb(1,m-ja+1))
endif
...
if(ia.gt.n-nr)then
  relaxxv(i,j,k,it)=max(relaxxv(i,j,k,it),relb(4,n-ia+1))
endif

input.F90 does not validate nr against n or m.

Problem
If nr is too large for the horizontal domain, the lateral sponge can cover the whole domain instead of
only boundary-adjacent cells.
For example, if both left and right boundaries are active and 2*nr >= n, every x-column is in at least
one x-direction sponge. If nr >= n, even a single active x-side sponge covers every x-column. The same
issue applies in y with m.
The index expressions remain in bounds because relb is allocated to nr+1, so this does not necessarily

 381

crash. It silently turns a boundary buffer into a domain-wide relaxation force toward xe, which can
suppress interior dynamics and make small-domain tests misleading.

After resolving the explicit boundary options, reject lateral sponge widths that leave no undamped
interior in an active direction.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 ! Local Variables
+ logical :: x_left_relax,x_right_relax,y_bot_relax,y_top_relax
@@
 if(ibc_top.eq.7825) ibc_top = ibcy
 if(ibc_bot.eq.7825) ibc_bot = ibcy
 if(ibc_left.eq.7825) ibc_left = ibcx
 if(ibc_right.eq.7825) ibc_right = ibcx
+
+ x_left_relax=(ibc_left.ge.1.and.ibc_left.lt.5)
+ x_right_relax=(ibc_right.ge.1.and.ibc_right.lt.5)
+ y_bot_relax=(ibc_bot.ge.1.and.ibc_bot.lt.5)
+ y_top_relax=(ibc_top.ge.1.and.ibc_top.lt.5)
+ if((x_left_relax.or.x_right_relax).and.nr.ge.n) then
+ print*,’INVALID RELAXATION WIDTH: nr must be smaller than n’
+ STOP
+ endif
+ if((y_bot_relax.or.y_top_relax).and.nr.ge.m) then
+ print*,’INVALID RELAXATION WIDTH: nr must be smaller than m’
+ STOP
+ endif
+ if(x_left_relax.and.x_right_relax.and.2*nr.ge.n) then
+ print*,’INVALID RELAXATION WIDTH: left/right sponge regions cover the x domain’
+ STOP
+ endif
+ if(y_bot_relax.and.y_top_relax.and.2*nr.ge.m) then
+ print*,’INVALID RELAXATION WIDTH: bottom/top sponge regions cover the y domain’
+ STOP
+ endif

 if(ibc_top.eq.0.and.ibc_bot.ne.0) then

If full-domain nudging is ever desired, it should be a separate named option rather than an accidental
consequence of an over-wide lateral boundary buffer.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs); a8b1c58 (2026-08-17,
tinit/topo/variables bug-list pass).
The relaxation-width inputs were covered by the validation pass and by the later tinit cleanup so
over-wide or invalid sponge settings are caught instead of silently corrupting damping.

BUG-2026-07-044: VARIABLES-008: icfmeflag promises slice-grid
input but has no runtime consumer

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/VARIABLES-008.md

Files
• variables.F90
• input.F90

variables.F90 declares a gridlist flag for reading grid slices:

integer :: icfmeflag = 0 ! Option to read-in slices of the grid

input.F90 reads it:

call QueryGridlist_string (’outname’,outname,48)
call QueryGridlist_string (’restartfile’,restartfile,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’icfmeflag’,icfmeflag,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’ihdf’,ihdf,48)

But in the current source tree, there are no other references to icfmeflag.

Problem
icfmeflag is accepted as a configuration option, but it does not control any code path. A user can
enable the documented "read-in slices of the grid" option and the model will silently run the normal
initialization/restart path instead.
That is dangerous for workflows that expect a slice-based initialization or partial-domain input. The
run can complete using the wrong initial condition while the gridlist still suggests that slice input was
enabled.

If slice-grid input is not supported in this branch, reject nonzero values during input parsing:

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 call QueryGridlist_string (’outname’,outname,48)
 call QueryGridlist_string (’restartfile’,restartfile,48)
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’icfmeflag’,icfmeflag,48)
+ if(icfmeflag.ne.0)then
+ print*,’ERROR: icfmeflag is configured, but slice-grid input is not implemented in this tree’
+ STOP

 385

+ endif
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’ihdf’,ihdf,48)

If slice input is intended, replace the guard with a real branch that initializes the grid from the slice
files and documents how it interacts with irst, restartfile, topofile, and MPI decomposition.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs).
The July validation pass added a runtime guard for this unsupported slice-grid path rather than
implementing a full consumer for icfmeflag.

BUG-2026-07-045: VARIABLES-009: isensor > 1 reads sensor input
but never initializes or writes sensors

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/VARIABLES-009.md

Files
• variables.F90
• input.F90
• rinit.F90
• compress.F90
• Sensors/input_sense.F90

variables.F90 defines the sensor switch as a generic integer:

integer :: isensor = 0 ! Switch for using sensors

input.F90 treats any positive value as enabled:

call QueryGridlist_integer(’isensor’,isensor,48)
if(isensor.gt.0) call input_sensors

Sensors/input_sense.F90 then allocates and reads the sensor configuration:

call QueryGridlist_integer(’se_frq_write’,se_frq_write,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’numsensors’,numsensors,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’ncycle’,ncycle,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’locfile’,locfile,48)

allocate(se_xloc(numsensors))
allocate(se_yloc(numsensors))
allocate(se_zloc(numsensors))

But initialization and writing only run for exactly isensor == 1:

! rinit.F90
if(isensor.eq.1) call rinitSense

! compress.F90
if((isensor.eq.1).and.(mod(it,se_frq_write).eq.0))then

endif

 388

Problem
isensor = 2 or any other positive unsupported value takes the input path, so the run reads and allocates
sensor configuration. Later, the model skips rinitSense and skips sensors_write, because those guards
only accept isensor.eq.1.
That gives users a silent no-op mode: sensors look enabled during input parsing, but no sensor ownership
is initialized and no sensor data are written. If future code assumes the positive input guard means
sensor arrays are fully initialized, the inconsistent state can also become an allocation/initialization
hazard.

If only one sensor mode is supported, validate isensor immediately after reading it and keep the
downstream eq.1 guards.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 ! Sensors
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’isensor’,isensor,48)
+ if(isensor.ne.0.and.isensor.ne.1)then
+ print*,’ERROR: isensor must be 0=off or 1=enabled’
+ STOP
+ endif
 if(isensor.gt.0) call input_sensors

sensor out-of-domain stop).

checks, header handling, and per-call CSV row writing.

BUG-2026-07-046: VEGETATION-007: Fire chemistry can use the u
velocity slot as oxygen

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/VEGETATION-007.md

Files
• Vegetation/burn_veg.F90
• definearray.F90
• variables.F90
• force.F90

The xvall module initializes optional species indices to 1:

integer :: itheta=1,ika=1,ikb=1,iO2=1,iH2O=1,irho=1

xvpointers only changes iO2 if an emitted species is named O2:

if(iemissions.gt.0)then
  iEmitStart = nv+1
  if(nEmit.gt.0)then
 ...
 do i=1,nEmit
 if(spEmit(i).eq.’O2’) iO2 = iEmitStart-1+i
 if(spEmit(i).eq.’H2O’) iH2O = iEmitStart-1+i
 enddo
  endif
endif
...
iuvel = 1

burnFuel always uses iO2 when ifire.eq.1:

hydroFactor=exp(-rno/rnfuel*psif* &
  xvfuel(ift,i,j,k,irhof)/xv(i,j,k,iO2))
slambdaof=sum(xvfuel(:,i,j,k,irhof))*xv(i,j,k,iO2) &
  /(sum(xvfuel(:,i,j,k,irhof))/rnfuel+xv(i,j,k,iO2)/rno)**2
...
force_xv(i,j,k,iO2)=force_xv(i,j,k,iO2)-ff*rno

The fire path is enabled independently of emissions:

if(ifire.eq.1)then
  call evapPDF(...)
  call burnFuel(...)
endif

 392

Problem
ifire defaults to enabled, while iemissions defaults to disabled. In that common configuration, iO2
remains 1, which is also the u velocity/momentum slot.
burnFuel then treats the u field as oxygen density. Depending on wind sign and magnitude, this can
produce negative oxygen, division by zero, exp overflow, or an oxygen sink applied to velocity instead
of a species tracer.
The water-vapor paths try to avoid this sentinel with if(iH2O.ne.1), but the fire chemistry has no
equivalent guard for iO2.

Fail fast when fire is enabled without a real O2 transported species. A broader fix should change
optional indices to a 0 sentinel, but this local guard prevents silent velocity-as-oxygen chemistry.

BUG-2026-07-047: VEGETATION-009: Invalid ifuel leaves psif
undefined

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/VEGETATION-009.md

Files
• Vegetation/burn_veg.F90
• Vegetation/input_veg.F90
• Vegetation/variables_veg.F90

ifuel is user-configurable:

integer :: ifuel = 1 ! Option for burning fuel pdf choice
...
call QueryGridlist_integer(’ifuel’,ifuel,48)

burnFuel calls computePsif and immediately uses the result:

call computePsif(psif,temps(ift,i,j,k))
...
ff=cf*xvfuel(ift,i,j,k,irhof)*xv(i,j,k,iO2)*sigmac*psif* &
  slambdaof/(100.0_wp*sizescale(ift,i,j,k)**2.0_wp)

computePsif assigns psif only for ifuel values 1, 2, or 3:

if(ifuel.eq.1)then
  ...
  psif=...
elseif(ifuel.eq.2)then
  ...
  psif = c1*(c3+er)
elseif(ifuel.eq.3)then
  ...
  psif = 1.0_wp
endif

Problem
If a gridlist sets ifuel to any value other than 1, 2, or 3, computePsif returns without assigning psif.
That leaves burnFuel using an undefined local value in the fuel reaction rate. Depending on compil-
er/runtime state, the burn rate can be random, negative, enormous, or NaN. Because this is inside the
innermost burn loop, one bad option can poison the whole simulation quickly.

 396

The minimal fix is to reject unsupported ifuel values during vegetation input processing so the bad
option never reaches the burn loop.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Vegetation/input_veg.F90
@@
 endif
 if(idiffsies.eq.1.and.ifire.ne.1)then
 print*,’ERROR: idiffsies=1 requires ifire=1’
 STOP
 endif
 call QueryGridlist_variable(’ifuel’,ifuel,48)
+ if(ifuel.lt.1.or.ifuel.gt.3)then
+ print*,’ERROR: ifuel must be 1, 2, or 3; received ’,ifuel
+ STOP
+ endif
 call QueryGridlist_variable(’ignfile’,ignfile,48)

This catches the bad option at setup time instead of letting burn_veg encounter an undefined psif. A
defense-in-depth guard in computePsif is still reasonable, but it is no longer the primary fix.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs); 798df8b (2026-08-18,
vegetation bug-list pass); 27c7afa (2026-08-17, subgrid turbulence and thermodynamics bug-list pass).

BUG-2026-07-048: VEGETATION-013: Ignition file coordinates are
never bounds-checked before indexing fuel arrays

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/VEGETATION-013.md

Files
• Vegetation/rinit_veg.F90
• Vegetation/ignite_veg.F90

rinitVeg reads ignition locations directly from the ignition file:

do i=1,nIgn
  read(1000,*) ignLocation(i,1),ignLocation(i,2),ignLocation(i,3), &
 ignTime(i)
enddo

ignite later converts the global x/y coordinates to local indices and uses the z coordinate directly as k:

if(time.ge.ignTime(iign).and. &
  time.le.ignTime(iign)+(targetTemp-tambient)/rampRate.and. &
  npos.eq.(ignLocation(iign,1)-1)/np+1.and. &
  mpos.eq.(ignLocation(iign,2)-1)/mp+1)then
  i=mod(ignLocation(iign,1)-1,np)+1
  j=mod(ignLocation(iign,2)-1,mp)+1
  k=ignLocation(iign,3)
  do ift=1,nfuel
 temps(ift,i,j,k)=max(temps(ift,i,j,k), &
 min((time-ignTime(iign))*rampRate+tambient,targetTemp))

Problem
Ignition coordinates are treated as trusted input. A typo in the ignition file can create out-of-bounds
fuel-array accesses:

• ignLocation(:,3) < 1 or > lfuel is assigned directly to k and then used to index temps, xvfuel, and
  force_sies.
• ignLocation(:,1) <= 0 or ignLocation(:,2) <= 0 can produce invalid owner-rank tests and local mod
  results. For example, a global x coordinate of 0 gives mod(-1,np)+1, which can be 0 with Fortran’s
  sign-of-dividend mod.
• ignLocation(:,1) > n or ignLocation(:,2) > m is silently ignored if no MPI rank owns it, making a
  bad ignition look like a valid but ineffective case.

This failure mode is distinct from empty schedules or invalid rampRate: even with a valid namelist and
positive ramp rate, one bad coordinate can crash the run or silently suppress ignition.

 400

Validate each ignition entry while reading the file, before the values reach ignite.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Vegetation/rinit_veg.F90
@@
 do i=1,nIgn
 read(1000,*) ignLocation(i,1),ignLocation(i,2),ignLocation(i,3), &
 ignTime(i)
+ if(ignLocation(i,1).lt.1.or.ignLocation(i,1).gt.n.or. &
+ ignLocation(i,2).lt.1.or.ignLocation(i,2).gt.m.or. &
+ ignLocation(i,3).lt.1.or.ignLocation(i,3).gt.lfuel)then
+ print*,’ERROR: ignition location out of bounds in ’,trim(ignfile)
+ print*,’Entry ’,i,’ location = ’,ignLocation(i,1), &
+ ignLocation(i,2),ignLocation(i,3)
+        print*,’Valid ranges: x=1..’,n,’ y=1..’,m,’ z=1..’,lfuel
+ STOP
+ endif
 enddo

ignite can also defensively skip or stop on invalid entries, but setup-time validation gives the user a
clear input-file diagnostic before the time loop begins.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs); 798df8b (2026-08-18,
vegetation bug-list pass); 27c7afa (2026-08-17, subgrid turbulence and thermodynamics bug-list pass).

BUG-2026-07-050: VEGETATION-021: Negative moisture ratios
initialize negative water density

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/VEGETATION-021.md

Files
• Vegetation/rinit_veg.F90

! Vegetation/rinit_veg.F90
call readLegacyVegArray(rmoist(ift,:,:,:),94,lfuel)
...
xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof)=rrhof
xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhow)=rmoist*xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof)
xvfuel(:,:,:,:,itemp)=temps
...
xvfuelLim(1,irhow)=0.0_wp
xvfuelLim(2,irhow)=1.e30_wp

Problem
The initial water density is computed directly from treesmoist.dat, but the lower limit for irhow is only
assigned after initialization. There is no validation or clipping of the initial rmoist values.
If a vegetation moisture file contains a negative moisture ratio, rhoWater is initialized negative. That
can corrupt several later calculations, including vegetation heat capacity, latent heating, drag layer
mass, solar heating, and ignition tests. The existing limiter may protect future tendency updates, but
it does not guarantee that the initial state entering the physics is valid.

BUG-2026-07-051: VEGETATION-023: Nonpositive vegetation
material constants are accepted and used as divisors

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/VEGETATION-023.md

Files
• Vegetation/input_veg.F90
• Vegetation/variables_veg.F90
• Vegetation/drag_veg.F90
• Vegetation/convection_veg.F90
• Vegetation/solarHeat_veg.F90

! Vegetation/input_veg.F90
call QueryGridlist_real (’rhoMicro’,rhoMicro,48)
call QueryGridlist_real (’cpwood’,cpwood,48)

! Vegetation/drag_veg.F90
av=2.0_wp/pi/sizeScale(ift,i,j,k)* &
  xvfuel(ift,i,j,k,irhof)/rhoMicro

! Vegetation/convection_veg.F90
av=2.0_wp*(xvfuel(ift,i,j,k,irhof)/rhoMicro)/sizeScale(ift,i,j,k)

! Vegetation/solarHeat_veg.F90
LAIlocal(i,j,k)=sum(rhoFuel(:,i,j,k)/sizeScale(:,i,j,k) &
  *(zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j))/rhoMicro)
...
av=2.0_wp*(rhoFuel(it,i,j,k)/rhoMicro)/sizeScale(it,i,j,k)

Problem
rhoMicro and cpwood are read directly from the gridlist without validation. rhoMicro is used as a divisor
in the vegetation projected-area and LAI calculations. If it is zero, the run can produce infinities or
trap on division by zero. If it is negative, the projected area and LAI become negative, reversing drag,
heat-transfer, and solar-heating terms.
cpwood is a heat capacity used to initialize and force the solid internal energy. A zero or negative heat
capacity gives nonphysical solid energy, ignition forcing, and burn heat-loss terms.
Because both values are core material constants, the input path should reject nonpositive values before
any vegetation arrays are initialized.

 412

BUG-2026-07-052: VEGETATION-025: Vegetation feature switches
accept invalid values that silently change physics

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/VEGETATION-025.md

Files
• Vegetation/input_veg.F90
• definearray.F90
• force.F90

! Vegetation/input_veg.F90
call QueryGridlist_integer(’ifire’,ifire,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’imoist’,imoist,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’inonlocal’,inonlocal,48)
call QueryGridlist_integer(’idiffsies’,idiffsies,48)

! definearray.F90
if(inonlocal.eq.1)then
  nv = nv+1
  imixfrac = nv
endif
...
if(imoist.eq.1.or.ifire.eq.1.or.irad.gt.0)then
  isies = nvfuel+1
  nvfuel = nvfuel+1
endif

! force.F90
if(idiffsies.eq.1) call diffusesies(...)
...
if(imoist.eq.1)then
  call solarHeating(...)
  call evapBulk(...)
endif
if(ifire.eq.1)then
  call evapPDF(...)
  call burnFuel(...)
endif

Problem
The vegetation feature switches are treated as binary flags by the rest of the code, but input_vegetation
accepts any integer value. A typo such as ifire = 2 does not fail; it silently behaves like fire is off
because the code only checks ifire.eq.1. The same pattern applies to imoist, inonlocal, and idiffsies.

 416

This is a dangerous configuration failure because it can change the model state layout and physics
ownership without any diagnostic:

• ifire = 2 skips ignition, evapPDF, and burnFuel.
• imoist = 2 skips solar moisture and bulk evaporation.
• inonlocal = 2 skips allocation of the mix-fraction field.
• idiffsies = 2 skips creeping-fire diffusion.

Invalid values should be rejected as soon as they are read.

diff --git a/Vegetation/input_veg.F90 b/Vegetation/input_veg.F90

 call QueryGridlist_string (’ignfile’,ignfile,48)
+

Problem
is, ie, js, and je are read from the gridlist and documented as windfield subdomain controls, but no
windfield writer, reader, or application path uses them. The writer always saves strips on the global
domain boundary, and xevariation applies data only at the global boundary strips.
That makes non-default subdomain input silently ineffective. A user can request a subdomain windfield
and still get full-domain edge files and full-domain boundary application.

 420

Either implement true subdomain windfield files, or fail fast when non-default subdomain bounds are
requested. The minimal safe fix is to reject unsupported bounds instead of silently ignoring them.

BUG-2026-07-054: XEVARIATION-016: Overlapping Windfield
Boundary Strips Leave Part Of The Output Buffer Unfilled

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/XEVARIATION-016.md

Files
• xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90
• xeVariation/windfield.F90

! xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90
26 call QueryGridlist_integer(’ibcells’,ibcells,48)
27 call QueryGridlist_integer(’jbcells’,jbcells,48)

! xeVariation/windfield.F90
 51 allocate(outdatai(ibcells*2,m,l,nv),outdataj(n,jbcells*2,l,nv))
...
 60 if(ia.le.ibcells)then
 61              outdatai(ia,ja,:,:)=tmparray(i,j,:,:,iproc)
 62 elseif(ia.gt.n-ibcells)then
 63 ii=2*ibcells-n+ia
 64              outdatai(ii,ja,:,:)=tmparray(i,j,:,:,iproc)
 65 endif

! xeVariation/windfield.F90
 66 if(ja.le.jbcells)then
 67              outdataj(ia,ja,:,:)=tmparray(i,j,:,:,iproc)
 68 elseif(ja.gt.m-jbcells)then
 69 jj=2*jbcells-m+ja
 70              outdataj(ia,jj,:,:)=tmparray(i,j,:,:,iproc)
 71 endif

Problem
The writer allocates separate left/right and bottom/top slots, each with 2*ibcells or 2*jbcells entries.
But if 2*ibcells > n or 2*jbcells > m, the two global boundary strips overlap.
For overlapping cells, the elseif means the left or bottom branch wins and the right or top slot is not
filled. Later, write(21) outdatai,outdataj writes those uninitialized buffer entries. A read-in run can
then apply uninitialized boundary data on the opposite side.
This is distinct from the local-subdomain limit: even a single-process run can set ibcells <= np but
still have 2*ibcells > n.

 424

Reject overlapping strip widths unless the file format is changed to handle overlap explicitly.

diff --git a/xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90 b/xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90
--- a/xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90
+++ b/xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90
@@
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’ibcells’,ibcells,48)
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’jbcells’,jbcells,48)
+ if(2*ibcells.gt.n.or.2*jbcells.gt.m)then
+ print*,’ERROR: windfield boundary strips overlap; reduce ibcells/jbcells’
+ STOP
+ endif
@@
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’ibcells’,ibcells,48)
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’jbcells’,jbcells,48)
+ if(2*ibcells.gt.n.or.2*jbcells.gt.m)then
+ print*,’ERROR: windfield boundary strips overlap; reduce ibcells/jbcells’
+ STOP
+ endif

BUG-2026-07-056: Top Absorption Layer Disabled by Invalid zab

Source report: aa-Jul8_completed/aa-easy_BOUND_1.md

Files
• tinit.F90
• variables.F90
• input.F90
• rinit.F90

Issue
The default top absorption-layer start height is:

real(prec) :: zab = 400.0_prec

For a run with l = 220 and dz = 1, the domain top is computed as:

zb = zedge(l+1)

which gives zb = 220 m. Because zab = 400 m is above the model top, this condition in tinit.F90 is never
true:

As a result, the vertical/top absorption layer is never applied. This leaves the model without the
intended top damping unless the user explicitly overrides zab to a value below zb in the gridlist.

Impact
With zab >= zb, the run silently proceeds with no active top absorber. This can allow vertically
propagating disturbances to reflect from the top boundary instead of being attenuated, which may
contribute to instability or boundary-driven oscillations.

Recommended Fix
Do not silently continue when the requested damping layer starts outside the domain. Kill the program
with a clear error message so the user must set a valid zab.

+++ b/CODE-dev/tinit.F90
@@ -75,6 +75,14 @@
 ! ... existing initialization code ...

+ if (zab .ge. zb) then

 432

+ write(*,*) ’WARNING: top absorption layer is inactive.’
+ write(*,*) ’ zab is at or above the model top.’
+        write(*,*) ’         zab = ’, zab, ’ zb = ’, zb
+ write(*,*) ’ No vertical/top damping will be applied.’
+ write(*,*) ’ To enable it, set zab < zb in the gridlist.’
+ endif
+
 do k=1,l
 do j=0,n
 do i=0,m

Notes
This is a configuration-validation bug rather than a formula bug. When zab > zb, the damping formulas
are not reached at all because the guard condition prevents entry. The failure mode is therefore silent
deactivation of the top absorber.

The tinit cleanup validates unsupported absorber modes and corrects the top-absorption formula so
invalid zab settings no longer silently disable the intended layer.

Problem
The documented valid values are 0, 1-4, and 5, but no input validation enforces that. A bad positive
value, for example ibc_left = 6, is treated as a physical edge by msga.F90, ignored by relaxation setup
in tinit.F90, treated as Neumann by the flow halo updater, treated as neither cyclic nor mirror by
radiation and solar ray tracing, and treated as absorbing/removal by firebrands. That means different
physics modules silently apply different boundary semantics for the same invalid input.

physics initialization. Fail fast if any value is outside ,1,2,3,4,50,1,2,3,4,5.

BUG-2026-07-058: Ground boundary loop writes past the xvrho
variable dimension

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/001_xvrho_ground_bc_nv_out_of_bounds.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/domainUpdates
 ,→ .F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/definearray.
 ,→ F90

definearray.F90 allocates xvrho without the density slot:

allocate(xvrho(1-ih:np+ih,1-ih:mp+ih,0:l,nv-1))

domainUpdates.F90 fills the interior with the correct upper bound:

do kv=1,nv-1
  xvrho(:,:,1:l,kv)=xv(:,:,:,kv)/xv(:,:,:,irho)
enddo

But the bottom-boundary loop iterates through nv:

do kv=1,nv
  xvrho(i,j,0,kv)=getSubGroundValue(xvrho(i,j,k,kv), &
    xvrho(i-1,j,k,kv),xvrho(i+1,j,k,kv),xvrho(i,j-1,k,kv), &
    xvrho(i,j+1,k,kv),g13,g23,g33)
enddo

Problem
xvrho is dimensioned as nv-1 because the density component irho == nv is not stored as xv/rho. The
ground-boundary loop writes xvrho(i,j,0,nv), which is one element beyond the allocated fourth dimen-
sion.
With bounds checking, this should fail immediately. Without bounds checking, it can corrupt adjacent
memory during every call to explicit_domain_updates.

+++ b/CODE-dev/domainUpdates.F90
@@
-      do kv=1,nv
+      do kv=1,nv-1
 xvrho(i,j,0,kv)=getSubGroundValue(xvrho(i,j,k,kv), &

 enddo

cleanup avoids writing past the variable dimension through mismatched array sections.

BUG-2026-07-059: Windfield boundary writer leaves output files
open

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/01_windfield_writer_leaves_boundary_file_open.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ windfield.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ xevariation.F90

windfld_write opens a boundary-data file on unit 21, writes the gathered x/y boundary strips, and then
deallocates the buffers:

  allocate(outdatai(ibcells*2,m,l,nv),outdataj(n,jbcells*2,l,nv))
  open(unit=21,file=fname,form=’unformatted’,status=’unknown’)
  ...
  write(21) outdatai,outdataj
  deallocate(outdatai,outdataj)
endif

The corresponding reader expects complete files:

open(41,file=fname,form=’unformatted’,status=’old’)
read(41) indatai,indataj
close(41)

Problem
The writer never closes unit 21. On repeated windfield output, the next open uses the same unit for a
new file while the previous connection may still be active. Depending on compiler/runtime behavior,
that can fail, silently reconnect, or leave data buffered longer than expected.
That is risky for windfield replay because the fire run immediately reads these files as boundary forcing.
Diagonal windfield input depends on both x-side and y-side boundary strips; a stale or incomplete
boundary file can make the replay look directionally broken even when the stored wind-run state was
correct.
Using status=’unknown’ also makes accidental reuse of an existing filename harder to detect. These files
are timestep snapshots, so replacing the target file is safer.

Open boundary snapshots for writing as replacements and close the unit immediately after the write
succeeds.

 443

diff --git a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/windfield.F90 b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ windfield.F90

- open(unit=21,file=fname,form=’unformatted’,status=’unknown’)
+ open(unit=21,file=fname,form=’unformatted’,status=’replace’, &
+ action=’write’)
@@
 write(21) outdatai,outdataj
+    close(21)
 deallocate(outdatai,outdataj)
 endif

For more defensive I/O, add iostat= checks around the open, write, and close calls and stop with the
filename if any operation fails.

writing.

• write only a wrong x strip,
• potentially index out of range,

This is directly relevant to sideways winds because any 45-degree ramped or windfield-driven wind
depends on both u and v being updated over the same physical region.

BUG-2026-07-061: EMISSIONS-001: Adding fire-required O2 drops
existing efEmit values

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-001.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
   ,→ input_ems.F90

When fire is enabled and the gridlist did not include O2, input_emissions prepends an O2 species. For
fixed emission-factor mode it resizes efEmit too:

  efEmit_tmp=efEmit
  deallocate(efEmit); allocate(efEmit(nEmit))
  efEmit(1)=0.0_wp
endif

Problem
The old emission factors are copied into efEmit_tmp, but they are never copied back into the resized
efEmit.
After this block runs, only efEmit(1) is initialized. efEmit(2:nEmit) contains undefined values, so efSource
can emit arbitrary gas masses for every user-specified species whenever ifire=1, iemissions=2, and O2
was not already listed in Species.

Copy the saved factors back after inserting O2, then release the temporary array.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Emissions/input_ems.F90
@@

 efEmit_tmp=efEmit
 deallocate(efEmit); allocate(efEmit(nEmit))
       efEmit(1)=0.0_wp
+ efEmit(2:nEmit)=efEmit_tmp(:)
+ deallocate(efEmit_tmp)
 endif
 endif

BUG-2026-07-062: EMISSIONS-003: Point sources use the lower
vertical edge to choose a cell

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-003.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ pointSource_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Firebrands/
   ,→ evolve_fb.F90

zedge(1) is initialized to ground level and zedge(k+1) is the top of cell k:

do k=1,l+1
  zedge(k)=(k-1)*dz
enddo

The firebrand code finds the containing vertical cell using the upper edge:

do k=1,lls
  if(zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j).gt.xvbrand(it,iz)) exit
enddo

pointSource instead checks the lower edge:

do k=1,lls
  if(zcart(zedge(k),i,j).gt.emitPointLocation(iemit,3)) exit
enddo
...
emitForcing(i,j,k,isp)=emitForcing(i,j,k,isp)+ &
  emitPointRate(iemit)/(dx*dy* &
  (zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j)))

The aerosol branch has the same pattern:

do k=1,lls
  if(zcart(zedge(k),i,j).gt.aeroPointLocation(iemit,3)) exit
enddo

Problem
For a point inside cell 1, zcart(zedge(1),i,j) is the ground and is not greater than the source height, so
the loop advances to k=2. The source is placed one cell too high.
For a point in the top cell, no lower edge is greater than the source height. The loop can finish normally
with k=lls+1, after which the code indexes emitForcing(i,j,k,...) and zedge(k+1) out of bounds.

 452

Use the top edge of each cell and skip points above the local vertical domain.

BUG-2026-07-063: EMISSIONS-004: Point-source horizontal
mapping rounds into the wrong cell or MPI rank

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-004.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ pointSource_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Firebrands/
   ,→ evolve_fb.F90

pointSource maps physical coordinates to processor position and local cell index with nint:

if(npos.eq.nint(emitPointLocation(iemit,1)/dx/np)+1.and. &
 mpos.eq.nint(emitPointLocation(iemit,2)/dy/mp)+1)then
  i=mod(nint(emitPointLocation(iemit,1)/dx),np)+1
  j=mod(nint(emitPointLocation(iemit,2)/dy),mp)+1

The aerosol branch does the same:

if(npos.eq.nint(aeroPointLocation(iemit,1)/dx/np)+1.and. &
 mpos.eq.nint(aeroPointLocation(iemit,2)/dy/mp)+1)then
  i=mod(nint(aeroPointLocation(iemit,1)/dx),np)+1
  j=mod(nint(aeroPointLocation(iemit,2)/dy),mp)+1

Other particle-like code uses floor for physical coordinates:

i=floor(xvbrand(it,ix)/dx)-(npos-1)*np+1
j=floor(xvbrand(it,iy)/dy)-(mpos-1)*mp+1

Problem
nint rounds to the nearest integer, not the containing grid cell. A source at 0.6*dx maps to cell 2
instead of cell 1, and a source just past half a processor block can be assigned to the next MPI rank.
That can put point emissions in the wrong cell, or skip them entirely because the wrong rank passes
the npos/mpos test.

Compute global integer cell positions with floor, then derive the owning rank and local index from
those integer positions.

BUG-2026-07-064: EMISSIONS-006: LagrangeInterp overwrites each
interpolation term

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-006.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ variables_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ deposit_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ stokesDrag_ems.F90

LagrangeInterp initializes the result to zero and loops over all basis terms:

LagrangeInterp=0.0_wp
do i=1,n
  iw=1
  do j=1,n
    if(i.ne.j) iw=iw*(p-j)/(i-j)
  enddo
  LagrangeInterp=log10(array(i))*iw
enddo
LagrangeInterp=10**LagrangeInterp

It is used by aerosol deposition and settling:

iM=LagrangeInterp(nMAero,r-1.0_wp/2.0_wp, &
  xvAero(i,j,k,nMAero*(it-1)+1:nMAero*it))

iM=LagrangeInterp(nMAero,r+2.0_wp/3.0_wp, &
  xvAero(i,j,k,nMAero*(it-1)+1:nMAero*it))

Problem
The loop assignment replaces the accumulated interpolation value on every iteration. The returned
value only contains the final basis contribution, not the sum of all Lagrange basis terms.
For nMAero=2, for example, the first moment has no effect on the returned interpolated value except
through the final exponentiation path. Aerosol deposition and settling rates are therefore computed
from the wrong moment interpolation.

Accumulate each basis contribution.

 460

+++ b/CODE-dev/Emissions/variables_ems.F90
@@
 do i=1,n
 iw=1
 do j=1,n
         if(i.ne.j) iw=iw*(p-j)/(i-j)
 enddo
- LagrangeInterp=log10(array(i))*iw
+ LagrangeInterp=LagrangeInterp+log10(array(i))*iw
 enddo
 LagrangeInterp=10**LagrangeInterp

BUG-2026-07-065: EMISSIONS-007: Aerosol routines declare
module function LagrangeInterp as external

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-007.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ variables_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ deposit_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ stokesDrag_ems.F90

LagrangeInterp is a module procedure inside emission_general_variables:

module emission_general_variables
  ...
  contains

  real(wp) function LagrangeInterp(n,p,array)

But the aerosol routines call it as an external procedure:

real(wp),external :: LagrangeInterp,zcart

stokesDrag imports only rhoAero from the module:

use emission_general_variables, only : rhoAero

Problem
A module procedure is not the same linker symbol as a standalone external function. Declaring
LagrangeInterp as external makes these routines call an external symbol such as lagrangeinterp_, while
the actual function is emitted as the module procedure symbol for emission_general_variables.
If deposit or stokesDrag is linked into an executable path, this can fail at link time with an unresolved
LagrangeInterp symbol. It also hides the explicit interface that the module procedure would provide.

Use-associate LagrangeInterp from emission_general_variables and leave only zcart as external.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Emissions/deposit_ems.F90

BUG-2026-07-066: EMISSIONS-008: Stokes ground deposition
divides by zero at the ground edge

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-008.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ stokesDrag_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/metric.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90

zedge(1) is initialized to zero:

do k=1,l+1
  zedge(k)=(k-1)*dz
enddo

zcart maps sigmax=0 to zs(i,j):

gdeform=aa3*sigmax**3+aa2*sigmax**2+aa1*sigmax
z=gdeform*(zb-zs(i,j))/zb+zs(i,j)

The Stokes ground-deposition term divides by the distance from zedge(1) to zs:

forcingAero(i,j,1,nMAero*(it-1)+r)= &
  forcingAero(i,j,1,nMAero*(it-1)+r)+w_set* &
  ((iMp-iM)/(zcart(zedge(2),i,j)-zcart(zedge(1),i,j))- &
    iM/(zcart(zedge(1),i,j)-zs(i,j)))

Problem
zcart(zedge(1),i,j) is exactly zs(i,j), so the denominator in the lower-boundary term is zero for every
terrain point.
Any call to stokesDrag with aerosols active can therefore create infinities or NaNs in forcingAero at the
first vertical level.

Use a positive distance from the first cell center to the ground. The grid already stores cell centers in
z, so import it and use zcart(z(1),i,j)-zs(i,j).

diff --git a/CODE-dev/Emissions/stokesDrag_ems.F90 b/CODE-dev/Emissions/stokesDrag_ems.F90

- use metric_variables, only : zedge,zs
+ use metric_variables, only : zedge,zs,z

 467

@@

 forcingAero(i,j,1,nMAero*(it-1)+r)+w_set* &
              ((iMp-iM)/(zcart(zedge(2),i,j)-zcart(zedge(1),i,j))- &
-               iM/(zcart(zedge(1),i,j)-zs(i,j)))
