BUG-2026-07-067: EMISSIONS-011: Aerosol deposition and settling
routines are never called

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-011.md

The Emissions library contains aerosol sink routines:

 il,iu,jl,ju,lls,nfuel)

subroutine stokesDrag(forcingAero,xvAero,Temp,rho,il,iu,jl,ju,lls)

But the only emission calls in small_implicit_forcings are source terms:

select case (iemissions)
  case (1)
 call pointSource(forceSI_xv(:,:,:,iEmitStart:iEmitStop), &
 1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,nEmit,nAero,nMAero)

Problem
Aerosol deposition onto vegetation/ground and Stokes settling are implemented but unreachable. Any
run that enables aerosol emissions transports the aerosol moments without these sink terms, so aerosol
residence time and near-ground loading can be substantially wrong.

in those routines may stay hidden because the main force path never exercises them.

 470

exact time integration choice is model-dependent, but the current force location suggests adding them
to small_implicit_forcings after source terms.

BUG-2026-07-068: EMISSIONS-012: LagrangeInterp takes log10 of
zero aerosol moments

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-012.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ variables_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ deposit_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/
 ,→ stokesDrag_ems.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/definearray.
 ,→ F90

Transported fields are initialized to zero:

allocate(xe(1-ih:np+ih,1-ih:mp+ih,l,nv)); xe=0.0_wp
allocate(xv(1-ih:np+ih,1-ih:mp+ih,l,nv)); xv=0.0_wp

rinitEmission initializes ambient gas species, but it does not initialize aerosol moments. A clean aerosol
field therefore starts at zero.
LagrangeInterp interpolates in log space:

LagrangeInterp=0.0_wp
do i=1,n
  iw=1
  do j=1,n
    if(i.ne.j) iw=iw*(p-j)/(i-j)
  enddo
  LagrangeInterp=log10(array(i))*iw
enddo
LagrangeInterp=10**LagrangeInterp

The aerosol sink routines call it directly on transported aerosol moments:

iM=LagrangeInterp(nMAero,r-1.0_wp/2.0_wp, &
  xvAero(i,j,k,nMAero*(it-1)+1:nMAero*it))

Problem
log10(0.0_wp) is undefined.  If deposition or settling is enabled in a cell with no aerosol mass yet,
LagrangeInterp can produce Inf, -Inf, or NaN depending on the interpolation weights. That bad value is
then multiplied into forcingAero.
This is independent of the separate accumulation bug in LagrangeInterp: even after accumulating all
basis terms correctly, the routine still needs a nonpositive-moment guard before taking logarithms.

 474

Treat a nonpositive moment vector as no valid aerosol distribution for log interpolation. The conservative
fix is to return zero before taking any logarithms.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Emissions/variables_ems.F90
@@
 integer :: i,j

 LagrangeInterp=0.0_wp
+ if(any(array.le.0.0_wp)) return
+
 do i=1,n
 iw=1
 do j=1,n
         if(i.ne.j) iw=iw*(p-j)/(i-j)
 enddo
- LagrangeInterp=log10(array(i))*iw
+ LagrangeInterp=LagrangeInterp+log10(array(i))*iw
 enddo
 LagrangeInterp=10**LagrangeInterp

If mixed positive/nonpositive moment vectors should be recoverable, replace the early return with a
model-specific floor and diagnostics. The important part is that zero aerosol concentration must not
enter log10.

BUG-2026-07-069: EMISSIONS-021: Explicit O2 gets the default

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/EMISSIONS-021.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Emissions/

Fixed emission-factor mode initializes every gas emission factor to the CO2-like default:

  allocate(efEmit(nEmit)); efEmit(:)=1.6_wp ! kg/kg (Initializing all values as CO2)
  call QueryGridlist_real_array(’efEmit’,efEmit,nEmit,48)

If fire is enabled and O2 was omitted from Species, the code prepends O2 and assigns it a zero emission
factor:

  ...

explicitly includes O2 in Species, efEmit starts at 1.6 for that O2 slot unless the gridlist also provides an

burnFuel is already consuming it. The missing-O2 branch shows the intended default for O2 is zero;
explicit O2 should get the same safe default.

BUG-2026-07-070: INPUT-003: input_firebrands is called with an
argument even though it accepts none

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/INPUT-003.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/input.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Firebrands/

input.F90 passes ifbrand to the firebrand input routine:

  ! Firebrands
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’ifbrand’,ifbrand,48)
  if(ifbrand.eq.1) call input_firebrands(ifbrand)

The callee has no dummy arguments:

subroutine input_firebrands
  use firebrand_gridlist_variables

  ...
end subroutine input_firebrands

Problem
The call signature and subroutine definition disagree. Because these are external subroutines without
an explicit interface, some compilers may accept this and the callee may simply ignore the extra ABI
argument. That is still nonconforming Fortran and can become a hard compile-time error as soon as
an explicit interface is introduced, stricter checks are enabled, or the routine is moved into a module.
The argument is also unused: the only supported firebrand mode in input.F90 is ifbrand.eq.1, and the
firebrand input values are stored in firebrand_gridlist_variables.

Remove the stray argument from the call.

+++ b/CODE-dev/input.F90
@@
 ! Firebrands
 call QueryGridlist_integer(’ifbrand’,ifbrand,48)
- if(ifbrand.eq.1) call input_firebrands(ifbrand)
+ if(ifbrand.eq.1) call input_firebrands

 482

Longer term, these input routines should live in modules or have explicit interface blocks so argument
mismatches are caught by the compiler.

Git evidence: 6e02566 (2026-07-09, validation crutches to reduce bad runs); 2bdf01f (2026-07-14,
no-fire segfault cleanup).

 ...

  endif

The emission-factor source later uses efEmit(isp) for every emitted species:

force_xv(i,j,k,isp)=force_xv(i,j,k,isp) &

 485

 +fuelConsumed(ift,i,j,k)*efEmit(isp)

 efEmit_tmp=efEmit

This keeps the emission factors aligned with the species array after O2 is inserted.

BUG-2026-07-072: METRIC-003: Time-varying power-law winds use
the terrain height from cell (1,1) everywhere

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/METRIC-003.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/metric.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation
 ,→ /xevariation.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90

zcart maps model height to physical height using the terrain height at the supplied horizontal cell:

function zcart(sigmax,i,j) result(z)
  ...
  z=gdeform*(zb-zs(i,j))/zb+zs(i,j)
end function zcart

The initial canopy-aware velocity profile uses local height above ground:

zk=zcart(z(k),i,j)-zs(i,j)
if(zk.ge.hmaxt)then
  uprofile(i,j,k)=c1/0.41_wp*log((zk/hmaxt+c2-1)/c3)
...

But the time-varying power-law ramp in xevariation uses zcart(z(k),1,1) for every i,j cell:

xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=min(uramp*xe(i,j,k,irho), &
  (time*uramp/uramptime+u0)*xe(i,j,k,irho)) &
  *max(0.0_wp,(1.0_wp-1.5_wp*sum(xvfuel(:,i,j,k,irhof))))     &
  *(min(100.0_wp,zcart(z(k),1,1))/zu)**(1.0_wp/7.0_wp)

The same (1,1) height is used for the non-fuel levels and the v-wind ramp:

*(min(100.0_wp,zcart(z(k),1,1))/zu)**(1.0_wp/7.0_wp)

Problem
On flat terrain, zcart(z(k),1,1) is effectively just a shared height profile. On topography, it is the
physical height for the first local grid cell, including that cell’s terrain elevation. Every other cell on
the MPI rank then uses the wrong height for the power-law wind factor.
That creates two topography-specific errors:

• Wind scaling depends on the terrain at local (1,1), so the same physical cell can get a different
  ramp profile when the MPI decomposition changes.

 489

• The power-law should use local height above ground for a terrain-following grid. The current
  expression uses an absolute height at another column, which is inconsistent with initialization code
  that uses zcart(z(k),i,j)-zs(i,j).

For ixevariation=1, ramped winds over terrain can therefore be discontinuous across subdomain bound-
aries and biased over ridges or valleys.

Import zs and evaluate the power-law factor using local height above ground.

+++ b/CODE-dev/xeVariation/xevariation.F90

- use metric_variables, only : z
+ use metric_variables, only : z,zs

- real(wp) :: totw
+ real(wp) :: totw,zagl

 do i=il,iu
+              zagl=max(0.0_wp,min(100.0_wp,zcart(z(k),i,j)-zs(i,j)))
 xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=min(uramp*xe(i,j,k,irho), &
 (time*uramp/uramptime+u0)*xe(i,j,k,irho)) &
                 *max(0.0_wp,(1.0_wp-1.5_wp*sum(xvfuel(:,i,j,k,irhof)))) &
-                *(min(100.0_wp,zcart(z(k),1,1))/zu)**(1.0_wp/7.0_wp)
+                *(zagl/zu)**(1.0_wp/7.0_wp)
@@
 do i=il,iu
+              zagl=max(0.0_wp,min(100.0_wp,zcart(z(k),i,j)-zs(i,j)))
 xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=min(uramp*xe(i,j,k,irho), &
 (time*uramp/uramptime+u0)*xe(i,j,k,irho)) &
-                *(min(100.0_wp,zcart(z(k),1,1))/zu)**(1.0_wp/7.0_wp)
+                *(zagl/zu)**(1.0_wp/7.0_wp)
@@
 do i=il,iu
+              zagl=max(0.0_wp,min(100.0_wp,zcart(z(k),i,j)-zs(i,j)))

 (time*vramp/vramptime+v0)*xe(i,j,k,irho)) &
                 *max(0.0_wp,(1.0_wp-1.5_wp*sum(xvfuel(:,i,j,k,irhof)))) &

- do i=jl,ju
+ do i=il,iu

BUG-2026-07-073: MOA-003: MOA advances global time before
large explicit forcings are evaluated on the old state

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/MOA-003.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/MOA.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/compress.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/force.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/HeatSource/
 ,→ heatsource_heat.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ ignite_veg.F90

MOA advances the module-level simulation clock during its inner loop:

! MOA.F90
50 ! beginning of the inner loop
51 do its=1,nts
52 time=time+dts

But the main transported arrays xv and xvfuel are not advanced until after MOA returns and forcing
runs:

! compress.F90
61 call small_explicit_forcings ! Calculates explicit large timestep forcings
62
64 call MOA ! Mehod of Averaging for semi-implicit small timestep forcings
65
68 call large_explicit_forcings
69
70 call forcing ! Applies forcings, post-forcing effects, and advance timestep

The post-MOA large explicit forcing stage contains time-windowed sources:

! force.F90
147 if(ifire.eq.1) call ignite(forceLE_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies),xvfuel, &
...
150 if(iheatsource.ge.1) &
151 call heatSource(iheatsource, &

Those routines read the already-advanced global time while operating on old-step state:

! HeatSource/heatsource_heat.F90
116 heatsource_active = time.ge.starttime_hs(itsource) .and. &
117 time.lt.endtime_hs(itsource)

 493

! Vegetation/ignite_veg.F90
27 if(time.ge.ignTime(iign).and. &
28 time.le.ignTime(iign)+(targetTemp-tambient)/rampRate.and. &

Problem
After MOA, time represents the end of the large step, but xv and xvfuel still represent the beginning of
that large step. large_explicit_forcings therefore evaluates ignition and heat-source schedules at t + dt
while building forcings from state at t.
For time-windowed sources this shifts behavior at source boundaries:

• A heat source with starttime_hs inside the current large step can be applied to the whole step
  because time has already crossed the start time.
• A heat source with endtime_hs exactly at the end of the current large step is skipped for the whole
  step because heatSource uses time.lt.endtime_hs.
• Ignition ramp forcing uses the end-of-step target temperature while dividing by dt and applying
  that tendency over the whole step.

This creates an off-by-one-large-step error around source activation and deactivation times. It is caused
by MOA updating the global clock before the old-state large explicit forcings have been evaluated.

Keep MOA’s substep time for small-step implicit physics, but restore the large-step clock before returning.
Then advance time once after forcing has advanced xv and xvfuel. This keeps old-state large explicit
forcings evaluated at the old large-step time.

BUG-2026-07-074: VEGETATION-018: Upper canopy drag layers
omit depth weighting for each fuel type

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/VEGETATION-018.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
   ,→ drag_veg.F90

! Vegetation/drag_veg.F90
layer_ht(1) = afd(itfindex(1))
layer_ms(1) = sum((rhoWater+rhoFuel)*layer_ht(1)/afd)
...
do it=2,nfuel
  layer_ht(it)=afd(itfindex(it))-afd(itfindex(it-1))
  layer_ms(it)= &
 sum(rhoWater(itfindex(it:nfuel))+rhoFuel(itfindex(it:nfuel))) &
 *layer_ht(it)
enddo
...
u_corr=u_corr+layer_ms(it)*(0.5_wp*(uFuel(it)+uFuel(it-1))-uCorr)/mass_lad
v_corr=v_corr+layer_ms(it)*(0.5_wp*(vFuel(it)+vFuel(it-1))-vCorr)/mass_lad
w_corr=w_corr+layer_ms(it)*(0.5_wp*(wFuel(it)+wFuel(it-1))-wCorr)/mass_lad

Problem
The first canopy layer computes each fuel type’s contribution as bulk fuel-plus-water density times
layer_ht/afd. The upper layers do not apply that per-fuel depth fraction; they sum full bulk densities
for all taller fuels and multiply the total by only the current layer height.
That makes the drag correction depend on the arbitrary discretization of afd rather than the amount
of each fuel actually present in the layer. A tall, sparse fuel contributes too much mass in short upper
slices, and fuels with different depths are weighted inconsistently between layer 1 and later layers. The
resulting u_corr, v_corr, and w_corr can be biased before the momentum drag tendencies are computed.
This is independent of the sorted-index/inverse-rank bug described in VEGETATION-005; if that fix is
applied first, the same depth weighting should be used with the corrected sorted fuel list.

BUG-2026-07-075: Safety check plan for accidental irst=1

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Jul15_completed/irst_check.md

Goal
Add a restart safety check so that when irst=1 is set accidentally, FIRETEC stops early with a clear
explanation instead of failing later with a confusing substring, read, open, or restart-state error.

What I found
• irst defaults to 0 in variables.F90.
• input.F90 reads irst near the top of subroutine input, then later reads restartfile.
• compress.F90 calls input before setup_MPI, so checks inside input.F90 should not depend on mpi_rank
  or MPI_Abort.
• rinit.F90 calls irstreadio only when irst.eq.1.
• io.F90 currently assumes restartfile contains out. followed by an integer suffix:

idot=index(restartfile,’out.’)+4
iend=len_trim(restartfile)
read(restartfile(idot:iend),*) itrestart

If irst=1 is accidental and restartfile is blank, malformed, stale, or missing, this can crash in a way
that does not explain the real problem.

Plan A: Minimal early guard in input.F90
Add a validation call immediately after restartfile is read:

call QueryGridlist_variable(’restartfile’,restartfile,48)
call validate_restart_config

The new validate_restart_config subroutine would:

• reject any irst value other than 0 or 1;
• if irst.eq.1, require restartfile to be nonblank;
• require restartfile to contain out. followed by a parseable integer restart step;
• use inquire(file=trim(restartfile),exist=restart_exists) and stop if the file is missing;
• print an explanation such as:

text ERROR: irst=1 requests a restart, but restartfile is blank. Set irst=0 for a fresh run, or set
,→ restartfile to an existing output/restart file.
Pros:

• smallest change;
• crashes before array allocation or restart reads;
• fits the existing input.F90 style of print* plus STOP;
• directly catches the common accidental case.

 501

Cons:

• does not prove the restart file contents match this build, domain, vegetation state, or enabled
  modules;
• because input runs before setup_MPI, it should stay as plain STOP rather than MPI-aware abort logic.

Plan B: Harden irstreadio in io.F90
Add defensive checks at the beginning of irstreadio:

• verify restartfile is nonblank;
• verify out. exists before slicing the string;
• parse the suffix using iostat;
• check file existence with inquire;
• open the file with iostat and report the filename on failure.

Pros:

• protects the restart reader itself, even if future callers bypass input.F90;
• keeps restart-specific assumptions near the restart code;
• can report failures close to the operation that failed.

Cons:

• rinit has already done significant initialization by then;
• if only rank 0 opens the file, a plain STOP on rank 0 can leave other MPI ranks in a bad state unless
  handled carefully;
• duplicates some checks if Plan A is also implemented.

Plan C: Add a small fatal-error helper
Create a tiny project-level fatal helper, for example fatal_error(message), that:

• prints a clear error message;
• checks whether MPI is initialized;
• if MPI is initialized, prints once on rank 0 and calls MPI_Abort;
• otherwise uses plain STOP.

Then use it for the restart check and possibly future configuration checks.
Pros:

• cleaner behavior for MPI runs;
• avoids scattered print*/STOP patterns over time;
• good foundation for future safety checks.

Cons:

• broader change than needed for this one bug;
• would require touching build files if implemented as a new module;
• existing code already uses many direct STOPs, so this introduces a new error-handling pattern.

 502

Plan D: Strict opt-in restart confirmation
If accidental restarts are especially costly, add a second gridlist flag such as irestart_confirm=0.
Behavior:

• irst=1 and irestart_confirm=0 always crashes with a message;
• intentional restart runs must set both irst=1 and irestart_confirm=1.

Pros:

• makes accidental irst=1 nearly impossible to miss;
• useful if most runs are fresh runs and restarts are rare.

Cons:

• changes the user workflow for every intentional restart;
• adds another gridlist variable that users must learn;
• probably too heavy unless accidental restarts are frequent and expensive.

Recommended path
Start with Plan A.
It gives the fastest protection against accidental irst=1 with minimal disruption:
1. Add call validate_restart_config in input.F90 immediately after reading restartfile. 2. Implement
validate_restart_config at the bottom of input.F90, similar to validate_lateral_ibc. 3. Use clear print*
messages and STOP. 4. Optionally add the same defensive parsing/open checks in irstreadio later as
Plan B.
Example failure messages to include:

ERROR: invalid irst value: 2
Allowed values are 0 fresh run or 1 restart.

ERROR: irst=1 requests a restart, but restartfile is blank.
Set irst=0 for a fresh run, or set restartfile to an existing output/restart file.

BUG-2026-07-076: Fuel-top wind interpolation is accidentally divided
in half

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/01_fuel_top_velocity_interpolation_is_halved.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
   ,→ drag_veg.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ convection_veg.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ evaporation_veg.F90

dragm interpolates velocity at the top of the fuel bed from levels 2 and 3:

rinterp=(actualFuelDepth(ift,i,j)-zla2)/(zla3-zla2)
uFuel=(xvrho(i,j,2,iuvel)+rinterp* &
  (xvrho(i,j,3,iuvel)-xvrho(i,j,2,iuvel)))/2.0_wp
vFuel=(xvrho(i,j,2,ivvel)+rinterp* &
  (xvrho(i,j,3,ivvel)-xvrho(i,j,2,ivvel)))/2.0_wp
wFuel=(xvrho(i,j,2,iwvel)+rinterp* &
  (xvrho(i,j,3,iwvel)-xvrho(i,j,2,iwvel)))/2.0_wp
sp=sqrt(uFuel**2.0_wp+vFuel**2.0_wp+wFuel**2.0_wp)

The shared fuelDragCorrection helper repeats the same pattern:

rinterp=(afd(itfindex(nfuel))-zla2)/(zla3-zla2)
uFuelTop=(u(2)+rinterp*(u(3)-u(2)))/2._wp
vFuelTop=(v(2)+rinterp*(v(3)-v(2)))/2._wp
wFuelTop=(w(2)+rinterp*(w(3)-w(2)))/2._wp

That helper feeds convection and evaporation:

sp=sqrt(rktemp)+ &
  sqrt(u_corr(ift)**2+v_corr(ift)**2+w_corr(ift)**2)

Problem
The interpolation formula should be u2 + r*(u3-u2). Dividing the whole interpolated value by two
makes the result wrong even at the interpolation endpoints:

rinterp = 0 -> current result is u2/2
rinterp = 1 -> current result is u3/2

That cuts the fuel-top speed in half before it is used for bottom-layer vegetation drag, convective heat
transfer, and evaporation. In a diagonal wind, both horizontal components are reduced before the
speed magnitude is built, so the fuel coupling sees a much weaker wind than the ambient u/v vector.

 507

This is independent of the existing multi-fuel sort-index bug in fuelDragCorrection; even a single fuel
type gets the wrong top velocity.

Remove the extra /2 from the interpolation. Leave the later layer-average expressions such as (uFuelTop
,→ +uFuelBot)/2._wp intact; those are actual averages over a layer.

BUG-2026-07-077: Windfield .0 is post-step and can already contain
the heat plume

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/01_windfield_zero_is_post_step_heat_contaminated.md

 Excluded for the reported run: windfieldout=0 and windfieldin=0 mean this code path
 is inactive. Retained as a separate defect found during the broader audit.

Assessment: Excluded here; very high likelihood only when windfield output is active and later
consumed.

The main loop reports the old time, advances the model, applies heat forcing, and only then writes
wind data:

! compress.F90:31-78
do while(ittot.lt.nt)
  ittot=it+itrestart
  ...
  write(*,’(a12,f12.3)’)’time(sec)=’,time
  ...
  call MOA
  call large_explicit_forcings
  call forcing

MOA advances physical time before heatSource is called:

! MOA.F90:51-52
do its=1,nts
  time=time+dts

! force.F90:157-162
if(ifire.eq.1) call ignite(...)
if(iheatsource.ge.1) &
  call heatSource(iheatsource,forceLE_xv(1:np,1:mp,:,:),1,np,1,mp,l,nv)

The first saved boundary file is deliberately named with a zero offset, not with physical time or the
absolute timestep:

! xeVariation/windfield.F90:14-18
if(ittot.ge.itwindfield.and.mod(ittot,itinterp).eq.0)then

endif
if(ittot.eq.itwindfield) call windFldRstWrite

Why this produces the reported symptom
At the first wind save, physical time is approximately:

 511

time = itwindfield * nts * dts

not zero. If the heat source has activated before that point, the model has already created buoyant
vertical motion. The file named xvdata.0 and windfieldstart both contain that evolved state. On a
later run, rinitXeVariation reads windfieldstart into xv before timestep 1, making the producer’s plume
appear to be a consumer-time-zero initialization problem.
The same mechanism explains why the anomaly remains: subsequent heat-contaminated windfield files
are read and interpolated at the boundaries for the entire consumer run.
This also explains why changing the consumer grid does not necessarily remove the feature. If the
same files are reused, the stored values remain; if new wind files are generated with the heat still active,
each new suite records a new plume.

Treat windfield production as a wind-only phase. A minimal containment is to reject a heat source
that activates during a wind-output run:

@@

+ use heatsource_gridlist_variables, only : starttime_hs
@@
 if(iheatsource.ge.1) call input_heatsource(iheatsource)
+ if(windfieldout.eq.1 .and. iheatsource.ge.1)then
+ if(any(starttime_hs.le.real(nt,wp)*real(nts,wp)*dts))then
+ print*,’ERROR: heat source activates during windfield production.’
+ print*,’Delay starttime_hs beyond the wind run or set iheatsource=0.’
+ stop
+ endif
+ endif

This is intentionally strict. Heat that turns off before itwindfield can still leave vertical motion at the
save point, so testing only whether it is active at the exact save instant is insufficient.
A separate usability improvement is to write the producer timestep and physical time in the file header
(finding 4), so .0 cannot be mistaken for physical t=0.

Validation
1. Delete or move the old windfieldstart and all matching xvdata.* files.
2. Regenerate the suite with iheatsource=0, or with every starttime_hs beyond the end of the wind-
 producing run.
3. In the consumer, inspect w immediately before and after rinitXeVariation.
4. Confirm that w does not jump during the load and that the first boundary targets do not contain a
 plume.

Do not validate this fix while retaining old wind files; they already contain the bad state.

 512

warning downgrade).

BUG-2026-07-078: Firebrand wind interpolation omits the high-side
x weight

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/02_firebrand_getwind_missing_x_interpolation_weight
,→ .md

GetWind claims to do trilinear interpolation, but each x interpolation omits *xd on the high-side cell:

u00=u_c(im,jm,km)*(1-xd)+u_c(ip,jm,km)
u01=u_c(im,jm,kp)*(1-xd)+u_c(ip,jm,kp)
u10=u_c(im,jp,km)*(1-xd)+u_c(ip,jp,km)
u11=u_c(im,jp,kp)*(1-xd)+u_c(ip,jp,kp)

v00=v_c(im,jm,km)*(1-xd)+v_c(ip,jm,km)
v01=v_c(im,jm,kp)*(1-xd)+v_c(ip,jm,kp)
v10=v_c(im,jp,km)*(1-xd)+v_c(ip,jp,km)
v11=v_c(im,jp,kp)*(1-xd)+v_c(ip,jp,kp)
...
w00=w_c(im,jm,km)*(1-xd)+w_c(ip,jm,km)
w01=w_c(im,jm,kp)*(1-xd)+w_c(ip,jm,kp)
w10=w_c(im,jp,km)*(1-xd)+w_c(ip,jp,km)
w11=w_c(im,jp,kp)*(1-xd)+w_c(ip,jp,kp)

Problem
The high-side sample should be multiplied by xd. Without that, a constant wind field does not
interpolate back to the same constant value. For example, if every neighboring u_c value is U, the
current first interpolation gives:

u00 = U*(1 - xd) + U = U*(2 - xd)

instead of:

u00 = U*(1 - xd) + U*xd = U

This does not affect the Eulerian wind solver directly, but it breaks wind-driven firebrand launch and
movement. In a 45-degree wind, both u and v sampled by firebrands can be overestimated and spatially
biased.

BUG-2026-07-079: Sensor-driven wind reconstruction gives larger
weight to farther sensors

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/03_xevariation_sensor_weights_use_distance_as_weight
,→ .md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ xevariation.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ input_xeVar.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ variables_xeVar.F90

Sparse sensor mode computes senw as a distance-like magnitude:

senw(kv)=sqrt((time-SensorTimes(kv))**2+ &
  ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)
totw=totw+senw(kv)

It then uses that distance directly as the interpolation weight:

xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=xe(i,j,k,iuvel)+SensorUvel(kv)* &
  max(0._wp,1._wp-1.5_wp*sum(xvfuel(:,i,j,k,irhof)))* &
  (zcart(z(k),i,j)/SensorZ(kv))**(1._wp/7._wp)* &
  senw(kv)/totw
xe(i,j,k,ivvel)=xe(i,j,k,ivvel)+SensorVvel(kv)* &
  max(0._wp,1._wp-1.5_wp*sum(xvfuel(:,i,j,k,irhof)))* &
  (zcart(z(k),i,j)/SensorZ(kv))**(1._wp/7._wp)* &
  senw(kv)/totw

Dense sensor mode repeats the same pattern for old and new sensor samples:

senw(kv)=sqrt((time-senDataNew(kv,1))**2+ &
  ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)
senw(nSensors+kv)=sqrt((time-senDataOld(kv,1))**2+ &
  ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)
totw=totw+senw(kv)+senw(nSensors+kv)

Problem
The computed senw is larger for farther-away or farther-in-time observations. Using senw/totw therefore
gives distant data more influence than nearby data.
For a reconstructed diagonal wind field, this can rotate or dilute the local wind vector if the nearest
sensor has one u/v direction and a distant sensor has another. The bug affects both components, but it
is much easier to notice when both u and v are supposed to matter.

 518

There is also a zero-distance edge case: if a cell coincides with a sensor at the same time, inverse-distance
weighting should select that sensor, while the current direct-distance weighting gives it zero weight.

Convert distances to inverse-distance weights and guard exact matches. The same pattern should be
applied in all four sensor loops in cases 3 and 4.

+ real(wp) :: totw,dist
@@
- senw(kv)=sqrt((time-SensorTimes(kv))**2+ &
-                ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)
+ dist=sqrt((time-SensorTimes(kv))**2+ &
+                ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)
+ senw(kv)=1.0_wp/max(dist,tiny(dist))

For dense sensor mode, apply the same conversion separately to senw(kv) and senw(nSensors+kv).

Git evidence: 811932f (2026-07-23, cross-wind and corner fix set); 8122925 (2026-08-05, xeVariation
fixes).

local/global coordinate handling for those distances.

BUG-2026-07-080: Turbulence initialization uses momentum squared
as wind speed squared

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/04_rinit_turb_initializes_tke_from_momentum_squared
,→ .md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/
 ,→ rinit_turb.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/domainUpdates
 ,→ .F90

The initial ambient wind is stored in conserved form. For example, setVelocityProfile multiplies velocity
by density:

xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=u0*xe(i,j,k,irho)
xe(i,j,k,ivvel)=v0*xe(i,j,k,irho)

The primitive velocity array is later built by dividing conserved fields by density:

do kv=1,nv-1
  xvrho(:,:,1:l,kv)=xv(:,:,:,kv)/xv(:,:,:,irho)
enddo

But rinitSubTurb computes the initial speed magnitude directly from conserved xe components:

sp2=xe(i,j,k,iuvel)**2+xe(i,j,k,ivvel)**2+xe(i,j,k,iwvel)**2
if(iturb.eq.2)then
  xe(i,j,k,ika)=max(min(sp2*0.05_wp,xe(i,j,k,irho)*2_wp), &
    xe(i,j,k,irho)*0.05_wp)
  xe(i,j,k,ikb)=max(min(sp2*0.01_wp,xe(i,j,k,irho)*0.5_wp),&
    xe(i,j,k,irho)*0.01_wp)
endif

Problem
xe(iuvel), xe(ivvel), and xe(iwvel) are momenta, not velocities. The current sp2 is therefore approxi-
mately rho**2 * speed**2.
The initialized turbulence variables are stored as density-weighted quantities, as shown later by
diffusivity updates that use xv(:,:,ika)/xv(:,:,irho). So the intended scaling is:

rho * coefficient * speed**2

The current code instead behaves like:

 522

coefficient * rho**2 * speed**2

then clips against density-weighted caps. This makes the initial turbulence depend incorrectly on
density. A diagonal wind with both u and v present is especially sensitive because this is the first
combined speed magnitude used by the turbulence model.

Convert conserved momentum to velocity before building sp2, then multiply the bounded turbulent
energy back by density.

diff --git a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/rinit_turb.F90 b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/

+++ b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/rinit_turb.F90
@@
- real(wp) :: sp2
+ real(wp) :: sp2,rhoLocal
@@
-            sp2=xe(i,j,k,iuvel)**2+xe(i,j,k,ivvel)**2+xe(i,j,k,iwvel)**2
+ rhoLocal=max(xe(i,j,k,irho),tiny(1.0_wp))
+            sp2=(xe(i,j,k,iuvel)**2+xe(i,j,k,ivvel)**2+ &
+              xe(i,j,k,iwvel)**2)/rhoLocal**2
 if(iturb.eq.2)then
-              xe(i,j,k,ika)=max(min(sp2*0.05_wp,xe(i,j,k,irho)*2_wp), &
-                xe(i,j,k,irho)*0.05_wp)
-              xe(i,j,k,ikb)=max(min(sp2*0.01_wp,xe(i,j,k,irho)*0.5_wp),&
-                xe(i,j,k,irho)*0.01_wp)
+              xe(i,j,k,ika)=rhoLocal*max(min(sp2*0.05_wp,2._wp),0.05_wp)
+              xe(i,j,k,ikb)=rhoLocal*max(min(sp2*0.01_wp,0.5_wp),0.01_wp)
 endif

Git evidence: 811932f (2026-07-23, cross-wind and corner fix set).
Turbulence initialization now converts momentum to velocity before squaring by dividing through
density, then stores the density-scaled turbulence fields afterward.

BUG-2026-07-081: Turbulence length-scale option isa=5 uses stale
saxy and mis-parenthesized saz

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/05_rinit_turb_isa5_uses_uninitialized_saxy_and_bad_saz_precedence
,→ .md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/
 ,→ rinit_turb.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/
 ,→ domainUpdates_turb.F90

rinitSubTurb initializes the turbulence length scales.The isa=5 branch computes saxy(i,j,k) using
saxy(i,j,k) on the right-hand side before the new value has been assigned:

elseif(isa.eq.5)then ! similar to isa=3 with a correction in the lower part of the domain
  saxy(i,j,k)=(dx*dy)**0.5_wp/sqrt(1._wp+(saxy(i,j,k)/ &
    (0.4_wp/0.23_wp*zcart(z(k),i,j)))**2)
  saz(i,j,k)=zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j)/ &
    sqrt(1._wp+(saxy(i,j,k)/ &
    (0.4_wp/0.23_wp*zcart(z(k),i,j)))**2)
endif

The resulting saxy and saz feed turbulent diffusivity:

K_axy(i,j,k) = diffcst * xv(i,j,k,irho) * &
  saxy(i,j,k) * sqrt(xv(i,j,k,ika)/xv(i,j,k,irho))
K_az(i,j,k) = diffcst * xv(i,j,k,irho) * &
  saz(i,j,k) * sqrt(xv(i,j,k,ika)/xv(i,j,k,irho))

Problem
There are two bugs in the isa=5 branch:

 1. saxy(i,j,k) is read before it is initialized in this branch. That makes

the correction depend on stale memory or on values left by a previous use.

 1. The saz assignment only divides the lower edge height by the correction

factor because division binds before subtraction:
“‘fortran zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j)/sqrt(...) “‘
If the intended value is the vertical cell thickness with the same near-ground correction, the parentheses
need to cover the full height difference.
This is not a pure direction-selection bug, but it changes turbulent diffusion and wind damping whenever
iturb=2 and isa=5 are used. With oblique winds, bad turbulence length scales can make the coupled
u/v evolution look directionally unstable or inconsistent.

 525

Compute uncorrected local length scales first, then use those temporary values to apply the correction.

diff --git a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/rinit_turb.F90 b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/
 ,→ rinit_turb.F90
--- a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/rinit_turb.F90
+++ b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/rinit_turb.F90
@@
- real(wp) :: sp2
+ real(wp) :: sp2,saxy0,saz0,zref,scaleCorrection
@@
 elseif(isa.eq.5)then ! similar to isa=3 with a correction in the lower part of the domain
-              saxy(i,j,k)=(dx*dy)**0.5_wp/sqrt(1._wp+(saxy(i,j,k)/ &
-                (0.4_wp/0.23_wp*zcart(z(k),i,j)))**2)
-              saz(i,j,k)=zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j)/ &
-                sqrt(1._wp+(saxy(i,j,k)/ &

input.F90 reads the windfield switches without an i prefix:

call QueryGridlist_variable(’windfieldin’,windfieldin,48)
...

The shipped wind-run template still uses the old names:

iwindfieldout = 1 ! Windfield output switch: 1->interpolate, 2-> one file
iwindfieldin = 0 ! Windfield input switch: 1->interpolate, 2-> one file

QueryGridlist_variable silently leaves the existing value unchanged when a key is absent:

do ! Iterate through all lines of file
  read(fileunit,"(a)",iostat=ierror) text ! Read line into text
  if (ierror/=0) exit
  ...
enddo
rewind(fileunit)

Problem
A user following TOOLS/Gridlist/gridlist-windrun expects windfield output, but the code never reads
iwindfieldout. windfieldout remains its default value of 0, so compress.F90 never calls:

That breaks wind-run/fire-run workflows. It is easy to mistake this for a sideways-wind failure if the
diagonal wind case depends on precomputed windfield boundaries.

Support the old aliases, with the new names taking precedence if both are present:

BUG-2026-07-083: Delayed heat-source waveforms use absolute
simulation time

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/08_heat_waveforms_use_absolute_time.md

Assessment: Medium likelihood for delayed, pulsed, or sinusoidal sources; not relevant when
isource_function_hs=0 (constant). It can make activation unexpectedly abrupt or put a source at
an arbitrary phase.

The active interval is source-relative, but waveform phase and pulse duration use global time:

! HeatSource/heatsource_heat.F90:118-163
heatsource_active = time.ge.starttime_hs(itsource) .and. &
  time.lt.endtime_hs(itsource)
...
select case(isource_function_hs(itsource))
  case(0)
 source_function=1.0_wp
  case(1)
    if(sin(2.0_wp*pi*freq_hs(itsource)*time).ge.0.0_wp) &
 source_function=1.0_wp
  case(2)
 source_function=0.5_wp* &
      (1.0_wp+sin(2.0_wp*pi*freq_hs(itsource)*time))
  case(3)
 if(freq_hs(itsource)*time.le.1.0_wp) source_function=1.0_wp

Consequences
• A delayed step or sine source begins at a phase determined by total simulation time, not at its own
  phase zero.
• A delayed single-pulse source may never turn on. For example, if starttime_hs > 1/freq_hs, case 3 is
  already outside its pulse window on the first active call.
• Multiple sources with different start times cannot share the same reproducible waveform relative to
  their activation.
• An arbitrary first amplitude can make the pressure/buoyancy startup impulse much sharper than
  intended. If windfield output is enabled, that response is then archived by findings 1 and 2.

For case 2 specifically, the current sine definition starts at half amplitude even after making time
source-relative. That may be intended, but it is not a zero-to-full ramp.

@@
- real(wp) :: source_function=0.0_wp
+ real(wp) :: source_function=0.0_wp,source_time
@@

 532

 source_function=0.0_wp
+ source_time=time-starttime_hs(itsource)
 select case(isource_function_hs(itsource))
@@
- if(sin(2.0_wp*pi*freq_hs(itsource)*time).ge.0.0_wp)then
+ if(sin(2.0_wp*pi*freq_hs(itsource)*source_time).ge.0.0_wp)then
@@
-          (1.0_wp+sin(2.0_wp*pi*freq_hs(itsource)*time))
+ (1.0_wp+sin(2.0_wp*pi*freq_hs(itsource)*source_time))
@@
- (freq_hs(itsource)*time.le.1.0_wp))then
+ (freq_hs(itsource)*source_time.le.1.0_wp))then

If case 2 is intended as a smooth ramp beginning at zero, use the separately reviewed waveform

0.5_wp*(1.0_wp-cos(2.0_wp*pi*freq_hs(itsource)*source_time))

rather than changing it silently as part of the timing fix.

Validation
• Start two otherwise identical pulsed sources at different times. Each should remain on for exactly
  1/freq_hs after its own start.
• Start two sine sources at different times and compare their values at equal source ages; they should
  match.
• Verify constant mode is bit-for-bit unchanged.
• Log source_time and source_function at activation, then confirm the values used in the first heat
  forcing.

Git evidence: fd22add (2026-07-23, heat-source waveform time fix).
Heat-source waveform cases now compute source_time=time-starttime_hs(itsource) before evaluating
delayed source shapes.

BUG-2026-07-084: Ramped wind components are not initialized
before xv is copied from xe

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/10_ramp_winds_not_initialized_before_xv_copy.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ xevariation.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/input.F90

input.F90 enables environmental variation when either wind switch is 1:

call QueryGridlist_variable(’u0’,u0,48)
call QueryGridlist_variable(’uswitch’,uswitch,48)
call QueryGridlist_variable(’v0’,v0,48)
call QueryGridlist_variable(’vswitch’,vswitch,48)
if(uswitch.eq.1.or.vswitch.eq.1) ixevariation=1

But rinit.F90 copies the environmental field into the prognostic state before the ramp logic has ever
populated switch-1 wind components:

! Initialize wind profiles
call setVelocityProfile

! Ignitialize fuel parameters
if(iturb.ge.1) call rinitSubTurb

xv(1:np,1:mp,:,:)=xe

...
time=itrestart*dts*nts
if(iheatsource.ge.1) call rinitHeatSource()
if(ixevariation.ge.1) call rinitXeVariation(ixevariation)

Inside setVelocityProfile, switch 1 is explicitly not assigned:

! NB uswitch.eq.1 is defined in xevariation.f
if(uswitch==0)then
  xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=u0*xe(i,j,k,irho)
elseif(uswitch==2)then
  xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=u0*xe(i,j,k,irho)*uprofile(i,j,k)
endif
if(vswitch==0)then
  xe(i,j,k,ivvel)=v0*xe(i,j,k,irho)
elseif(vswitch==2)then
  xe(i,j,k,ivvel)=v0*xe(i,j,k,irho)*uprofile(i,j,k)
endif

xevariation.F90 can later compute switch-1 winds:

 535

if(uswitch==1)then
  xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=min(uramp*xe(i,j,k,irho), &
 (time*uramp/uramptime+u0)*xe(i,j,k,irho)) &
    *(min(100._wp,zcart(z(k),1,1))/zu)**(1._wp/7._wp)
endif

Problem
For ramped wind runs, xv is initialized from xe before xevariation has had a chance to set the ramped
component to its initial value. If both components are ramped, a diagonal wind can start with no
horizontal momentum. If one component is profile-driven and the other is ramped, only one component
is present in the initial prognostic field.
That matters for sideways winds because a 45-degree ramp such as uswitch=1, vswitch=1 depends on
both components being present from the start. The first call to explicit_domain_updates updates xe, but
it does not replace the already-copied interior xv state.

Treat switch 1 like switch 0 during the initial ambient setup, using u0 and v0 as the initial ramp values.
This complements the structural fix in 01_velocity_profile_skips_constant_switches.md, which moves the
velocity assignment outside the switch-2-only guard.

diff --git a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90 b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
--- a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
+++ b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
@@
- ! NB uswitch.eq.1 is defined in xevariation.f
- if(uswitch==0)then
+ ! Switch 1 is ramped by xevariation during the run, but its
+ ! initial state should still start from u0/v0.
+ if(uswitch==0.or.uswitch==1)then
 xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=u0*xe(i,j,k,irho)
 elseif(uswitch==2)then
 xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=u0*xe(i,j,k,irho)*uprofile(i,j,k) !u0 represents speed at zu
 endif
- if(vswitch==0)then
+ if(vswitch==0.or.vswitch==1)then
 xe(i,j,k,ivvel)=v0*xe(i,j,k,irho)
 elseif(vswitch==2)then
 xe(i,j,k,ivvel)=v0*xe(i,j,k,irho)*uprofile(i,j,k) !v0 represents speed at zu

Apply the same switch==1 handling in the icorio.eq.2 branch if ramped winds are allowed with icorio=2.

BUG-2026-07-085: Ambient velocity initialization can leave constant
or vertical wind components unset

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/11_ambient_velocity_initialization_skips_constant_winds
,→ .md

Scope
This report focuses on ordinary ambient wind initialization and the xe values used as boundary
relaxation targets.

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/definearray.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.
 ,→ F90

definearray.F90 allocates xe without initializing it:

allocate(xe(np,mp,l,nv))

rinit.F90 then initializes thermodynamic fields, calls setVelocityProfile, and copies xe into the trans-
ported state:

call setRhoThetaP
...
call setVelocityProfile
...
xv(1:np,1:mp,:,:)=xe

Inside setVelocityProfile, the velocity assignment for the ordinary ambient profile is nested inside a
profile-only guard:

if(uswitch.eq.2.or.vswitch.eq.2)then ! Empirical profile of Kaimal and Finnigan 1994 and Raupach 1993
  ...
 do k=1,l
 do j=1,mp
 do i=1,np
 ! NB uswitch.eq.1 is defined in xevariation.f
 if(uswitch==0)then
 xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=u0*xe(i,j,k,irho)
 elseif(uswitch==2)then
 xe(i,j,k,iuvel)=u0*xe(i,j,k,irho)*uprofile(i,j,k) !u0 represents speed at zu
 endif
 if(vswitch==0)then
 xe(i,j,k,ivvel)=v0*xe(i,j,k,irho)
 elseif(vswitch==2)then
 xe(i,j,k,ivvel)=v0*xe(i,j,k,irho)*uprofile(i,j,k) !v0 represents speed at zu

 539

 endif
 enddo
 enddo
 enddo
  deallocate(uprofile)
endif

Why this can break sideways winds
For a 45 degree wind, a user may naturally set both components directly, for example u0 = U/sqrt(2),
v0 = U/sqrt(2), with uswitch = 0 and vswitch = 0 for constant profiles. In that case, setVelocityProfile
never enters the outer if(uswitch.eq.2.or.vswitch.eq.2) block, so neither u nor v is assigned.
Even when one component uses profile option 2, iwvel is never set in setVelocityProfile. Since xe is
uninitialized at allocation, xv=xe can seed the model with undefined vertical ambient momentum. That
can contaminate the apparent horizontal wind behavior and makes diagonal cases harder to diagnose.
Axis-aligned runs can hide this if they use the default/profile path (uswitch=2) while the diagonal test
uses constant components.

Initialize the ambient velocity slots deterministically, and assign constant/ramp initial components
before the profile-specific block. The profile block can then overwrite only the components that actually
requested option 2.

diff --git a/rinit.F90 b/rinit.F90

+ logical :: need_profile

BUG-2026-07-086: The normal output workflow does not write the
initialized t=0 state

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/11_no_true_t0_output_and_stale_output_risk.md

Assessment: High likelihood for the claim that the anomaly is "present at t=0." It can mislabel a
post-step heat response or reuse an old comp.out.0.

After rinit, the solver enters timestep 1 without writing an initial output:

! compress.F90:27-35

it=1
do while(ittot.lt.nt)
  ittot=it+itrestart
  ...
  write(*,’(a12,f12.3)’)’time(sec)=’,time

The displayed time is the value before MOA advances it. Normal output occurs only after the complete
large step and all forcing:

! compress.F90:68-83
call MOA
call large_explicit_forcings
call forcing
...
if(mod(ittot,frqoutput).eq.0) call binary_writeio(ittot)

Output contains no timestep or physical-time header; the filename contains only ittot:

! io.F90:20-30
write(fend,"(i0)") ittot
fname=outname(1:it-1)//’.’//fend
...
do it=1,nv
  call writeio(xv(1:np,1:mp,:,it),48,l)
enddo

Meanwhile, the supplied VTK converter defaults to initial=0 and attempts to read comp.out.0:

# TOOLS/Make_VTS_Files/Fire_Run/convert_firetec_binary_to_VTK.py:11-17, 128-136
readfilename = ’comp.out.’
initial = 0
...
for i in range(initial, final, incr):
 filename = fname+str(i)
 ...
 gridToVTK(vtsfile, XI, YI, ZI, pointData=...)

The current fresh-run solver never creates comp.out.0.

 543

Consequences
• The first available output is post-step, even if a viewer labels its position in a series as time zero.
• A comp.out.0 left by an older run can be converted as the current initial state.
• Existing output files beyond a shorter rerun remain in the directory and can be mixed into a new
  visualization.
• VTS files contain no explicit physical-time field in this converter, so file-series indexing can be
  mistaken for simulation seconds.

The controlled trace showed literal initialized w=0; heat first activated at time=nts*dts, and heat-driven
w appeared in the following pressure solve. A viewer’s t=0 is therefore not proof that the Fortran
initialized a nonzero w.

Write a true fresh initial state immediately after rinit, and embed time metadata in a versioned output
header or VTK FieldData:

@@

+ if(itrestart.eq.0) call binary_writeio(0)

At minimum, print and store the corresponding physical time. A durable binary format should write
ittot and time in a header rather than relying on the filename.
Update conversion defaults so they agree with the files actually requested, and fail if a file’s modification
time or run identifier does not match the current suite.

Immediate operational mitigation
Before each run, use a new empty output and VTS directory. Confirm that comp.out.0 is created by
the current executable after implementing the diff; do not retain a legacy file with that name.

Validation
1. Inspect comp.out.0 and confirm w=0 immediately after analytic initialization.
2. Confirm comp.out.1 corresponds to physical time nts*dts, not zero.
3. Run with delayed heat and verify output timestamps show the correct activation interval.
4. Shorten a rerun and confirm no stale later VTS files appear in the current time series.

Fresh runs now call binary_writeio(0) after initialization when itrestart.eq.0, writing the initialized
t=0 state.

BUG-2026-07-087: Sensor-driven winds compute distances from local
MPI coordinates

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/12_sensor_wind_distances_use_local_rank_coordinates
,→ .md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ xevariation.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ input_xeVar.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul16/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ variables_xeVar.F90

Sensor wind modes read SensorX and SensorY as user-provided locations:

call QueryGridlist_array(’SensorX’,SensorX,nSensors,48)
call QueryGridlist_array(’SensorY’,SensorY,nSensors,48)

xevariation imports the local MPI rank position:

But sensor distances are computed from local cell indices:

senw(kv)=sqrt((time-SensorTimes(kv))**2+ &
  ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)

Dense sensor mode repeats the same coordinate expression:

senw(kv)=sqrt((time-senDataNew(kv,1))**2+ &
  ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)
senw(nSensors+kv)=sqrt((time-senDataOld(kv,1))**2+ &
  ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)

Problem
On a multi-rank run, local i and j restart at 1 on every MPI rank. That means every rank computes
sensor distances as though it owned the lower-left corner of the global domain.
For example, the first x cell on rank npos=2 should be near global index np+1, but the current formula
uses (i-1)*dx = 0. The same issue applies in y through mpos.
Sensor-driven diagonal winds are vulnerable because the reconstructed u and v components can repeat
rank-by-rank instead of varying with the real sensor geometry. This is separate from the existing
distance-weighting bug: even with inverse-distance weights, the wrong coordinate frame will still choose
the wrong sensors on all but the first rank in each direction.

 546

Use global cell indices when comparing cells to SensorX and SensorY. Apply the same replacement in all
sensor-distance loops in cases 3 and 4.

diff --git a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/xevariation.F90 b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation

@@

+            ia=(npos-1)*np+i
+            ja=(mpos-1)*mp+j

-                ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)
+                ((ia-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2+ &
+                ((ja-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2)

 enddo
@@
 do i=il,iu
+            ia=(npos-1)*np+i
+            ja=(mpos-1)*mp+j

 do kv=1,nSensors
 senw(kv)=sqrt((time-senDataNew(kv,1))**2+ &

BUG-2026-07-088: A fresh run extrapolates HRR/MLR before the
first input timestamp

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/13_fresh_hrr_mlr_input_extrapolates_before_first_record
,→ .md

Assessment: High likelihood if MLRHRRinputs_hs=1 and the first data timestamp is later than the first
active heat call.

For a fresh run, initialization reads the first two records but does not clamp simulation time to their
range:

! HeatSource/rinit_heat.F90:143-164
read(unit_hs,*,iostat=iostat) TME(itsource,1), &
  MLR(itsource,1),HRR(itsource,1)
...
read(unit_hs,*,iostat=iostat) TME(itsource,2), &
  MLR(itsource,2),HRR(itsource,2)

heatSource then uses linear interpolation unconditionally unless the timestamps are identical:

! HeatSource/heatsource_heat.F90:205-220
if(abs(TME(itsource,2)-TME(itsource,1)).lt.tolerance) then
  fm_hs(itsource)=MLR(itsource,2)
else
  fm_hs(itsource)=MLR(itsource,1)+ &
 (time-TME(itsource,1))/(TME(itsource,2)-TME(itsource,1))* &
 (MLR(itsource,2)-MLR(itsource,1))
endif
...
hrr_now=HRR(itsource,1)+ &
  (time-TME(itsource,1))/(TME(itsource,2)-TME(itsource,1))* &
  (HRR(itsource,2)-HRR(itsource,1))

The restart path in rinit_heat.F90 explicitly handles time<=told, but the fresh-run path does not.

Failure mode
If the table begins at 10 s and the source is active at 0.01 s, the interpolation fraction is negative. A
rising table is extrapolated backward, potentially producing a large negative value; a falling table can
produce a value above the first recorded HRR. Either can create an incorrect initial pressure pulse.
There is a second timing ambiguity: the interpolation uses global simulation time, not time-starttime_hs.
A data file intended to be relative to source activation is shifted whenever the source has a nonzero
start time.

Clamp to the first record before interpolating:

 550

@@ MLR interpolation
- if(abs(TME(itsource,2)-TME(itsource,1)).lt.tolerance) then
+ if(time.le.TME(itsource,1))then
+ fm_hs(itsource)=MLR(itsource,1)
+ elseif(abs(TME(itsource,2)-TME(itsource,1)).lt.tolerance)then
 fm_hs(itsource)=MLR(itsource,2)
@@ HRR interpolation
- if(abs(TME(itsource,2)-TME(itsource,1)).lt.tolerance) then
+ if(time.le.TME(itsource,1))then
+ hrr_now=HRR(itsource,1)
+ elseif(abs(TME(itsource,2)-TME(itsource,1)).lt.tolerance)then
 hrr_now=HRR(itsource,2)

Do not overwrite TME(:,2) to clamp: the file is already positioned after the second record, so doing so
would lose that record when advancing.
Separately document whether table times are absolute simulation times or source ages. If they are
source-relative, use source_age=time-starttime_hs(itsource) consistently in the advance and interpolation
comparisons.

Validation
• Use a table whose first timestamp is later than zero; HRR/MLR must equal the first record until
  that timestamp.
• Test before, exactly at, between, and after the first two timestamps.
• Repeat with a delayed starttime_hs under the documented absolute/relative convention.
• Reject non-monotonic timestamps rather than allowing division by a negative or zero interval.

Git evidence: ba0bb93 (2026-07-23, heat-source HRR/MLR initial value fix).
MLR/HRR interpolation now uses the first tabulated value when simulation time is at or before the
first timestamp, avoiding backward extrapolation on fresh runs.

BUG-2026-07-089: Windfield File Cadence Uses Absolute Timesteps
While File Names Use Relative Timesteps

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/13_windfield_cadence_uses_absolute_timestep.md

• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/windfield.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/rinit_xeVar.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/xevariation.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/variables_xeVar.F90

The writer gates output using the absolute timestep, but names each file using the timestep relative to
itwindfield:

subroutine windField(ittot)
  use windfieldio, only : itwindfield,itinterp,xvdataname
  ...
  if(ittot.ge.itwindfield.and.mod(ittot,itinterp).eq.0)then

  endif
  if(ittot.eq.itwindfield) call windFldRstWrite
end subroutine windField

The reader initializes its interpolation window relative to the restart timestep:

itabsold=itrestart
itabsnew=itrestart+itinterp

do kv=1,nvwind
  xvdataold(:,:,:,kv)=xv(1:np,1:mp,:,w2f_index(kv))
enddo

call windfld_read(fxvdataname)

But the runtime reader advances files on absolute multiples of itinterp:

case (2)
  if(mod(ittot,itinterp).eq.0) then
 xvdataold = xvdatanew
 itabsold = itabsnew
 itabsnew=itabsold+itinterp

 call windfld_read(fxvdataname)
  endif

The defaults make this easy to miss because the default start is divisible by the default interval:

integer :: windspeedupfactor= 1
integer :: itwindfield = 80000

 553

integer :: itinterp = 10

Problem
The writer and reader both mix relative file numbering with absolute cadence checks.
On output, if itwindfield is not divisible by itinterp, the first saved boundary file is not the file the
reader expects. Example with itwindfield=5 and itinterp=10: the writer first passes the gate at ittot=10
and writes xvdata.5, then xvdata.15; a replay initialized from timestep 5 expects xvdata.15 first, then
xvdata.25, or with a start-file workflow may expect xvdata.10 depending on the configured speed-up.
Either way, the output sequence is shifted from the interpolation window.
On input, itabsold and itabsnew are explicitly relative to itrestart, but the advance test ignores that
and fires on absolute multiples of itinterp. For a restart at timestep 5 with itinterp=10, the next data
window is 5 to 15, but the runtime read fires at timestep 10 and advances to the next file too early.
This can make diagonal windfield replay look broken even when the boundary files contain both u and
v: the strips are missing, read at the wrong time, or interpolated against the wrong pair of files.

Anchor the output cadence to itwindfield, and advance the input reader when the active interpolation
window actually reaches itabsnew:

diff --git a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/windfield.F90 b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/
 ,→ windfield.F90
--- a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/windfield.F90
+++ b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/windfield.F90
@@
- if(ittot.ge.itwindfield.and.mod(ittot,itinterp).eq.0)then
+ if(ittot.ge.itwindfield.and.mod(ittot-itwindfield,itinterp).eq.0)then

 endif
diff --git a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/xevariation.F90 b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation
 ,→ /xevariation.F90
--- a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/xevariation.F90
+++ b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/xevariation.F90
@@

+ if(ittot.ge.itabsnew) then
 xvdataold = xvdatanew
 itabsold = itabsnew
 itabsnew=itabsold+itinterp

If the main loop can skip more than one large timestep between calls, wrap the input advance in a
bounded loop and read until ittot.lt.itabsnew.

Windfield-file cadence was changed to use the relative timestep expression mod(ittot-itwindfield,itinterp

BUG-2026-07-090: Bottom xvrho Plane Is Filled Only in the Interior,
but Turbulence Reads Its Lateral Halos

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/14_bottom_xvrho_plane_missing_lateral_halo_update.
,→ md

• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/domainUpdates.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/definearray.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/stressrij_turb.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/diffuse_turb.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/force_turb.F90

xvrho is allocated with a bottom plane at k=0:

allocate(xvrho(1-ih:np+ih,1-ih:mp+ih,0:l,nv-1))

explicit_domain_updates fills xvrho(:,:,1:l,:), then computes the bottom plane:

do kv=1,nv-1
  xvrho(:,:,1:l,kv)=xv(:,:,:,kv)/xv(:,:,:,irho)
enddo
...
k=1 !bottombc
do j=1-ih+1,mp+ih-1
  do i=1-ih+1,np+ih-1
    g13 = c13(i,j)*gmul(1)
    g23 = c23(i,j)*gmul(1)
    g33 = g13**2+g23**2+gi(i,j,1)**2
 do kv=1,nv
 xvrho(i,j,0,kv)=getSubGroundValue(xvrho(i,j,k,kv), &
        xvrho(i-1,j,k,kv),xvrho(i+1,j,k,kv),xvrho(i,j-1,k,kv), &
        xvrho(i,j+1,k,kv),g13,g23,g33)
 enddo
 uground=0.5_wp*(xvrho(i,j,1,iuvel)+xvrho(i,j,0,iuvel))
 vground=0.5_wp*(xvrho(i,j,1,ivvel)+xvrho(i,j,0,ivvel))
 wground = - (g13 * uground + g23 * vground)/gi(i,j,1)
 xvrho(i,j,0,iwvel) = 2*wground-xvrho(i,j,1,iwvel)
  enddo
enddo

For the normal ih=1 case, that loop range fills only i=1:np and j=1:mp on the k=0 plane. It does not
update i=0, i=np+1, j=0, or j=mp+1.
The turbulence stress operator reads those bottom lateral halos at k=1:

uz = 0.5_wp*(xvrho(i,j,kp1,iuvel)-xvrho(i,j,k-1,iuvel)+ &
  xvrho(i-1,j,kp1,iuvel)-xvrho(i-1,j,k-1,iuvel))*hdzi
...
uz = 0.5_wp*(xvrho(i,j,kp1,iuvel)-xvrho(i,j,k-1,iuvel)+ &

 556

  xvrho(i,j-1,kp1,iuvel)-xvrho(i,j-1,k-1,iuvel))*hdzi

It also reads k=0 halos in the k-1/2 face calculations:

ux = 0.5_wp*(xvrho(i+1,j,kk,iuvel)-xvrho(i-1,j,kk,iuvel)+ &
  xvrho(i+1,j,k0,iuvel)-xvrho(i-1,j,k0,iuvel))*hdxi
...
uy = 0.5_wp*(xvrho(i,j+1,kk,iuvel)-xvrho(i,j-1,kk,iuvel)+ &
  xvrho(i,j+1,k0,iuvel)-xvrho(i,j-1,k0,iuvel))*hdyi

The scalar diffusion operator has the same dependency:

pz = 0.5_wp*(phi(i,j,kp1)-phi(i,j,k-1)+ &
  phi(i-1,j,kp1)-phi(i-1,j,k-1))*hdzi
...
pz = 0.5_wp*(phi(i,j,kp1)-phi(i,j,k-1)+ &
  phi(i,j-1,kp1)-phi(i,j-1,k-1))*hdzi

force_turb.F90 passes the xvrho fields into both operators:

call stressrij(force_xv(:,:,:,iuvel),force_xv(:,:,:,ivvel), &
  force_xv(:,:,:,iwvel),1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l)
...
call diffuse(force_xv(:,:,:,kv),xvrho(:,:,:,kv), &
  1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,one)

Problem
The k=0 subground plane is a special derived plane, not a transported field. The interior values are
recomputed each large step, but the lateral halo cells on that plane are left stale or undefined.
That matters most for off-axis winds because the lower boundary and turbulence terms couple both
horizontal directions:

• the bottom vertical velocity uses g13 * uground + g23 * vground;
• stressrij uses both x-side and y-side derivatives at k=0;
• diffuse uses the same bottom-plane side values for scalar diffusion.

An x-only or y-only case can accidentally hide part of the damage. A 45-degree flow exercises both
sets of k=0 side halos at the same time.

After recomputing the bottom plane, run the same lateral halo exchange/boundary update on xvrho
,→ (:,:,0,:) that the rest of the code expects for fields read with side derivatives.
The nv-1 loop bound shown here is also required because xvrho is allocated only through nv-1:

The 0:0 section gives update a one-level third dimension while mapping that level to the real k=0 plane.

BUG-2026-07-091: Gridlist Query Calls Can Erase Defaults When
Keys Are Absent

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/15_gridlist_query_intent_out_erases_defaults.md

• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/input.F90
• higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation/input_xeVar.F90

variables.F90 documents the intended default model:

! Gridlist variables set to defaults here and changed only in the
! gridlist itself
...
real(wp):: u0               = 3._wp
integer :: uswitch = 2
real(wp):: v0               = 0._wp
integer :: vswitch = 0
...
integer :: windfieldout = 0
integer :: windfieldin = 0
integer :: ixevariation = 0

But the generic gridlist readers use intent(out):

subroutine QueryGridlist_variable(variableName,variable,fileunit)
  ...
  character(len=*),intent(in) :: variableName
  class(*),intent(out) :: variable

  ...
  do
 read(fileunit,"(a)",iostat=ierror) text
 if (ierror/=0) exit
 if(text/=’’)then
 read(text,*) word

 select type (x=>variable)
 type is (integer)
 read(text,*) word,equal,x
 type is (integer(int64))
 read(text,*) word,equal,x
 type is (real(wp))
 read(text,*) word,equal,x
 type is (character(len=*))
 read(text,*) word,equal,x

subroutine QueryGridlist_array(variableName,array,size,fileunit)

 561

  ...
  class(*),intent(out) :: array(size)

The wind-related inputs are read as optional gridlist overrides:

call QueryGridlist_variable(’u0’,u0,48)
call QueryGridlist_variable(’uswitch’,uswitch,48)
call QueryGridlist_variable(’v0’,v0,48)
call QueryGridlist_variable(’vswitch’,vswitch,48)
...
call QueryGridlist_variable(’ixevariation’,ixevariation,48)
call QueryGridlist_variable(’windfieldin’,windfieldin,48)
call QueryGridlist_variable(’windfieldout’,windfieldout,48)

Problem
In Fortran, an intent(out) dummy argument becomes undefined on entry to the procedure. If the
requested key is not found in gridlist, QueryGridlist_variable exits without assigning the dummy, so
the caller’s previous default is no longer guaranteed.
That contradicts the design in variables.F90: defaults are supposed to remain valid unless the gridlist
overrides them. Sideways-wind setups are especially exposed because they often rely on some component
settings being defaulted while only the other component is supplied. For example, a run may specify v0
but rely on the default uswitch, or specify windfield input while relying on default output and timing
switches. Those missing keys can leave wind switches and magnitudes undefined.
The array reader has the same issue for optional array-style inputs.

Preserve the caller’s existing value unless a matching key is found:

diff --git a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist.F90 b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist.F90
--- a/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist.F90
+++ b/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist.F90
@@
- class(*),intent(out) :: variable
+ class(*),intent(inout) :: variable
@@
- class(*),intent(out) :: array(size)
+ class(*),intent(inout) :: array(size)

Optional follow-up: return a found flag or status code from these routines so required gridlist keys can
still be enforced explicitly.

Git evidence: 811932f (2026-07-23, cross-wind and corner fix set); 38a57e9 (2026-08-14, readgridlist,
rmaxmin, and wind initialization fixes).
QueryGridlist scalar and array outputs were changed to intent(inout) and the parser was later generalized
so absent keys preserve defaults instead of erasing them.

BUG-2026-07-092: FIREBRANDS-015: Firebrand restart reader
leaves unit 48 open

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/FIREBRANDS-015.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Firebrands/
   ,→ io_fb.F90

irstreadio_fb opens the firebrand restart file and reads the count and particle array:

open(48,file=restartfile_fb,form=’unformatted’,status=’old’)

The subroutine then partitions the brands but never closes unit 48.

Problem
Every rank leaves the restart file connected to unit 48. Later code reuses unit 48 for normal model
output and firebrand output. Depending on the runtime, reopening an already-connected unit for a
different file can fail, implicitly close the previous file, or leave file state harder to reason about.
The main restart reader in io.F90 closes unit 48 after reading; the firebrand restart reader should do
the same.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Firebrands/io_fb.F90
@@

+ close(48)

 ! Identify the brands to be removed from processor

Git evidence: af8cb71 (2026-07-23, firebrand restart close).
The firebrand restart reader now closes unit 48 after reading.

BUG-2026-07-093: IO-001: Restart reads pass an input-only buffer
to MPI_Scatter

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/IO-001.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/io.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/definearray.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ definearray_veg.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation
 ,→ /rinit_xeVar.F90

readio declares the destination array as input-only:

subroutine readio(array,iunit,nzdim)
  use gridlist_variables, only : n,m,nprocx,nprocy,wp

  use msga_variables, only : mpi_comm_world,mpi_rank,numprocs,ierror

  integer,intent(in) :: nzdim,iunit
  real(wp),intent(in) :: array(np,mp,nzdim)

The same dummy argument is then used as the receive buffer for MPI_Scatter:

  nsize=np*mp*nzdim
  call mpi_scatter(tmparray,nsize,mpi_wp,array,nsize,mpi_wp,0, &

Restart and windfield initialization pass array sections into that buffer:

  call readio(xv(1:np,1:mp,:,it),48,l)

  call readio(xvfuel(ift,:,:,:,it),48,lfuel)

  call readio(xv(1:np,1:mp,:,w2f_index(kv)),48,l)

Those sections are not naturally contiguous in memory for the main xv halo layout or for the fuel array
layout:

allocate(xv(1-ih:np+ih,1-ih:mp+ih,l,nv))

 567

allocate(xvfuel(nfuel,np,mp,lfuel,nvfuel))

Problem
readio treats array as an output buffer: it reads a global record on rank 0, scatters each subdomain,
and fills the caller’s array. Marking array as intent(in) makes that write illegal from Fortran’s point of
view.
This can show up in two ways:

• MPI modules with stricter explicit interfaces can reject the call because MPI_Scatter writes to a
  dummy argument declared intent(in).
• With non-contiguous array sections, compilers may use temporary buffers. The wrong intent gives
  the compiler license to treat the dummy as read-only, which can prevent reliable copy-out of restart
  data into xv, xvfuel, or windfield arrays.

The result is a fragile restart path: a restart can compile/run with one compiler and fail, warn, or
silently keep initialized values with another.

Declare the receive buffer as output. readio fills the whole np,mp,nzdim interior block, so intent(out)
matches the routine’s behavior.

+++ b/CODE-dev/io.F90
@@
 ! Local Variables
 integer,intent(in) :: nzdim,iunit
- real(wp),intent(in) :: array(np,mp,nzdim)
+ real(wp),intent(out) :: array(np,mp,nzdim)

If explicit interfaces are added later, this change also makes the readio contract match its callers and
the MPI receive-buffer contract.

Git evidence: 79cd809 (2026-07-23, restart buffer intent fix).
The restart read buffer passed through MPI scatter was changed from intent(in) to intent(out).

# Full command: git show --find-renames --unified=3 79cd809 -- CODE-dev/io.F90

index e9f8095..0b9658a 100644

+++ b/CODE-dev/io.F90
@@ -129,7 +129,7 @@ subroutine readio(array,iunit,nzdim)

 ! Local Variables
 integer,intent(in) :: nzdim,iunit

 568

- real(wp),intent(in) :: array(np,mp,nzdim)
+ real(wp),intent(out) :: array(np,mp,nzdim)

    real(wp),allocatable:: tmparray(:,:,:,:),indata(:,:,:)

BUG-2026-07-094: READGRIDLIST-005: Duplicate gridlist keys
silently use the first value

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/READGRIDLIST-005.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist
 ,→ .F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/input.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/TOOLS/Basic_Run/
 ,→ gridlist
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/TOOLS/Test_Run/
 ,→ gridlist

Every query exits on the first matching line:

! readgridlist.F90
  do ! Iterate through all lines of file
 read(fileunit,"(a)",iostat=ierror) text ! Read line into text
 if (ierror/=0) exit
 if(text/=’’)then
 read(text,*) word

 read(text,*) word,equal,variable
 exit
 endif
 endif
  enddo
  rewind(fileunit)

The gridlist files are loose text configuration files rather than a single structured read:

! input.F90
  open(unit=48,file="gridlist",action="read")
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’nt’,nt,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’frqoutput’,frqoutput,48)
  ...

Problem
If a key appears twice, readgridlist.F90 silently uses the first value and ignores the later one:

nt = 10000
...
nt = 20

That is a dangerous configuration-file behavior. Users commonly append overrides near the bottom of
a run setup or leave an old value above a revised value while testing. In this reader, the later correction

 570

is inert, and there is no warning that two different values were supplied.
This is especially easy to miss because the reader rewinds for every key; it does not parse the gridlist
once and validate uniqueness.

Either reject duplicates or intentionally implement last-value-wins behavior. The safer fix is to count
matches and stop when a duplicate key is encountered:

+++ b/CODE-dev/readgridlist.F90
@@
- integer :: ierror
+ integer :: ierror,nfound
@@
 ! Executable Code
+ nfound = 0
 do ! Iterate through all lines of file
@@
 read(text,*) word

+ nfound = nfound + 1
+ if(nfound.gt.1)then
+ print*,’ERROR: duplicate gridlist key: ’,trim(variableName)
+ STOP
+ endif
 read(text,*) word,equal,variable
- exit
 endif

Apply the same duplicate detection to each query routine. If override semantics are preferred, keep
scanning after each match and let the final value win, but print a warning when nfound.gt.1 so accidental
duplicates are visible.

Git evidence: 5117a2a (2026-07-23, duplicate gridlist key check).
Gridlist lookup now counts duplicate matches and reports duplicate keys instead of silently using the
first occurrence.

BUG-2026-07-095: READGRIDLIST-006: Gridlist key matching is
case-sensitive

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/READGRIDLIST-006.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist
 ,→ .F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/input.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Firebrands/
   ,→ input_fb.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Firebrands/
 ,→ variables_fb.F90

The reader compares the raw token from the gridlist to the requested name:

! readgridlist.F90
  read(text,*) word

 read(text,*) word,equal,variable
 exit
  endif

Several queried keys use mixed case:

! Firebrands/input_fb.F90
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’shapeFB’,shapeFB,48)
  call QueryGridlist_integer(’dsizeFB’,dsizeFB,48)
  call QueryGridlist_real(’radiusFB’,radius,48)
  call QueryGridlist_real(’heightFB’,height,48)
  call QueryGridlist_real(’rhoFB’,rhoFB,48)
  call QueryGridlist_real(’TempThreshFB’,TempHot,48)

The main variables module also exposes mixed-case Fortran identifiers, while input.F90 queries a
different spelling for at least one of them:

! variables.F90
  real(wp) :: relativeHumidity = 0.0_wp

! input.F90
  call QueryGridlist_real(’relativehumidity’,relativeHumidity,48)

 573

Problem
Fortran identifiers are case-insensitive, and the gridlist format is visually namelist-like. A user mirroring
the module variable name might reasonably write:

relativeHumidity = 35.0

but input.F90 only asks for relativehumidity, so the current reader will not match it. Similarly,
tempthreshfb, TempThreshFb, or RHOFB will not match the firebrand keys even though those spellings
refer to the same Fortran identifier conceptually.
Because the query routines also lack missing-key status, this case mismatch is silent. The intended
override is skipped, and the run proceeds with a default or undefined value depending on the target
variable.

Normalize both the gridlist token and requested key before comparing:

+++ b/CODE-dev/readgridlist.F90
@@
 character(len=1) :: equal
 character(len=20) :: word
+ character(len=1000) :: queryName
 character(len=1000) :: text
@@
 ! Executable Code
+ queryName = variableName
+ call lowercase_inplace(queryName)
 do ! Iterate through all lines of file
@@
 read(text,*) word
- if(word.eq.variableName)then
+ call lowercase_inplace(word)
+ if(trim(word).eq.trim(queryName))then
 read(text,*) word,equal,variable
 exit
 endif

Add a shared helper in readgridlist.F90:

subroutine lowercase_inplace(text)
  implicit none
  character(len=*),intent(inout) :: text
  integer :: i,c

  do i=1,len_trim(text)
 c = iachar(text(i:i))
 if(c.ge.iachar(’A’).and.c.le.iachar(’Z’)) then
 text(i:i) = achar(c + iachar(’a’) - iachar(’A’))
 endif
  enddo
end subroutine lowercase_inplace

 574

Apply the same normalized comparison in each query routine. Combining this with the found/required
API from READGRIDLIST-004 makes case mistakes produce either a valid match or a clear missing-key
error.

Git evidence: cb6a126 (2026-07-23, case-insensitive gridlist keys).
Gridlist key matching was made case-insensitive by lowercasing the lookup text before comparison.

BUG-2026-07-096: SENSORS-008: Sensor path buffers can truncate
valid file names

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Jul23/SENSORS-008.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ variables_sense.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ rinit_sense.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ sensors.F90

sensorfile allows 260 characters, but sensorlocs and the local derived filename buffers are shorter:

character(len=260) :: sensorfile = ’sensor’
character(len=60) :: sensorlocs = ’sensorlocs.txt’

character(len=200) :: sensorFileName
...

inquire(file=trim(sensorFileName)//’.csv’, exist = exists)

sensors_write repeats the same 200-character buffer:

character(len=200) :: sensorFileName
...
call namefile(ni,sensorfile,sensorFileName)

Problem
A user can provide a sensorfile value that fits the module variable but not the local sensorFileName
used to hold the suffixed path. namefile appends .<sensor number>, and the caller then appends .csv, so
a path much shorter than 260 can still overflow the 200-character local buffer.
Likewise, sensorlocs is only 60 characters, so location-file paths that are valid elsewhere in the codebase
can be truncated before the open.
Fortran character assignment truncates silently. The result is an open of the wrong path, an unexpected
file prefix collision, or a failure that does not point back to the real input path.

Use one larger sensor path length consistently. If the project has a shared path-length constant, use
that instead of introducing a local parameter.

diff --git a/CODE-dev/Sensors/variables_sense.F90 b/CODE-dev/Sensors/variables_sense.F90

 ,→ Z locations for all sensors - must be tab-delimited
+ character(len=512) :: sensorfile = ’sensor’ ! Name of the sensor output files
+ character(len=512) :: sensorlocs = ’sensorlocs.txt’ ! File that contains X, Y, and Z locations for
 ,→ all sensors

- character(len=200) :: sensorFileName
+ character(len=512) :: sensorFileName

+++ b/CODE-dev/Sensors/sensors.F90
@@
- character(len=200) :: sensorFileName
+ character(len=512) :: sensorFileName

For a stricter fix, check len_trim(sensorfile) before calling namefile and stop with a clear error if the
final .<id>.csv path will not fit.
