BUG-2026-08-001: POST-001: the no-emission state passes the
wrong xvrho section to thermodynamics

,→ POST-001-zero-emission-state-passes-invalid-species-section.md

• Defect: confirmed invalid argument association and component-index bug
• Relevance to the reported wind symptom: high; it occurs on the first timestep, before the
  heat-source forcing is reached, and can become allocation-layout sensitive when heat input is enabled
• Static-only conclusion: the heat source is not the direct writer in this path, but enabling it
  changes the input/allocation path around this invalid call

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul24/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.
   ,→ F90:146-165
• CODE-dev/definearray.F90:67-115
• CODE-dev/domainUpdates.F90:27-61,83-126
• CODE-dev/thermodynamics.F90:5-29
• CODE-dev/input.F90:272-285
• Trace: .ai_trace/EXECUTION_PHASE_DETAILS.md phase 6 and phase 8; .ai_trace/ROUTINE_DEPENDENCIES.md
  entries for implicit_domain_updates and explicit_domain_updates
• Trial controls: 01–14, 15–24, 31, 34–38

When emissions are disabled, the species-property arrays are never allocated:

! input.F90

The dynamic component indexes start with these defaults:

! variables.F90
integer :: iEmitStart=1,iEmitStop=1

For the original gridlist, iturb=2, so xvpointers assigns the transported components as u=1, v=2, w=3
,→ , theta=4, ka=5, kb=6, and rho=7. Because iemissions=0, the emission-index block is skipped, leaving
iEmitStart=iEmitStop=1. The first domain update then unconditionally does:

call updateGasThermProps(xvrho(i,j,k,iEmitStart:iEmitStop), &
  cpEmit,mwEmit,nEmit,xvrho(i,j,k,itheta),xv(i,j,k,irho), &
  cp_gas(i,j,k),cv_gas(i,j,k),mw_gas(i,j,k),pr(i,j,k),tempg(i,j,k))

The callee declares all three species arguments with extent nEmit:

real(wp),intent(in) :: yEmit(nEmit),cpEmit(nEmit),mwEmit(nEmit)

 582

Problem
For the supplied no-emission input, the actual yEmit section is component 1:1, which is the resolved u
field, while the dummy extent is nEmit=0. At the same call, cpEmit and mwEmit are unallocated. This is
not a valid zero-length species state; it is a shape-mismatched call that also associates unallocated
arrays with ordinary array dummies.
The iemissions=2, nEmit=0 trial controls (23 and 24) are not clean controls either. In that configuration
iEmitStart becomes the next component index, but iEmitStop remains its default value. With iturb=2,
the resulting section is effectively xvrho(...,7:1) even though the last xvrho component is 6. The
zero-species allocation alone does not repair the component bounds.
updateGasThermProps  is called in explicit_domain_updates before small_explicit_forcings, MOA, and
large_explicit_forcings. Thus it can produce invalid thermodynamic fields before the heat routine
is called. The pressure residual is converted directly into all three momentum forcings by gradmoa,
including iwvel.
This defect exists with heat off too. It explains why the heat-on symptom can be compiler-, allocation-,
or restart-layout-sensitive rather than proving that a dormant heat source physically generated the
initial wind. The clean behavior of cases 15–22, which supply a real O2 species and valid component
bounds, is consistent with this diagnosis.

Do not pass a velocity component or an out-of-range section when nEmit=0. Use a valid zero-size
temporary for all three no-species arguments in both domain update routines. This also avoids passing
unallocated cpEmit and mwEmit in the iemissions=0 case.

BUG-2026-08-002: POST-002: initialization and the first
thermodynamic update use different ambient gases

,→ POST-002-ambient-mixture-changes-at-first-thermo-update.md

• Defect: confirmed equation-of-state inconsistency
• Relevance to the reported wind symptom: high; it creates a pressure residual before the heat
  source is evaluated, and gradmoa turns that residual into horizontal and vertical momentum forcing
• Heat-source specificity: not intrinsic; the heat option can expose or amplify the error through
  the invalid/allocation-sensitive path in POST-001

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul24/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
 ,→ :97-199
• CODE-dev/thermodynamics.F90:5-29
• CODE-dev/domainUpdates.F90:48-61,113-126
• CODE-dev/higrad.F90:67-142
• CODE-dev/compress.F90:40-79
• Trace: .ai_trace/EXECUTION_PHASE_DETAILS.md phases 6 and 8
• Trial controls: 01–14, 23–29, 31, 34–38 versus explicit-O2 cases 15–22

setRhoThetaP initializes the atmosphere using an H2O/O2/N2 mixture. With the trial defaults
(relativeHumidity=0), the relevant part is:

yH2O = specificHumidity
yO2 = 0.233_wp/(specificHumidity+1.0_wp)
yN2 = 1.0_wp-yH2O-yO2
cpGas = yH2O*1996.0_wp+yO2*918.0_wp+yN2*1040.0_wp
mwGas = yH2O*18.015_wp+yO2*31.998_wp+yN2*28.014_wp

Those cpGas and mwGas values are used to construct pre, rho, and theta.
The first timestep then calls updateGasThermProps, whose no-emission path is:

real(wp) :: cp_N2=1040.0_wp
real(wp) :: MW_N2=28.014_wp

cp_gas=sum(cpEmit*yEmit)+cp_N2*(1._wp-sum(yEmit))
mw_gas=sum(mwEmit*yEmit)+MW_N2*(1._wp-sum(yEmit))

With no tracked species, that reconstructs the gas as pure N2. The resulting pr is compared against
the initialization-time pre in gradmoa:

pr_local=(xvtmp(i,j,k,itheta)*rg_over_prrcp_gas)** &

 586

  (cp_gas(i,j,k)/cv_gas(i,j,k))-pre(i,j,k)

The residual is differentiated and applied to all three momentum components, including:

forceSI_xv(i,j,k,iwvel)=forceSI_xv(i,j,k,iwvel)-g33*pz(i,j,k)

Problem
For zero humidity, initialization uses approximately

cp_initial = 0.233*918 + 0.767*1040 = 1011.574 J/(kg K)
mw_initial = 0.233*31.998 + 0.767*28.014 = 28.942272 kg/kmol

The first update instead uses cp=1040 and mw=28.014. The same state is therefore interpreted with a
different equation of state immediately after initialization. Even if the transported fields have not
changed, the pressure residual is nonzero; terrain metrics, vertical variation, and any perturbation turn
that residual into a spatially varying wind forcing.
The original cases and cases 01–14 leave emissions disabled, while cases 15–22 explicitly transport O2 and
were reported as clean. That is consistent with the mismatch being an important common-mode driver
in the original matrix. It does not prove that this common-mode error alone explains the heat-only
portion of the symptom; POST-001 explains why the heat-on and heat-off versions can manifest it
differently.

Use the same ambient mixture in the no-emission branch. The long-term safer fix is to put the
composition calculation in one shared routine and call it from both initialization and thermodynamic
updates; this small diff keeps the change local.

diff --git a/CODE-dev/thermodynamics.F90 b/CODE-dev/thermodynamics.F90

BUG-2026-08-003: POST-003: a dormant heat source still enters the
timestep routine and allocates saved state

,→ POST-003-dormant-heatsource-call-allocates-saved-state.md

• Defect: confirmed unnecessary pre-activation side effect
• Relevance to the reported wind symptom: medium-to-high as an indirect allocation-layout
  trigger; the inactive branch does not intentionally write force, but it changes the heat-on execution
  path before the first update
• Static-only conclusion: allocation by itself is not proof of wind corruption. In combination with
  POST-001’s invalid calls, it is a plausible reason the same physical controls manifest differently
  when heat is enabled.

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul24/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/force.F90
   ,→ :129-155
• CODE-dev/HeatSource/heatsource_heat.F90:98-143
• CODE-dev/HeatSource/input_heat.F90:16-128
• CODE-dev/compress.F90:69-82
• Trace: .ai_trace/EXECUTION_PHASE_MAP.md phases 6, 9, and 10; .ai_trace/ROUTINE_DEPENDENCIES.md entry
  for heatsource
• Trial evidence: 34/35 and 38, where the heat source starts at 1000 s but the reported difference
  develops around comp 40 (about 4 s)

The large-step forcing routine calls the heat routine whenever the option is enabled, without checking
whether any source has reached its start time:

! force.F90:153-155
if(iheatsource.ge.1) &
  call heatSource(iheatsource, &
    forceLE_xv(1:np,1:mp,:,:),1,np,1,mp,l,nv)

At entry, heatSource allocates two save arrays before checking the source activity gate:

logical, save, allocatable :: heatsource_logged(:)
logical, save, allocatable :: heatsource_off_logged(:)

if(.not.allocated(heatsource_logged)) then
  allocate(heatsource_logged(nsource_hs))
  heatsource_logged = .false.
endif
if(.not.allocated(heatsource_off_logged)) then
  allocate(heatsource_off_logged(nsource_hs))
  heatsource_off_logged = .false.

 590

endif

Only after those allocations does the inactive branch test time and cycle:

heatsource_active = time.ge.starttime_hs(itsource) .and. &
  time.lt.endtime_hs(itsource)
...
else
  ...
  cycle
endif

Problem
For the original source (starttime_hs=100) and dormant controls with starttime_hs=1000, the heat-enabled
job enters heatSource on its first large step even though no source can apply heat. The heat-off job
does not enter this routine and does not allocate these arrays. The two jobs therefore have different
allocation histories before the same invalid thermodynamic calls and pressure solve run.
The current inactive branch does not write force after the gate, so this is not a claim that the two
logical arrays directly create w. It is an avoidable heat-only side effect that makes undefined behavior
elsewhere allocation- sensitive. The reported early divergence in dormant cases 34/35 and 38 is why
this path remains relevant even though the configured physical source is not active.

Do not enter the heat routine until at least one source has reached its start time. Once the first source
has started, continue calling it so finite end times can still produce the deactivation log.

BUG-2026-08-004: POST-004: heatSource receives a noncontiguous
forcing section as contiguous storage

,→ POST-004-heatsource-passes-noncontiguous-force-section.md

• Defect: confirmed unsafe external-procedure argument association
• Relevance to the reported wind symptom: high; when the source is active, the wrong assumed
  strides can place a theta forcing in a velocity component, including w
• Dormant relevance: the invalid call is made even before activation, so the same ABI/temporary
  behavior can also alter a dormant heat-on control

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul24/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/definearray.
   ,→ F90:18-33
• CODE-dev/force.F90:129-155
• CODE-dev/HeatSource/heatsource_heat.F90:68-86,313-365
• CODE-dev/compress.F90:69-82
• CODE-dev/CMakeLists.txt:10-21
• Trace: .ai_trace/EXECUTION_PHASE_DETAILS.md phase 9 and .ai_trace/CALLERS_BY_ROUTINE.md entry for
 heatsource
• Trial evidence: 30 (activation at 2 s), 31 (active zero-flux call), and dormant cases 34–38

The global forcing array includes horizontal halo cells:

allocate(forceLE_xv(1-ih:np+ih,1-ih:mp+ih,l,nv))

The heat caller strips those halos by passing a section:

if(iheatsource.ge.1) &
  call heatSource(iheatsource, &
    forceLE_xv(1:np,1:mp,:,:),1,np,1,mp,l,nv)

heatSource is a standalone external routine and declares the dummy with an explicit shape:

...
real(wp),intent(inout) :: force(il:iu,jl:ju,lls,nv)

When the source is active, it writes the thermal component:

force(i,j,k,itheta)=force(i,j,k,itheta)+fi

The component indexes are u=1, v=2, w=3, and theta=4.

 594

Problem
forceLE_xv(1:np,1:mp,:,:) is not contiguous in memory because the parent array’s first two dimensions
include halos. For the supplied decomposition, np=12, mp=25, and ih=1; the parent plane is 14 x 27, while
the dummy assumes a contiguous 12 x 25 plane. Therefore the dummy’s stride from one j value to the
next is 12 elements, but the parent section’s physical stride is 14 elements. The mismatch continues for
the vertical and component strides.
Because the call is to an external routine with no explicit interface, the caller/callee have no shared
descriptor that reliably communicates the section’s strides. A compiler-generated copy-in/copy-out
temporary may hide the problem; passing the section’s base address directly makes the callee’s intended
theta writes land at the wrong addresses. In that case a source thermal write can become a force
on component 3 (w) or another neighboring component. The subsequent forcing loop applies every
component directly to xv, so the corruption appears as an anomalous wind.
The call is also made for a dormant source. The cycle in heatSource prevents the later force writes,
 but it cannot make the original invalid argument association valid. This is why dormant heat-on
 cases can still be sensitive to compiler and allocation behavior. The permissive GNU build flag
-fallow-argument-mismatch does not repair the storage-stride contract.

Pass the contiguous full allocation and declare the dummy with the same halo bounds. The existing
loops still use i=1:np and j=1:mp, so no halo cell is intentionally heated.

@@
 if(iheatsource.ge.1) &
 call heatSource(iheatsource, &
-      forceLE_xv(1:np,1:mp,:,:),1,np,1,mp,l,nv)
+      forceLE_xv,1,np,1,mp,l,nv)

@@
- use gridlist_variables, only : dx,dy,wp
+ use gridlist_variables, only : dx,dy,wp,ih
@@
- real(wp),intent(inout) :: force(il:iu,jl:ju,lls,nv)
+ real(wp),intent(inout) :: force(1-ih:np+ih,1-ih:mp+ih,lls,nv)

The stronger structural fix is to put heatSource in a module and use an assumed-shape dummy with an
explicit interface. That would allow a deliberately noncontiguous section to be passed safely, but the
diff above is the smallest change that removes the current stride mismatch.

Git evidence: 561333f (2026-08-01, heat-source, no-emission, and O2 fixes).
heatSource now receives the full halo-shaped forcing array rather than a noncontiguous interior section
masquerading as contiguous storage.

BUG-2026-08-005: POST-005: radiation uses the u wind component
as oxygen when O2 is not tracked

,→ POST-005-radiation-uses-u-as-oxygen-when-o2-is-untracked.md

• Defect: confirmed dynamic-index alias
• Relevance to the reported wind symptom: secondary radiation amplifier; it cannot explain a
  difference with radiation disabled, but it can make a heat-correlated temperature error feed back
  into wind in irad=2 cases

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_Jul24/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.
   ,→ F90:158-165
• CODE-dev/definearray.F90:67-109
• CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90:62-136
• CODE-dev/force.F90:78-117
• CODE-dev/Radiation/variables_rad.F90:5-18
• Trial controls: 01/02, 03/04, 09/10, and explicit-O2 cases 19–22

The component indexes are initialized by aliasing optional fields to component 1:

integer :: iuvel=1,ivvel=1,iwvel=1
integer :: itheta=1,ika=1,ikb=1,iO2=1,iH2O=1,irho=1

xvpointers changes iO2 only if a tracked species is named O2:

if(spEmit(i).eq.’O2’) iO2=iEmitStart-1+i

With the original gridlist, emissions are disabled, so iO2 remains 1, which is u. The Monte Carlo
radiation code then reads it as oxygen:

aemit=rmaxsootcon*xv(i,j,kcell,irho)* &
  sqrt(max(0.233_wp-xvrho(i,j,kcell,iO2),0._wp)/0.233_wp)

The alternate soot model has the same alias in its O2-deficit expression. force.F90 calls this routine for
irad=2 through the Monte Carlo branch.

Problem
Radiation absorption and emission are being inferred from horizontal wind speed, not oxygen mass
fraction. Whenever the local u value is below the 0.233 reference, the code fabricates an oxygen deficit.
That changes papvgas, then the radiation source and theta forcing, and finally the pressure-derived

 597

wind. The value can vary near boundaries or after an upstream wind error, making the result spatially
strange and decomposition-sensitive.
This is not the primary explanation for the radiation-off failures in cases 05/06 and 11/12. It is still
a confirmed bug relevant to the normal radiation cases. The explicit-O2 controls 19–22 provide the
appropriate diagnostic comparison because they assign iO2 to a real transported species.

Use an invalid sentinel for an absent optional component and fall back to the ambient O2 mass fraction
in radiation.

Problem
When restarting dense sensor mode, rinitXeVariation tries to skip to the records around the restart time.

BUG-2026-08-007: XEVARIATION-010: Sensor Distance Uses Local
MPI Indices Instead Of Global Coordinates

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Aug5/XEVARIATION-010.md

• xeVariation/xevariation.F90
• rinit.F90

! rinit.F90
34 do i=1-ih,n+ih
35    x(i)=(i-1)*dx-((n+1)/2._wp-1)*dx
36 enddo
37 do j=1-ih,m+ih
38    y(j)=(j-1)*dy-((m+1)/2._wp-1)*dy
39 enddo

! xeVariation/xevariation.F90
114      do k=1,lfuel
115        do j=1,mp
116          do i=1,np
...

120                ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2.0_wp+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2.0_wp)

! xeVariation/xevariation.F90
176 do kv=1,nSensors
177              senw(kv)=sqrt((time-senDataNew(kv,1))**2.0_wp+ &
178                ((i-1)*dx-SensorX(kv))**2.0_wp+((j-1)*dy-SensorY(kv))**2.0_wp)

Problem
The sensor modes compute sensor distance from local subdomain indices i and j. On MPI ranks where
npos > 1 or mpos > 1, local cell (1,1) is not global cell (1,1), but the distance calculation treats it that
way.
That makes sparse and dense sensor interpolation spatially wrong on all but the lower-left MPI
subdomain. Sensors can influence the wrong parts of the global domain, and the same local cell index
on different ranks can receive the same sensor weight even though those cells are far apart globally.

Use global indices when computing physical sensor distances. The subroutine already imports npos and
mpos and already uses ia/ja for windfield boundaries, so reuse those variables in the sensor paths.

BUG-2026-08-008: XEVARIATION-011: Dense Sensor Records
Advance One Large Step Too Early

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Aug5/XEVARIATION-011.md

• compress.F90
• MOA.F90
• xeVariation/xevariation.F90

! compress.F90
34 do while(ittot.lt.nt)
35 ittot=it+itrestart
...
41 call explicit_domain_updates ! Updates environmental variables (pressure, etc.)
...

! MOA.F90
52 time=time+dts

! xeVariation/xevariation.F90
162    case (4)
163 if(mod(ittot,freqSensor).eq.0) then
164 senDataOld = senDataNew
165 do kv=1,nSensors
166          read(4884+kv,*) senDataNew(kv,1),senDataNew(kv,2), &
167 senDataNew(kv,3),senDataNew(kv,4)

Problem
explicit_domain_updates calls xevariation before MOA advances time. At loop iteration ittot=N, the model
time used by dense sensor interpolation is still the start-of-step time, approximately (N-1)*dt.
Dense sensor mode advances its input files using mod(ittot,freqSensor). Therefore, when ittot=freqSensor
,→ , it shifts from the initial [0, freqSensor] bracket to [freqSensor, 2*freqSensor] even though time is
still one large step before the first sensor datum endpoint.
The interpolation then uses future sensor data too early.

Advance dense sensor records based on the sensor timestamp that is already stored in the data file,
not the loop counter. Keep reading while the current model time has passed the current senDataNew
timestamp.

BUG-2026-08-009: XEVARIATION-019: Fire Restarts Use The
Simulated Field As The Old Windfield Target

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-completed-Aug5/XEVARIATION-019.md

Problem
For irst==1, rinit reads a fire restart into xv before rinitXeVariation runs. Windfield input then seeds
xvdataold from that simulated solution.
xvdataold is supposed to be the old environmental windfield target for boundary interpolation. The
simulated boundary state can differ from that target because the model only relaxes toward xe; it is not
guaranteed to equal the windfield file. After a fire restart, the boundary forcing therefore interpolates
from the current model state to the next windfield file instead of from the previous windfield file to the
next windfield file.
This can create a restart-only discontinuity or drift in windfield boundary conditions.

 610

On fire restarts, read the old windfield boundary file into xvdataold instead of copying xv. A clean
implementation is to factor windfld_read so it can fill either xvdatanew or a caller-provided destination.

BUG-2026-08-010: updateSolidThermProps divides by
rhoFuel + rhoWater without a mass guard

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/004_updateSolidThermProps_divides_by_zero_fuel_mass.md

Symptom
Temps can become NaN, Inf, or extremely large if a fuel cell has zero or near-zero total solid mass but
still reaches updateSolidThermProps.
This is not the strongest explanation for the shown timestep-2 printout because the printed rhoFuel
and rhoWater ranges are positive. It is still a real bug in the same temperature path and can produce
the same kind of bad RMAXMIN for Temps output later in a run or under different fuel input.

Cause
thermodynamics.F90 computes:

cpsolid=(rhoFuel*cpwood+rhoWater*cpwater)/(rhoFuel+rhoWater)
temps=sies/cpsolid

There is no guard for rhoFuel + rhoWater <= 0. Some initialization paths set xvfuel(...,isies)=0.0_wp
when total fuel mass is zero, but the later recompute path does not repeat that protection.

Return a benign temperature when no solid mass exists:

diff --git a/thermodynamics.F90 b/thermodynamics.F90
@@
 subroutine updateSolidThermProps(rhoFuel,rhoWater,sies,temps)

 use vegetation_gridlist_variables, only : cpwood
+ use fuel_variables, only : min_rhoFuel
 use thermo_variables, only : cpwater
@@
 ! Executable Code
+ if(rhoFuel + rhoWater .le. min_rhoFuel)then
+    temps = 0.0_wp
+ return
+ endif
 cpsolid=(rhoFuel*cpwood+rhoWater*cpwater)/(rhoFuel+rhoWater)
 temps=sies/cpsolid

If 0.0 K is undesirable for downstream physics, use ambient gas temperature at the caller instead. The
important part is to avoid computing solid heat capacity from a zero denominator.

Why this matters
The code already has a min_rhoFuel floor in vegetation initialization and fuel limits, which suggests the
model expects very small solid mass to be special-cased. The thermodynamics helper should enforce
the same invariant because it is called from both explicit_domain_updates and implicit_domain_updates.

 614

Git evidence: 16d97bb (2026-08-11, solid-temperature mass guard and double-precision I/O work).
The committed implementation differs from the suggested early-return patch: CODE-dev/thermodynamics.
,→ F90 imports tolerance and computes cpsolid with rhoFuel+rhoWater+tolerance in the denominator.

BUG-2026-08-011: IO-002: Restart timestep parsing only works for
filenames containing out.

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/IO-002.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/io.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/input.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/compress.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90

The output prefix and restart filename are user-configurable:

character(len=257) :: outname = ’comp.out’ ! Name of output files
character(len=257) :: restartfile = ’’ ! Name of restart file

call QueryGridlist_string (’outname’,outname,48)
call QueryGridlist_string (’restartfile’,restartfile,48)

binary_writeio writes files as <outname>.<ittot>:

write(fend,"(i0)") ittot
it=index(outname,’␣’)
fname=outname(1:it-1)//’.’//fend

But irstreadio derives itrestart by looking specifically for the first out. substring:

idot=index(restartfile,’out.’)+4
iend=len_trim(restartfile)
read(restartfile(idot:iend),*) itrestart

rinit then uses that parsed value to set simulation time:

if(irst.eq.1) call irstreadio

time=itrestart*dts*nts

Problem
The restart parser is coupled to the default comp.out.N naming pattern even though outname is config-
urable.
Examples that fail or parse the wrong substring:

 616

• outname = ’./restart/run’ writes ./restart/run.4000, but index(restartfile,’out.’) returns 0 and the
  code tries to read from character 4 of the path.
• A directory containing out., such as ./old.out.files/comp.out.4000, matches the directory component
  first and attempts to parse files/comp.out.4000.
• Any prefix that does not contain out. cannot be restarted even if it was produced by binary_writeio.

Because itrestart controls ittot and time, a bad parse can either abort the restart or resume at the
wrong timestep.

Parse the integer suffix after the last period in restartfile, which matches the way binary_writeio
appends .<ittot> regardless of the prefix.

+++ b/CODE-dev/io.F90
@@
- integer :: idot,iend
+ integer :: idot,iend,ios
@@
- idot=index(restartfile,’out.’)+4
 iend=len_trim(restartfile)
- read(restartfile(idot:iend),*) itrestart
+ idot=index(restartfile(:iend),’.’,back=.true.)
+ if(idot.le.0.or.idot.ge.iend)then
+ if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’ERROR: restartfile must end with .<timestep>: ’, &
+ trim(restartfile)
+ STOP
+ endif
+ read(restartfile(idot+1:iend),*,iostat=ios) itrestart
+ if(ios.ne.0)then
+ if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’ERROR: could not parse timestep from restartfile: ’, &
+ trim(restartfile)
+ STOP
+ endif

This keeps the existing comp.out.4000 behavior while allowing any valid output prefix.

Git evidence: fd65110 (2026-08-11, metric/MOA fixes and fuel limits); ee12db0 (2026-08-14, restart
bad-value parser fix).
Restart timestep parsing was changed to use the last dot in the restart filename, then fixed to read
after that dot with idot+1; this supports restart names beyond the old out. convention.

BUG-2026-08-012: MOA-004: Fuel limits are applied with a 4-D
limiter to 5-D fuel arrays

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/MOA-004.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/MOA.F90

The fuel state and fuel forcing arrays include fuel type as their first dimension:

nfuel is a gridlist option and can be greater than one:

! Vegetation/input_veg.F90
13 call QueryGridlist_integer(’nfuel’,nfuel,48)

But forcingLimits is a 4-D limiter:

! force.F90
45 subroutine forcingLimits(xv,xvLimits,il,iu,jl,ju,lls,nvp)
...
51 real(wp),intent(inout) :: xv(il:iu,jl:ju,lls,nvp)
52 real(wp),intent(in) :: xvLimits(2,nvp)
...
56   do kv=1,nvp
57 do i=il,iu
58 do j=jl,ju
59          do k=1,lls
60 xv(i,j,k,kv)=max(xvLimits(1,kv),min(xvLimits(2,kv), &
61              xv(i,j,k,kv)))

MOA passes the 5-D xvfueltmp array to that 4-D limiter:

! MOA.F90
94 xvfueltmp=xvfueltmp+forceSE_xvfuel*dts

 619

95 xvfueltmp=xvfueltmp+forceSI_xvfuel*dts

The final large-step fuel update has the same shape mismatch:

! force.F90
37 xvfuel=xvfuel+forceLE_xvfuel*dt
38 call forcingLimits(xvfuel,xvfuelLim,1,np,1,mp,lfuel,nvfuel)

Problem
This only works accidentally when nfuel == 1. When nfuel > 1, the actual array layout is:

xvfuel(ift,i,j,k,kv)

but the limiter walks the memory as if it were:

xv(i,j,k,kv)

Because these routines are external procedures without explicit interfaces, the rank mismatch can
compile. At runtime the limiter then interprets the fuel-type dimension as part of the x-index
dimension. The loop bounds cover only np*mp*lfuel*nvfuel elements, while the actual fuel array contains
nfuel*np*mp*lfuel*nvfuel elements.
Consequences for multi-fuel runs include:

• some fuel types and cells are never clipped to xvfuelLim;
• some elements are clipped using the wrong variable’s bounds;
• rhoFuel, rhoWater, sies, or psiw can remain negative or exceed their intended limits after MOA small
  steps;
• the final large-step fuel state can have the same corruption because force.F90 repeats the same call
  pattern.

This directly affects MOA because xvfueltmp is the fuel state used by small-step convection, evaporation,
burning, emissions, and solid-temperature updates.

Add a fuel-specific limiter with the correct 5-D shape and call it for fuel arrays.

+++ b/CODE-dev/force.F90

BUG-2026-08-013: RADIATION-002: Monte Carlo convergence
compares neighboring cells instead of iterations

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-002.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90

montecarlo stores the old absorption percentage in a scalar and overwrites it while walking the grid:

maxpercabsdiff=1.0_wp
percabsAZnew=0.0_wp
do while(maxpercabsdiff.gt.accuracythreshold) ! loop for dynamic allocation of photons
  call shoot_photons
  nphottot=nphottot+nphotbatch
  iternum=iternum+1
  maxpercabsdiff=0.0_wp
  do k=1,lmc
 do j=1,m
 do i=1,n
 percabsAZold=percabsAZnew
 percabsAZnew=nphotonAZ(i,j,k)/nphottot
 maxpercabsdiff=max(maxpercabsdiff,percabsAZnew-percabsAZold)
 enddo
 enddo
  enddo
enddo

Each MPI rank decides loop termination locally, then computes its own photon energy:

Qphot=Etot/nphottot

Problem
percabsAZold is not the previous-iteration value for the same cell. It is just the previous scalar value
from the last cell visited in the loop. This makes the stopping condition depend on spatial ordering
and cell-to-cell differences, not convergence between photon batches.
The loop also never performs an MPI max reduction on the convergence metric. Different ranks can
take a different number of Monte Carlo batches, giving different nphottot and therefore different Qphot
values on different ranks before the final absorbed-photon reduction.
Consequences:

• the Monte Carlo solve can stop too early or run longer for the wrong reason.
• rank-local stopping can make radiative heating/cooling inconsistent across subdomains.
• the final Qphot can differ by MPI rank even though Etot is global.

 623

Store the previous absorption fraction per cell, compare with abs, and reduce the local maximum across
ranks each iteration.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@
- use msga_variables, only : mpi_rank,mpi_integer,mpi_sum, &
+ use msga_variables, only : mpi_rank,mpi_integer,mpi_sum,mpi_max, &
 mpi_comm_world,ierror
+ use msga_variables, only : mpi_wp
@@
- real(wp) :: maxpercabsdiff
+ real(wp) :: maxpercabsdiff,maxpercabsdiffLocal
 real(wp) :: Qphot
- real(wp) :: percabsAZold,percabsAZnew
 real(wp) :: accuracythreshold=5.e-5_wp
+ real(wp),allocatable :: percabsAZold(:,:,:),percabsAZnew(:,:,:)
@@
 call allocate_photons
+ allocate(percabsAZold(n,m,lmc),percabsAZnew(n,m,lmc))
+ percabsAZnew = 0.0_wp

 if(iradeastflux.eq.1) accuracythreshold=1.e-5_wp
@@
- percabsAZnew=0.0_wp
 do while(maxpercabsdiff.gt.accuracythreshold) ! loop for dynamic allocation of photons
+ percabsAZold = percabsAZnew
 call shoot_photons
 nphottot=nphottot+nphotbatch
 iternum=iternum+1
- maxpercabsdiff=0.0_wp
-    do k=1,lmc
- do j=1,m
- do i=1,n
- percabsAZold=percabsAZnew
- percabsAZnew=nphotonAZ(i,j,k)/nphottot
- maxpercabsdiff=max(maxpercabsdiff,percabsAZnew-percabsAZold)

+ percabsAZnew=real(nphotonAZ(:,:,1:lmc),kind=wp)/ &
+ real(nphottot,kind=wp)
+ maxpercabsdiffLocal=maxval(abs(percabsAZnew-percabsAZold))
+ call mpi_allreduce(maxpercabsdiffLocal,maxpercabsdiff,1,mpi_wp, &
+ mpi_max,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
 enddo ! do while (maxpercabsdiff.gt.accuracythreshold) dynamic allocation
@@
 call updateRadArrays(Qphot)
+ deallocate(percabsAZold,percabsAZnew)

This preserves the existing convergence threshold while making the comparison actually mean "change
since the previous batch" and keeping all ranks synchronized.

 624

Monte Carlo convergence now compares per-cell absorption between iterations using old/new arrays
and a max absolute change reduction, rather than comparing neighboring cells within one iteration.

BUG-2026-08-014: RADIATION-003: Photon batch splitting drops
or over-assigns photons

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-003.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90

allocate_photons divides a batch across MPI ranks:

nperproc(:)=nphotbatch/numprocs
n2=MOD(nphotbatch,numprocs)
nperproc(0:n2-1)=nperproc(0:n2-1)+n2

It then maps each rank’s global photon range onto emitting cells:

mypstrt=SUM(nperproc(0:mpi_rank-1))+1
mypstp =mypstrt+nperproc(mpi_rank)-1
icpt=0
do k=1,lmc
  do j=1,m
 do i=1,n
 icptold=icpt
 icpt=icpt+int(nphotemisAZ(i,j,k))
 if(icptold.le.mypstrt)then
 if(icpt.ge.mypstp)then ! All photons go here
 nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=mypstp-mypstrt+1
 else ! Only some photons go here
 nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=icpt-mypstrt+1
 endif
 elseif(icptold.ge.mypstp)then
 if(icpt.ge.mypstp)then ! remainder of my photons go here
 nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=mypstp-icptold
 else ! icpt is less than mystp so only some of my remaining photons go here
 nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=icpt-icptold
 endif
 endif
 enddo
  enddo
enddo

Problem
There are two independent off-by-logic errors here.
First, the remainder distribution adds n2 to each of the first n2 ranks. It should add one. For example,
a remainder of 3 gives three ranks three extra photons each, creating 9 extra rank slots instead of 3.
Second, the cell/rank overlap test is wrong. A cell before a rank’s start can produce negative
nphotemisAZsplit values (icpt-mypstrt+1), and cells in the middle of a rank’s assigned range are skipped

 626

unless their icptold is still before mypstrt. For a rank with photon range 1:100 and emitting cells of 10
photons each, only the first cell receives photons; cells 2 through 10 are left at zero.
Consequences:

• many emitted photons are never shot.
• some ranks can be assigned too many photons when nphotbatch is not divisible by numprocs.
• nphottot is incremented by nphotbatch, but the actual number of photons shot can be much smaller
  or inconsistent.

Use a standard interval-overlap calculation between the cell’s global photon interval and the rank’s
assigned interval.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@
 integer :: n2
 integer :: mypstrt,mypstp
 integer :: icpt,icptold
+ integer :: cellFirst,cellLast,overlapFirst,overlapLast
@@
 nperproc(:)=nphotbatch/numprocs
 n2=MOD(nphotbatch,numprocs)
- nperproc(0:n2-1)=nperproc(0:n2-1)+n2
+ if(n2.gt.0) nperproc(0:n2-1)=nperproc(0:n2-1)+1
@@
 icptold=icpt
 icpt=icpt+int(nphotemisAZ(i,j,k))
- if(icptold.le.mypstrt)then
- if(icpt.ge.mypstp)then ! All photons go here
- nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=mypstp-mypstrt+1
- else ! Only some photons go here
- nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=icpt-mypstrt+1

- elseif(icptold.ge.mypstp)then
- if(icpt.ge.mypstp)then ! remainder of my photons go here
- nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=mypstp-icptold
- else ! icpt is less than mystp so only some of my remaining photons go here
- nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=icpt-icptold

+ cellFirst=icptold+1
+ cellLast=icpt
+ overlapFirst=max(cellFirst,mypstrt)
+ overlapLast=min(cellLast,mypstp)
+ if(overlapLast.ge.overlapFirst)then
+ nphotemisAZsplit(i,j,k)=overlapLast-overlapFirst+1
 endif

This still preserves the existing integer truncation of EAZ/Qphotbatch. A separate improvement would
reconcile nphottot with the actual integer photon count after truncation.

 627

Photon counts are now computed as integer per-AZ emissions, the actual batch size is recomputed
from that sum, and overlap start/stop ranges divide work without dropping or over-assigning photons.

BUG-2026-08-015: RADIATION-008: Monte Carlo radiation reuses
stale source terms when Etot < Emin

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-008.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90

firerad_MC refreshes the Monte Carlo radiation fields only when the global emitted energy is at least
Emin:

  call papv_defs ! define papvtotAZ,papvgas,papvtot
  call source_defs ! define sourcegas, sourcesol, EAZ, Etot, and lmc
  if(Etot.ge.Emin) call montecarlo
  do ift=1,nfuel
 write(iftname,"(i0)") ift
 call rmaxmin_3D(fsiesrad(ift,:,:,:),’fsiesrad_’//iftname, &
 il,iu,jl,ju,1,lfuel)
  enddo
  call rmaxmin_3D(firad,’firad’,il,iu,jl,ju,1,lls)
endif

The previously stored radiation fields are applied every call:

force(i,j,k)=force(i,j,k)+firad(i,j,k)/cp_gas(i,j,k)* &
  (pref/pr(i,j,k))**(1.0_wp-cv_gas(i,j,k)/cp_gas(i,j,k))

and for fuel:

force_fuel(ift,i,j,k)=force_fuel(ift,i,j,k)+ &
  fsiesrad(ift,i,j,k)/xvsolid(ift,i,j,k)

When source_defs finds too little energy, it only prints a diagnostic:

if(Etot.LT.Emin)then
  if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’Etot=’,Etot,’␣is␣neglected’
else
  lmc=5+nfuel

Problem
If a previous radiation update produced nonzero firad or fsiesrad, and a later radiation update has
Etot < Emin, montecarlo is skipped and updateRadArrays is never called. That leaves the old radiation
source terms in place.
The code then continues adding those stale terms to force and force_fuel, even though the current call

 629

explicitly decided the radiation energy should be neglected. A fire that cools below Emin can therefore
keep applying old radiative heating/cooling indefinitely until a later MC solve overwrites the arrays.

When the MC solve is skipped because energy is negligible, clear the radiation source arrays before
applying them.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@
 call papv_defs ! define papvtotAZ,papvgas,papvtot
 call source_defs ! define sourcegas, sourcesol, EAZ, Etot, and lmc

+ if(Etot.ge.Emin)then
+ call montecarlo
+ else
+      firad=0.0_wp
+ fsiesrad=0.0_wp
+ endif
 do ift=1,nfuel

If the intended behavior is to keep the last radiation field between scheduled MC calls, this still
preserves that behavior; it only clears the field on a scheduled radiation call that explicitly decides the
current radiation energy is negligible.

When total emitted energy is below Emin, the radiation source setup now returns cleanly so stale source
terms are not reused.

BUG-2026-08-016: RADIATION-012: Photon tracing can divide by
zero for RNG endpoint directions

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-012.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90

shoot_photons samples a direction directly from random_number:

call random_number(Rtheta)
call random_number(Rphi)
costheta=1.0_wp-2.0_wp*Rtheta
sintheta=sqrt(1.0_wp-costheta**2.0_wp)
phi=2.0_wp*pi*Rphi
dir(1)=sintheta*cos(phi)
dir(2)=sintheta*sin(phi)
dir(3)=costheta

It later divides by horizontal direction components:

if(dir(1).gt.0)then
  tx=(i1*dx-xf)/dir(1)
else
  tx=(i1*dx-dx-xf)/dir(1)
endif
if(dir(2).gt.0)then
  ty=(j1*dy-yf)/dir(2)
else
  ty=(j1*dy-dy-yf)/dir(2)
endif

The optical path length is sampled with:

call random_number(lopt)
lopt=-log(lopt)

Problem
Fortran’s random_number returns values in the interval 0 <= x < 1. Exact zero is allowed.
If Rtheta=0, then costheta=1, sintheta=0, and both horizontal direction components are zero. The code
then divides by dir(1) and dir(2) while computing tx and ty. If floating-point exceptions are enabled,
that can crash; otherwise it relies on infinities propagating benignly through min.
If lopt=0, -log(lopt) is infinite and can also raise a floating-point exception.
These endpoint cases are rare, but Monte Carlo radiation takes many random draws, so rare numerical
endpoints eventually become reproducibility and portability hazards.

 632

Clamp random samples away from zero where they are used in denominators/logs, and avoid dividing
by horizontal direction components that are effectively zero.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@
 call random_number(Rtheta)
 call random_number(Rphi)
+ Rtheta=max(tiny(Rtheta),min(1.0_wp-tiny(Rtheta),Rtheta))
 costheta=1.0_wp-2.0_wp*Rtheta
@@
 kt=0
 call random_number(lopt)
- lopt=-log(lopt)
+ lopt=-log(max(lopt,tiny(lopt)))
           do while(i1.ge.1.and.i1.le.n.and.j1.ge.1.and.j1.le.m.and. &
             k1.ge.1.and.k1.le.lmc.and.lopt.gt.0)
-            if(dir(1).gt.0)then
-              tx=(i1*dx-xf)/dir(1)
+ if(abs(dir(1)).le.tolerance)then
+ tx=huge(tx)
+ elseif(dir(1).gt.0)then
+              tx=(i1*dx-xf)/dir(1)
 else
               tx=(i1*dx-dx-xf)/dir(1)
 endif
-            if(dir(2).gt.0)then
-              ty=(j1*dy-yf)/dir(2)
+ if(abs(dir(2)).le.tolerance)then
+ ty=huge(ty)
+ elseif(dir(2).gt.0)then
+              ty=(j1*dy-yf)/dir(2)
 else
               ty=(j1*dy-dy-yf)/dir(2)
 endif

tiny preserves the random distribution for practical purposes while avoiding the exact endpoint values
that make the tracing math singular.

Photon tracing now transforms random optical length with -log(1-lopt) and guards endpoint directions
with tolerance-limited denominators.

BUG-2026-08-017: RADIATION-013: firerad_MC declares fuel arrays
with the gas-layer count

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-013.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/force.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/

force.F90 passes fuel arrays into firerad_MC:

  forceSE_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,isies), &
  xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof)+xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhow), &
  1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,1,np,1,mp,l,nfuel)

The last integer before nfuel is l, the number of gas layers.
Inside firerad_MC, that value is named lls and is used to declare both gas and fuel dummy arrays:

subroutine firerad_MC(force,force_fuel,xvsolid,ilh,iuh,jlh,juh, &
 il,iu,jl,ju,lls,nfuel)

  ...

  real(wp),intent(in) :: xvsolid(nfuel,il:iu,jl:ju,lls)

  real(wp),intent(inout) :: force_fuel(nfuel,il:iu,jl:ju,lls)

The fuel loops use lfuel, not lls:

  do j=jl,ju
 do i=il,iu
 do ift=1,nfuel

 fsiesrad(ift,i,j,k)/xvsolid(ift,i,j,k)

Problem
xvsolid and force_fuel are fuel-layer arrays. Their fourth dimension is lfuel, but firerad_MC declares
them with lls, which is passed as the gas-layer count l.
This creates a nonconforming interface whenever l /= lfuel. With the current external-subroutine
style, the caller may not catch the mismatch, but the dummy argument shape is still wrong:

• if bounds checking uses the dummy bounds, it checks fuel arrays against l, not lfuel;
• if lfuel > l, the loop can index beyond the dummy’s declared upper bound;

 635

• if an explicit interface is added later, this call can become a compile-time shape error;
• the declaration documents the wrong contract and makes future changes easy to break.

radiationSink already uses the safer pattern: gas arrays are dimensioned with lls, while fuel arrays are
dimensioned with lfuel.

Declare fuel dummy arrays with lfuel, matching the arrays passed from force.F90 and the loop bounds
used by firerad_MC.

+ real(wp),intent(inout) :: force_fuel(nfuel,il:iu,jl:ju,lfuel)

No caller change is needed because lfuel is already imported from fuel_variables in firerad_MC.

firerad_MC fuel arrays were changed to use the fuel-layer count rather than the gas-layer count.

BUG-2026-08-018: RADIATION-014: kfindex is used as both
fuel-rank and rank-to-fuel maps

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-014.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
   ,→ rinit_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ definearray_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ variables_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ solarHeat_veg.F90

rinit_rad.F90 sorts individual fuel depths into kfindex:

! sort individual fuel zones by afd
allocate(afdtmp(nfuel)); afdtmp = 0.0_wp
do j=1,mp
  do i=1,np
 afdtmp=actualFuelDepth(:,i,j)
 do k=1,nfuel
 kfindex(i,j,minloc(afdtmp,dim=1))=k
 afdtmp(minloc(afdtmp,dim=1))=maxval(actualFuelDepth(:,i,j))+1
 enddo
  enddo
enddo

This assignment stores the rank at the fuel-type index: kfindex(i,j,fuel_type)=rank.
The same array is then used as though kfindex(i,j,rank)=fuel_type when building AZ fuel-zone heights:

zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,i,j,k)=max(zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,i,j,k-1)+ &
  0.0001_wp,min(zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,i,j,nfuel+1)- &
  0.0001_wp*(1+nfuel-k),zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,i,j,0)+ &
  actualFuelDepth(kfindex(i,j,k),i,j)))

monteCarlo_rad.F90 uses it as fuel-type-to-rank:

if(kfindex(i,j,ift).ge.k.and. &
  xvfuel(ift,i,j,1,irhof).gt.min_rhoFuel)then
  papvift(ift,i,j,k)=2.0_wp/sizeScale(ift,i,j,1)* &
 xvfuel(ift,i,j,1,irhof)/(4.0_wp*rhoMicro)* &
 volumeAZ(i,j,k)/sum(volumeAZ(i,j,1:kfindex(i,j,ift)))

solarHeat_veg.F90 uses it as rank-to-fuel:

 638

LAIlocal(i,j,k)=sum(rhoFuel(kfindex(i,j,k:nfuel),i,j,1)/ &
  sizeScale(kfindex(i,j,k:nfuel),i,j,1)*zlayer/rhoMicro)

Problem
One array cannot safely represent both mappings.
For example, if three fuel types have depths [30, 10, 20], the current sort produces kfindex = [3, 1, 2],
meaning:

• fuel type 1 has rank 3
• fuel type 2 has rank 1
• fuel type 3 has rank 2

But the AZ geometry code reads kfindex(:,:,1) as the fuel type for rank 1, so it picks fuel type 3
instead of fuel type 2. The bottom-cell fuel-zone interfaces are placed at the wrong heights. Solar
LAI then sums the wrong fuel types above each AZ layer. Meanwhile the Monte Carlo projected-area
calculation relies on the opposite interpretation.
This corrupts radiation geometry and fuel optical-depth partitioning whenever the fuel depths are not
already in sorted fuel-type order.

Store both mappings explicitly: one array for rank -> fuel_type and one for fuel_type -> rank. Keep
kfindex as rank-to-fuel because geometry and solar LAI index sorted fuel layers directly, and add kfrank
for Monte Carlo bottom-layer distribution.

BUG-2026-08-019: RADIATION-015: zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,:,:,:) is
a non-contiguous MPI send buffer

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-015.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
   ,→ rinit_rad.F90

rinitrad stores four cell-corner height fields in the first dimension:

allocate(zCartEdgeAZLocal(4,np,mp,0:l+nfuel))

It then gathers one corner at a time:

allocate(zCartEdgeAZTmp(np,mp,0:l+nfuel,numprocs))
zCartEdgeAZTmp = 0.0_wp
do it=1,4
  nsize=np*mp*(l+nfuel+1)
  call mpi_allgather(zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,:,:,:),nsize,mpi_wp, &
 zCartEdgeAZTmp,nsize,mpi_wp,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
  do iprocx=1,nprocx
 do jprocy=1,nprocy
 iproc=1+(iprocx-1)+(jprocy-1)*nprocx
 do k=0,l+nfuel
 do j=1,mp
 do i=1,np
 ia=(iprocx-1)*np+i
 ja=(jprocy-1)*mp+j
 zCartEdgeAZGlobal(it,ia,ja,k)=zCartEdgeAZTmp(i,j,k,iproc)

Problem
Fortran arrays are column-major, so the first index is the fastest-varying dimension. Fixing the first
index in zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,:,:,:) leaves a strided, non-contiguous section.
The mpi_allgather call provides only a raw buffer and element count. Unless the compiler creates a
hidden contiguous temporary for this non-contiguous section, MPI will read contiguous memory starting
at zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,1,1,0), interleaving the other corner fields and potentially reading the wrong
values. Because this call has no explicit packing, behavior can change with compiler, optimization level,
MPI module/interface, or bounds-checking options.
The gathered zCartEdgeAZGlobal drives photon path intersections, so corrupted corner heights can send
photons through the wrong geometry.

Gather all four corner fields in one contiguous 4D buffer, then unpack the gathered result into the
global array.

 643

+ allocate(zCartEdgeAZTmp(4,np,mp,0:l+nfuel,numprocs))

- do it=1,4
- nsize=np*mp*(l+nfuel+1)
- call mpi_allgather(zCartEdgeAZLocal(it,:,:,:),nsize,mpi_wp, &
- zCartEdgeAZTmp,nsize,mpi_wp,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
- do iprocx=1,nprocx
- do jprocy=1,nprocy
- iproc=1+(iprocx-1)+(jprocy-1)*nprocx

- do j=1,mp
- do i=1,np
-               ia=(iprocx-1)*np+i

BUG-2026-08-020: RADIATION-017: Opacity threshold is

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-017.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/

source_defs computes the opacity threshold from the active fuel parameters:

  if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’Etot=’,Etot,’␣is␣neglected’

updateRadArrays uses a hard-coded threshold:

Problem
The two thresholds are meant to represent the same "optically active enough" cutoff, but only one of
them responds to the actual configuration.

• source_defs may include a layer in lmc because it is above the computed threshold, while
  updateRadArrays ignores absorption and solid tendencies because it is below the hard-coded threshold.
• updateRadArrays may apply absorption for layers that source_defs would not have considered optically
  active under the current fuel parameters.

That creates inconsistent photon-domain selection and energy deposition/removal, especially for
non-default vegetation size scales.

BUG-2026-08-021: RADIATION-018: Monte Carlo convergence
fraction is truncated by integer division

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-018.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90

montecarlo computes the absorbed-photon fraction in a real variable:

integer :: nphottot
real(wp) :: percabsAZold,percabsAZnew
...
do k=1,lmc
  do j=1,m
 do i=1,n
 percabsAZold=percabsAZnew
 percabsAZnew=nphotonAZ(i,j,k)/nphottot
 maxpercabsdiff=max(maxpercabsdiff,percabsAZnew-percabsAZold)
 enddo
  enddo
enddo

Both operands in the division are integers:

integer,allocatable :: nphotonAZ(:,:,:)
integer :: nphottot

Problem
Fortran evaluates nphotonAZ(i,j,k)/nphottot as integer division because both operands are integers. The
result is then converted to real(wp) only after truncation.
For almost all cells, nphotonAZ(i,j,k) < nphottot, so the computed fraction is exactly zero instead of a
small nonzero real value. A cell only reports 1.0 once it contains at least all photons shot by that rank,
which should not happen in normal Monte Carlo absorption statistics.
That makes maxpercabsdiff mostly insensitive to actual photon statistics and can terminate the dynamic
photon-batch loop after one iteration even when the absorbed distribution has not converged.
This is separate from the scalar old-value bug in RADIATION-002: even if the previous-iteration state is
stored correctly, this assignment still truncates the fraction unless at least one operand is explicitly
converted to real(wp).

Convert both numerator and denominator before dividing.

 649

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@
- percabsAZnew=nphotonAZ(i,j,k)/nphottot
+ percabsAZnew=real(nphotonAZ(i,j,k),kind=wp)/ &
+ real(nphottot,kind=wp)

If RADIATION-002 is fixed by switching to full percabsAZold(:,:,:) and percabsAZnew(:,:,:) arrays, make
the same conversion in the array expression:

- percabsAZnew=nphotonAZ(:,:,1:lmc)/nphottot
+ percabsAZnew=real(nphotonAZ(:,:,1:lmc),kind=wp)/ &
+ real(nphottot,kind=wp)

Monte Carlo convergence fractions now use real(...,kind=wp) values and reduced max changes, avoiding
the integer-division truncation in the old test.

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log August 2026

BUG-2026-08-022: RADIATION-019: Bottom gas absorption is
scaled by AZ sublayer volume

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Radiation/RADIATION-019.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
   ,→ rinit_rad.F90

rinitrad splits the first gas cell into nfuel fuel-zone AZ layers plus the first gas-cell AZ layer, and stores
a separate volume for each AZ layer:

! AZ volume
do k=1,l+nfuel
  do j=1,mp
 do i=1,np
 volumeAZ(i,j,k)=dx*dy*0.25_wp*(sum(zCartEdgeAZLocal(:,i,j,k))- &
 sum(zCartEdgeAZLocal(:,i,j,k-1)))
 enddo !i
  enddo !j
enddo !k

updateRadArrays maps every bottom AZ layer to the same gas cell, kcell=1:

do k=1,lmc !FPAZ
  if(k.le.nfuel)then
 kcell=1
  else
 kcell=k-nfuel
  endif

It then accumulates gas absorption into the gas-cell radiation tendency while dividing each contribution
by the individual AZ sublayer volume:

if(papvtotAZ(ia,ja,k).gt.papvthresh)then
  firad(i,j,kcell)=firad(i,j,kcell)+Qphot* &
 nphotonAZgather(ia,ja,k)* &
 papvgas(i,j,k)/papvtotAZ(ia,ja,k)/volumeAZ(i,j,k)

Gas emission is stored once per gas cell:

firad=-sourcegas

and the bottom source energy is distributed over the AZ split by multiplying the same first-cell sourcegas
by each bottom AZ volume:

do k=1,nfuel+1

 652

  do j=1,mp
 do i=1,np
 EAZlocal(i,j,k)=(sourcegas(i,j,1)+ &
 sum(sourcesol(:,i,j,k)))*volumeAZ(i,j,k)
 enddo !do i
  enddo !do j
enddo !do k

Problem
firad(i,j,1) is a single gas-cell tendency. For bottom-cell absorption, the absorbed gas energy from AZ
layers 1:nfuel+1 should be accumulated and converted back to a gas-cell volumetric tendency using the
full first gas-cell volume.
The current code divides each AZ-layer absorbed energy by that AZ layer’s own volumeAZ(i,j,k) and
then adds all of those already-normalized rates into the same gas-cell firad(i,j,1). That overweights
thin bottom AZ slices and makes the result depend on how fuel zones split the first gas cell.
For example, if two AZ sublayers of equal opacity each absorb the same energy but one sublayer is very
thin, the thin sublayer contributes a much larger firad increment solely because its bookkeeping volume
is smaller. Since there is only one gas temperature/energy value for kcell=1, the correct normalization
is the full first gas-cell volume, not each sublayer volume.

Use a separate gas normalization volume for the bottom split. The full first gas-cell AZ volume is
sum(volumeAZ(i,j,1:nfuel+1)); all other gas layers can keep their existing one-to-one AZ volume.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@
- integer :: i,j,k,kcell,ift,ia,ja
+ integer :: i,j,k,kcell,ift,ia,ja
+ real(wp) :: gasVolume
@@
         ia=(npos-1)*np+i
 if(papvtotAZ(ia,ja,k).gt.papvthresh)then
+ if(kcell.eq.1)then
+ gasVolume=sum(volumeAZ(i,j,1:nfuel+1))
+ else
+ gasVolume=volumeAZ(i,j,k)
+ endif
 firad(i,j,kcell)=firad(i,j,kcell)+Qphot* &
 nphotonAZgather(ia,ja,k)* &
- papvgas(i,j,k)/papvtotAZ(ia,ja,k)/volumeAZ(i,j,k)
+ papvgas(i,j,k)/papvtotAZ(ia,ja,k)/gasVolume

This fix can be combined with RADIATION-016, which handles the separate solid-fuel tendency accumulation
problem in the same loop.

removing the old bottom-cell scaling mismatch.

BUG-2026-08-023: SENSORS-002: Sensor cell search misses lower
domain boundaries

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Sensors/SENSORS-002.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ rinit_sense.F90

rinitSense locates sensors by scanning every local cell. The x/y tests add a positive fuzz to both the
lower and upper edge:

real(wp) :: fuzz=0.0001_wp
...
ia = (npos-1)*np + i - 1
...
if((se_xloc(ni).ge.real(ia)*dx + fuzz).and. &
  (se_xloc(ni).lt.(real(ia)+1.0_wp)*dx + fuzz).and. &
  (se_yloc(ni).ge.real(ja)*dy + fuzz).and. &
  (se_yloc(ni).lt.(real(ja)+1.0_wp)*dy + fuzz).and. &
  (se_zloc(ni).ge.zmh) .and. &

Problem
Adding fuzz to both edges shifts every horizontal cell interval upward. The first cell in x is tested as:

0.0001 <= se_xloc < dx + 0.0001

so a valid sensor exactly on the lower domain boundary, such as se_xloc = 0.0, is never assigned to any
processor. The same problem exists for se_yloc = 0.0.
The shift also changes exact internal-boundary behavior. For example se_xloc = dx is assigned to
the lower cell rather than the cell whose lower edge is dx, which is the usual half-open [lower, upper)
convention used by integer/floor cell mapping.

Do not implement tolerance by translating all cell bounds. Use explicit half-open cell bounds. If
roundoff tolerance is still desired, apply it in a single integer-index conversion so cells do not overlap or
leave boundary holes.

BUG-2026-08-024: SENSORS-003: Unmatched sensors fail silently

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Sensors/SENSORS-003.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ rinit_sense.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ sensors.F90

rinitSense initializes every local owner to -1, then only changes it if the local rank finds the sensor in
one of its cells:

se_proc(:)=-1
do ni=1,numsensors
  do k=1,l
 ...
 if((se_xloc(ni).ge.real(ia)*dx + fuzz).and. &
 ...

 print*,’sensor’,ni,’is␣in␣processor’,mpi_rank

 se_proc(ni) = mpi_rank
             se_i(ni) = i
             se_j(ni) = j
             se_k(ni) = k

Later, sensors_write only writes on the rank whose local se_proc matches its rank:

if(mpi_rank.eq.se_proc(ni)) then
  ...
  open(unit=unitnum,file=trim(sensorFileName)//’.csv’, &
 form=’formatted’,status=’old’,position=’append’)

Problem
If a sensor location is outside the domain, above the top, exactly in a boundary gap like SENSORS-002,
or otherwise not found, every rank keeps se_proc(ni) = -1. No rank writes data for that sensor and no
rank reports an error.
Rank 0 may still create the CSV header during initialization, so the run can appear successful while
producing a header-only sensor file. That is a costly failure mode because the bad sensor may not be
noticed until post-processing.

Track local matches and reduce them across MPI ranks after the search. Abort early if any configured
sensor is not owned by exactly one cell.

 659

+++ b/CODE-dev/Sensors/rinit_sense.F90
@@
- use msga_variables, only : mpi_rank,npos,mpos
+ use msga_variables, only : mpi_rank,npos,mpos,mpi_comm_world, &
+ mpi_integer,mpi_sum,mpi_abort,ierror
@@
- integer :: i,j,k,ia,ja,ni
+ integer :: i,j,k,ia,ja,ni
+ integer,allocatable :: foundLocal(:),foundGlobal(:)
@@
 allocate(se_x(numsensors),se_y(numsensors),se_z(numsensors))
 allocate(xv_values(numsensors,size(xv_list)))
+ allocate(foundLocal(numsensors),foundGlobal(numsensors))
+ foundLocal = 0
@@
             se_i(ni) = i
             se_j(ni) = j
             se_k(ni) = k
+ foundLocal(ni) = foundLocal(ni) + 1
 endif
@@
 enddo
+
+ call mpi_allreduce(foundLocal,foundGlobal,numsensors,mpi_integer, &
+ mpi_sum,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
+ if(any(foundGlobal.ne.1)) then
+ if(mpi_rank.eq.0) then
+ do ni=1,numsensors
+ if(foundGlobal(ni).eq.0) &
+ write(*,*) ’ERROR: sensor was not found:’, ni, &
+ se_xloc(ni),se_yloc(ni),se_zloc(ni)
+ if(foundGlobal(ni).gt.1) &
+ write(*,*) ’ERROR: sensor matched multiple cells:’, ni, &
+ foundGlobal(ni),se_xloc(ni),se_yloc(ni),se_zloc(ni)
+ enddo
+ endif
+ call mpi_abort(mpi_comm_world,1,ierror)
+ endif

 end subroutine rinitSense

Using mpi_sum rather than mpi_max also catches accidental duplicate ownership if future tolerance changes
create overlapping search intervals.

BUG-2026-08-025: SENSORS-004: Sensor CSV output inserts blank
records and relies on close to end rows

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Sensors/SENSORS-004.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ rinit_sense.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ sensors.F90

rinitSense writes the CSV header without explicitly ending the record:

write(unitnum,’(A16)’,advance=’no’)’cycle,␣time,␣’
do ni=1,size(xv_list)
  write(unitnum,’(A8)’,advance=’no’) xv_list(ni)
  if(ni.ne.size(xv_list)) then
    write(unitnum,’(A1)’,advance=’no’)’,’
  endif
enddo

Each sensor write starts by writing an empty record, then writes the data row with advance=’no’ and
closes the file without explicitly ending the row:

if(ncycle.lt.ittot) then
  write(unitnum,’(A1)’) ’’
  write(unitnum,’(I8,A1)’,advance=’no’)ittot,’,’
  write(unitnum,’(F14.6,A1)’,advance=’no’)time,’,’
  do i=1,size(xv_list)
 write(unitnum,’(F23.16)’,advance=’no’)xv_values(ni,i)
 if(i.ne.size(xv_list)) then
      write(unitnum,’(A1)’,advance=’no’)’,’
 endif
  enddo
endif

Problem
The blank write(unitnum,’(A1)’) ’’ creates an extra empty/blank CSV record before every data row.
The actual data row is never explicitly terminated; the code relies on close to finish the current
non-advancing record.
This produces awkward CSV files with blank rows, and the final-record behavior is less portable than
writing a normal record terminator. Some parsers tolerate this, but high-frequency sensor files should
be predictable and easy to consume.

 663

Terminate the header once, remove the leading blank row, and explicitly terminate each data row after
the last value.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Sensors/rinit_sense.F90
@@
- write(unitnum,’(A16)’,advance=’no’)’cycle, time, ’
+ write(unitnum,’(A)’,advance=’no’)’cycle,time’

- write(unitnum,’(A8)’,advance=’no’) xv_list(ni)

-            write(unitnum,’(A1)’,advance=’no’)’,’

+ write(unitnum,’(A)’,advance=’no’)’,’//trim(xv_list(ni))
 enddo
+ write(unitnum,*)
 endif

+++ b/CODE-dev/Sensors/sensors.F90
@@

 if(ncycle.lt.ittot) then
-        write(unitnum,’(A1)’) ’’
-        write(unitnum,’(I8,A1)’,advance=’no’)ittot,’,’
+        write(unitnum,’(I0,A1)’,advance=’no’)ittot,’,’
         write(unitnum,’(F14.6,A1)’,advance=’no’)time,’,’
 do i=1,size(xv_list)
 write(unitnum,’(F23.16)’,advance=’no’)xv_values(ni,i)
@@
             write(unitnum,’(A1)’,advance=’no’)’,’

+ write(unitnum,*)
 endif

Using trim(xv_list(ni)) also avoids padding header fields with the fixed character length.

BUG-2026-08-026: SENSORS-007: Fresh sensor runs silently append
to stale CSV files

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Sensors/SENSORS-007.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ rinit_sense.F90

When a sensor CSV already exists, rinitSense always appends:

inquire(file=trim(sensorFileName)//’.csv’, exist = exists)
if(exists)then ! if file does exists
  open(unit=unitnum,file=trim(sensorFileName)//’.csv’, &
 form=’formatted’,status=’old’,position=’append’)

 write(*,*)’WARNING:␣itrestart␣>␣ncycle␣in␣sensors.’
 write(*,*)’WARNING:␣sensor␣times␣may␣be␣out␣of␣order.’
  endif
else ! if file does not exist
  open(unit=unitnum,file=trim(sensorFileName)//’.csv’, &
 form=’formatted’,status=’unknown’)
  write(unitnum,’(A16)’,advance=’no’)’cycle,␣time,␣’

Problem
A normal fresh run has itrestart = 0 and usually ncycle = 0. If CSVs from an earlier run are still
present, this branch appends new samples to the old files without warning because ncycle.lt.itrestart
is false.
The resulting sensor files can contain multiple unrelated runs with duplicate cycle numbers and time
resets. Post-processing then treats stale and current data as one continuous series.
Appending is useful for restarts, but for non-restart runs the safer behavior is to replace existing sensor
CSVs and write a fresh header.

Only append existing files when this is actually a restart. Replace files for fresh runs.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Sensors/rinit_sense.F90
@@

 write(*,*)’WARNING: sensor times may be out of order.’
 endif
- else ! if file does not exist
+ else ! fresh run or missing restart file
 open(unit=unitnum,file=trim(sensorFileName)//’.csv’, &
- form=’formatted’,status=’unknown’)
+ form=’formatted’,status=’replace’)
 write(unitnum,’(A16)’,advance=’no’)’cycle, time, ’

This pairs well with SENSORS-004’s explicit header record terminator.

BUG-2026-08-027: SENSORS-009: Sensor location-file reads have no
I/O error checks

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Sensors/SENSORS-009.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ input_sense.F90

When locfile = 1, input_sensors opens the location file and reads exactly numsensors rows:

  call QueryGridlist_string(’sensorlocs’,sensorlocs,48)
  open(unit=7825,file=sensorlocs, form=’formatted’,status=’old’)
  do s=1,numsensors
    read(7825,*) se_xloc(s),se_yloc(s),se_zloc(s)
  enddo

else

Problem
The open and read statements have no iostat checks. If the file is missing, has fewer rows than numsensors,
or contains a malformed coordinate line, the Fortran runtime aborts at the raw I/O statement.
Because input is called before setup_MPI, every MPI process reads this file before ranks are initialized.
A bad location file can therefore produce repeated runtime I/O failures instead of one clear diagnostic
that says which sensor line is bad.

Check both the file open and each row read, and report the sensor index that failed.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Sensors/input_sense.F90
@@
- integer :: s
+ integer :: s,ios
@@

 call QueryGridlist_string(’sensorlocs’,sensorlocs,48)
- open(unit=7825,file=sensorlocs, form=’formatted’,status=’old’)
+ open(unit=7825,file=sensorlocs,form=’formatted’,status=’old’, &
+ iostat=ios)
+ if(ios.ne.0) then
+ write(*,*) ’ERROR: unable to open sensor location file: ’, &
+ trim(sensorlocs)
+ stop 1
+ endif

 670

 do s=1,numsensors
-      read(7825,*) se_xloc(s),se_yloc(s),se_zloc(s)
+ read(7825,*,iostat=ios) se_xloc(s),se_yloc(s),se_zloc(s)
+ if(ios.ne.0) then
+ write(*,*) ’ERROR: failed reading sensor location ’, s, &
+ ’ from ’,trim(sensorlocs)
+ stop 1
+ endif
 enddo

If input is later moved after setup_MPI, this should use the same MPI-aware fatal-error path as the rest
of initialization.

BUG-2026-08-028: SENSORS-010: ncycle start cycle is treated as
exclusive

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Sensors/SENSORS-010.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ variables_sense.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ sensors.F90

The sensor gridlist variable is documented as the cycle at which sensors begin:

integer :: ncycle = 0 ! time step to begin sensors

sensors_write only writes when the current total cycle is strictly greater than ncycle:

if(ncycle.lt.ittot) then
  write(unitnum,’(A1)’) ’’
  write(unitnum,’(I8,A1)’,advance=’no’)ittot,’,’
  write(unitnum,’(F14.6,A1)’,advance=’no’)time,’,’

Problem
The configured start cycle is skipped. For example, with ncycle = 100, the first eligible sensor record is
cycle 101, subject to the write-frequency gate in compress.F90.
That is an off-by-one relative to the variable’s comment and to the usual meaning of "begin at cycle N".
It also makes restart setups harder to reason about because ncycle = itrestart will not allow a record
at the restart cycle.

Treat ncycle as an inclusive first cycle.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Sensors/sensors.F90
@@
- if(ncycle.lt.ittot) then
+ if(ittot.ge.ncycle) then
         write(unitnum,’(A1)’) ’’
 write(unitnum,’(I8,A1)’,advance=’no’)ittot,’,’

After applying SENSORS-004, keep the same condition but use the cleaned-up row-writing code from
that report.

BUG-2026-08-029: SENSORS-013: Missing inline sensor coordinate
arrays leave uninitialized locations

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Sensors/SENSORS-013.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ input_sense.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist
 ,→ .F90

When locfile is not 1, the sensor coordinate arrays are allocated and then populated from three gridlist
arrays:

allocate(se_xloc(numsensors))
allocate(se_yloc(numsensors))
allocate(se_zloc(numsensors))
...
else
  call QueryGridlist_real_array(’se_xloc’,se_xloc,numsensors,48)
  call QueryGridlist_real_array(’se_yloc’,se_yloc,numsensors,48)
  call QueryGridlist_real_array(’se_zloc’,se_zloc,numsensors,48)
endif

The real-array query routine silently returns if the variable name is never found:

do ! Iterate through all lines of file
  read(fileunit,"(a)",iostat=ierror) text ! Read line into text
  if (ierror/=0) exit
  ...

 read(text,*) word,equal,array
 exit
  endif
enddo
rewind(fileunit)

Problem
se_xloc, se_yloc, and se_zloc have no module defaults. If locfile = 0 and one of these gridlist arrays is
missing or misspelled, the corresponding allocated array is never populated with valid coordinates.
Even after preserving defaults in the query routines, there is no default coordinate list to preserve. The
sensor search then uses undefined x/y/z locations, which can silently place sensors in arbitrary cells or
leave them unmatched.

locfile = 0. A separate routine avoids optional dummy arguments on the current external-subroutine
interface.

BUG-2026-08-030: MPI speedup: replace repeated LSPGF gathers
with one MPI_Allgather

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/01_lspgf_replace_repeated_gathers_with_allgather.md

In largeScalePGF.F90:323-340, the ilspgf == 3 branch gathers the local flspgf field once for every possible
root:

do iproc=1,numprocs
  call mpi_gather(flspgf,np*mp,mpi_wp,flspgftmp,np*mp, &
 mpi_wp,iproc-1,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
enddo

Each rank participates in all numprocs gathers. Every rank then reconstructs and filters the full global
field, so every rank needs the complete gathered result. The loop is therefore an all-gather implemented
as numprocs separate collective operations.

Use one mpi_allgather. It fills the existing flspgftmp(np,mp,numprocs) buffer on every rank, preserves the
current source/rank layout, and reduces the number of collective synchronizations from numprocs to one.
This applies only when ilspgf == 3, but that branch performs a global filter, so the saved collective
latency can be substantial at larger MPI process counts.

--- a/largeScalePGF.F90
+++ b/largeScalePGF.F90
@@
- do iproc=1,numprocs
- call mpi_gather(flspgf,np*mp,mpi_wp,flspgftmp,np*mp, &
- mpi_wp,iproc-1,mpi_comm_world,ierror)

+ call mpi_allgather(flspgf,np*mp,mpi_wp,flspgftmp,np*mp, &
+ mpi_wp,mpi_comm_world,ierror)

largeScalePGF.F90 already imports MPI, and no reconstruction or filtering loop needs to change.

Git evidence: c21d0ea (2026-07-08, broad bug-list cleanup); ae1a78e (2026-08-18, speedups part 2).
The large-scale PGF reductions were consolidated into array collectives and the later speedup pass
cleaned loop ordering in largeScalePGF.F90 and higrad.F90.

BUG-2026-08-031: MPI speedup: replace repeated firebrand scatters
with MPI_Alltoall

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/02_firebrand_migration_use_alltoall.md

Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90:updateFB first computes sndBrands(destination). It then loops over every process
and calls mpi_scatter to obtain one incoming count per source (:229-230). It repeats the same root loop
to send firebrand data from xvsndBrands(:,:,destination) into xvrcvBrands(:,:,source) (:249-250).
The two loops implement an all-to-all exchange one root at a time. Every rank participates in 2*numprocs
collective calls for one migration step.

Use one mpi_alltoall for the counts and one for the already-packed firebrand blocks. The existing
third-dimension layout is exactly the layout expected by MPI_Alltoall: the send block for destination p
is xvsndBrands(:,:,p), and the receive block from source p is xvrcvBrands(:,:,p).
This reduces the collective count from 2*numprocs to two without changing the firebrand ordering or
destination bookkeeping. It preserves the current mxbrand padding, so a later MPI_Alltoallv change could
reduce bandwidth further, but is not needed for this minimal diff.

- enddo
+ call mpi_alltoall(sndBrands,1,mpi_integer,rcvBrands,1,mpi_integer, &
+ mpi_comm_world,ierror)
@@
- do iproc=1,numprocs
- call mpi_scatter(xvsndBrands,nsize,mpi_wp,xvrcvBrands(:,:,iproc), &
- nsize,mpi_wp,iproc-1,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
- enddo
+ call mpi_alltoall(xvsndBrands,nsize,mpi_wp,xvrcvBrands,nsize,mpi_wp, &
+ mpi_comm_world,ierror)

The routine already has use mpi, so the collective is available without an additional module import.

Firebrand processor-count exchange was changed from a loop of scatters to one MPI_Alltoall.

BUG-2026-08-032: MPI speedup: gather the complete firebrand
record in one MPI_Gatherv

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/04_firebrand_output_one_gatherv.md

Firebrands/io_fb.F90:21-39 first gathers the number of firebrands, then calls mpi_gatherv once for every
component of xvbrand:

do it=1,nvbrand
  call mpi_gatherv(xvbrand(:,it),numBrands,mpi_wp, &
 xvtotBrands(:,it),totNumBrands,displs,mpi_wp,0, &

Because xvbrand(numBrands,nvbrand) and xvtotBrands(totalBrands,nvbrand) are contiguous with the brand
index first, the complete two-dimensional records already have a compatible packed order. The loop
adds nvbrand collective synchronizations to each firebrand output.

Scale each rank’s receive count and displacement by nvbrand and gather the entire two-dimensional array
in one call. The root receives the same xvtotBrands layout that the current component-by-component
loop produces, so the file format and subsequent write remain unchanged.
The current routine also allocates the receive array on non-root ranks using totNumBrands values that
are only populated on rank 0. The minimal safe diff below gives non-root ranks a one-element dummy
receive buffer while consolidating the collective; this avoids retaining that unrelated root-only allocation

BUG-2026-08-033: MPI speedup: remove heap allocation from every
halo update

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/05_update_remove_per_call_halo_allocations.md

update.F90:55-76 allocates six temporary halo buffers and an MPI status array every time update is
called:

allocate(tmpxsnd(nxbuf),tmpxrcv(nxbuf),tmpysnd(nybuf),tmpyrcv(nybuf))
allocate(tmpcorsnd(ncorbuf),tmpcorrcv(ncorbuf))

The buffers are filled and passed to the eight blocking MPI_Sendrecv calls, then deallocated at :617-619.
update is used throughout the timestep and advection paths, so this repeats allocator work around
every halo exchange. The status contents are never inspected.

Use automatic local arrays sized directly from the procedure arguments and pass MPI_STATUS_IGNORE to
every MPI_Sendrecv. The communication pattern, message sizes, tags, and boundary handling do not
change; only per-call heap allocation and unused status copying are removed.
This is a low-risk hot-path optimization, but automatic arrays use the stack. The local subdomain
and halo dimensions should be checked against the target compiler’s stack limits before adopting it for
unusually large decompositions.

BUG-2026-08-034: MPI speedup: use MPI_Alltoallv to stop padding
every firebrand exchange

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/06_firebrand_alltoallv_remove_padding.md

After packing brands by destination in Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90:updateFB, the code allocates:

xvsndBrands(mxbrand,nvbrand,numprocs)
xvrcvBrands(mxbrand,nvbrand,numprocs)

mxbrand is the global maximum number of brands sent to any one destination. The current fixed-count
exchange sends mxbrand*nvbrand real values to every rank, even when a particular destination has fewer
brands. Empty slots are transmitted and discarded later when rcvBrands is used to rebuild xvbrand.

Keep the existing packed block layout but use mpi_alltoallv with the actual per-destination counts.
Each send count is sndBrands(iproc)*nvbrand; each receive count is rcvBrands(iproc)*nvbrand. The block
stride can remain mxbrand*nvbrand, so no packing-layout rewrite is required.
This preserves the minimal MPI_Alltoall count exchange from the companion migration report, but
reduces payload volume from numprocs*mxbrand*nvbrand values per rank to the actual local number
of brands times nvbrand. The benefit is largest when brands are concentrated in a few destination
subdomains.

--- a/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
+++ b/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
@@

+ integer :: sndCounts(numprocs),rcvCounts(numprocs)
+ integer :: sndDispls(numprocs),rcvDispls(numprocs)
@@
- do iproc=1,numprocs
- call mpi_scatter(sndBrands,1,mpi_integer,rcvBrands(iproc), &

- enddo
+ call mpi_alltoall(sndBrands,1,mpi_integer,rcvBrands,1,mpi_integer, &
+ mpi_comm_world,ierror)
@@

 nsize=mxbrand*nvbrand
- do iproc=1,numprocs
- call mpi_scatter(xvsndBrands,nsize,mpi_wp,xvrcvBrands(:,:,iproc), &
- nsize,mpi_wp,iproc-1,mpi_comm_world,ierror)
- enddo
+ do iproc=1,numprocs
+ sndCounts(iproc)=sndBrands(iproc)*nvbrand
+ rcvCounts(iproc)=rcvBrands(iproc)*nvbrand

 691

+ sndDispls(iproc)=(iproc-1)*nsize
+ rcvDispls(iproc)=(iproc-1)*nsize
+ enddo
+ call mpi_alltoallv(xvsndBrands,sndCounts,sndDispls,mpi_wp, &
+ xvrcvBrands,rcvCounts,rcvDispls,mpi_wp,mpi_comm_world,ierror)

The displacements are in mpi_wp elements, matching the third-dimension block stride of the two arrays.
The receive buffer remains padded for a small diff; only transmitted counts change.

BUG-2026-08-035: MPI speedup: reuse the radiation allgather for

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/11_reuse_radiation_allgather_for_total_energy.md

Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90:344-373 first allgathers every rank’s local EAZlocal into EAZtmp, then remaps
that data into the global EAZ array. Immediately afterward, it sums only the local EAZlocal and calls a
second mpi_allreduce to obtain the global Etot.
The allgather already contains every rank’s contribution on every rank. The second collective therefore
repeats a global communication step whose result can be formed while the gathered data is being
remapped.

local sum and scalar mpi_allreduce, along with the now-unused Etotlocal declaration and MPI imports.
This removes one global reduction from every radiation solve while adding no new traversal: the sum
is performed inside the existing i,j,iproc remapping loop. The result is assembled from the same

BUG-2026-08-036: Put the contiguous Fortran index in the
innermost hot loop

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/13_fix_hot_loop_order_for_fortran_layout.md

Fortran stores the first array index contiguously. Several timestep loops currently iterate i -> j -> k,
leaving k as the innermost index even though the arrays are indexed (i,j,k,...). Examples are:

• force.F90:28-34 and force.F90:60-69;
• domainUpdates.F90:52-68, domainUpdates.F90:72-82, domainUpdates.F90:125-140, and domainUpdates.F90
  ,→ :166-176;
• Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90:142-155 when Monte Carlo radiation is enabled.

These loops update independent cells, so changing only the nesting order preserves the calculation
while making adjacent iterations access adjacent memory. The domain-update loop runs inside the
small-timestep MOA loop, making it a particularly useful target.

Minimal speedup
Use k -> j -> i for arrays whose spatial shape is (i,j,k,...); keep the fuel-type loop innermost where
the first dimension is fuel type. This improves cache-line use and gives the compiler a contiguous inner
loop without changing the scheme.

Minimal diff

--- a/force.F90
+++ b/force.F90
@@
- do i=1,np
- do j=1,mp
- do k=1,l
+ do k=1,l
+ do j=1,mp
+ do i=1,np
@@
- do i=il,iu
- do j=jl,ju
-        do k=1,lls
+    do k=1,lls
+ do j=jl,ju
+ do i=il,iu

Apply the same three-line nesting replacement to the two gas-property loops in domainUpdates.F90; for
the solid-property loops use do k, do j, do i, then the existing do ift. In Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
,→ :142-155, swap only the do i and do j lines so i is innermost:

--- a/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
+++ b/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90
@@

 697

 do k=1,nfuel
- do i=1,np
- do j=1,mp
+ do j=1,mp
+ do i=1,np

The edits are valid only for loops with no cross-cell dependencies; the cited loops have none. The likely
benefit is highest on large local domains and in runs using MOA, turbulence, vegetation, or radiation
heavily.

Git evidence: f349df9 (2026-08-18, speedups part 1); ae1a78e (2026-08-18, speedups part 2).
Loop order was changed in hot paths such as forcing, ZBEST, domain updates, and large-scale PGF so
the innermost loops better match contiguous memory access.
