BUG-2026-08-037: Use move_alloc when compacting firebrands

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/14_move_alloc_firebrand_compaction.md

Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90:evolveFB removes burned or out-of-domain brands by first allocating xvtmpbrand,
copying retained rows into it, then deallocating xvbrand, allocating a second array of the new exact size,
copying xvtmpbrand back, and finally deallocating the temporary.
This path runs every time firebrands are evolved. It performs two full firebrand-array copies and two
allocations even though the temporary already has the desired final shape.

Use Fortran’s move_alloc to transfer the temporary allocation directly into xvbrand. The existing
temporary-copy loop remains unchanged, but the second allocation and second full-array copy disappear.
move_alloc also automatically releases the old allocation held by xvbrand.

--- a/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
+++ b/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
@@

 if(retain(it))then
 xvtmpbrand(count,:)=xvbrand(it,:)
 count=count+1
 endif
 enddo

- allocate(xvbrand(numBrand,nvbrand))
- numBrands=numBrand
- xvbrand=xvtmpbrand
- deallocate(xvtmpbrand)
+ call move_alloc(xvtmpbrand,xvbrand)
+ numBrands=numBrand

The retained-row ordering and exact-size allocation are preserved; only the redundant copy and
allocation are removed.

Firebrand array growth/shrink operations now use move_alloc instead of manual allocate/copy/deallocate
sequences.

BUG-2026-08-038: Avoid the extra firebrand launch copy and no-op
reallocation

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/15_reduce_firebrand_launch_copies.md

Firebrands/generation_fb.F90:launchFB counts newly launchable brands, allocates newBrand, and fills it. It
then copies the entire existing xvbrand into an automatic tempBrand, reallocates xvbrand to the combined
size, copies tempBrand back, appends newBrand, and frees both temporaries.
Even when newBrands is zero, the routine still copies and reallocates the entire existing firebrand list.
When brands are launched, the old list is copied twice before the final list is ready.

Return immediately when no new brands were found. Otherwise allocate one final-size buffer, copy
the old brands into its leading rows, write new brands directly into the trailing rows, and transfer
ownership with move_alloc.
This retains the existing row ordering and avoids the automatic tempBrand array, one allocation, and
one full copy.

--- a/Firebrands/generation_fb.F90
+++ b/Firebrands/generation_fb.F90

@@
- allocate(newBrand(newBrands,nvbrand))
- it=1
+ if(newBrands.eq.0) return
+ allocate(newBrand(numBrands+newBrands,nvbrand))
+ it=numBrands+1
@@
- tempBrand=xvbrand

- allocate(xvbrand(numBrands+newBrands,nvbrand))
- xvbrand(1:numBrands,:)=tempBrand
- xvbrand(numBrands+1:numBrands+newBrands,:)=newBrand
- numBrands=numBrands+newBrands
- deallocate(newBrand)
+ if(numBrands.gt.0) newBrand(1:numBrands,:)=xvbrand
+ numBrands=numBrands+newBrands
+ call move_alloc(newBrand,xvbrand)

The existing generation loop should write into newBrand starting at it=numBrands+1, as shown. The old
list is copied into the leading rows after generation and before the ownership transfer.

BUG-2026-08-039: Remove full-array negation temporaries in
emission models

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/17_remove_negated_fuel_forcing_temporaries.md

small_implicit_forcings passes -forceSI_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof) to both efSource and ZBEST.
 The unary
minus is an array expression, so the compiler must materialize a full fuel-domain temporary before
either routine begins.
The value represents a positive consumption rate because forceSI_xvfuel stores a negative fuel forcing.
Both routines only consume this input; neither needs a separately stored positive array.

Pass the original negative forcing and apply the sign to a scalar inside the callee. This removes the
full-array negation and its memory traffic. The change is limited to the emission-model interface and
keeps the calculated positive consumption rate unchanged.

For efSource, which has a single caller in this tree:

--- a/force.F90
+++ b/force.F90
@@

+ call efSource(forceSI_xv(:,:,:,iEmitStart:iEmitStop), &
+        forceSI_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof),1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l, &

--- a/Emissions/efSource_ems.F90
+++ b/Emissions/efSource_ems.F90
@@
-subroutine efSource(forcing,fuelConsumed,ilh,iuh,jlh,juh,ku, &
+subroutine efSource(forcing,fuelForcing,ilh,iuh,jlh,juh,ku, &
@@
- real(wp),intent(in) :: fuelConsumed(nfuel,il:iu,jl:ju,lls)
+ real(wp),intent(in) :: fuelForcing(nfuel,il:iu,jl:ju,lls)
@@
- +fuelConsumed(ift,i,j,k)*efEmit(isp)
+ -fuelForcing(ift,i,j,k)*efEmit(isp)

Apply the same scalar-sign pattern to ZBEST: pass forceSI_xvfuel(:,:,:,:,irhof) without the unary
minus, set frate=-frhof(ift,i,j,k) at the top of its inner cell loop, and replace the existing frhof(ift,i
,→ ,j,k) uses with frate. The current positive-rate test and all seven rate-dependent formulas then
retain their original signs without a full-array temporary.

BUG-2026-08-040: Make the gradmoa pressure-gradient loop
contiguous

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Speedups/19_fix_gradmoa_gradient_loop_order.md

higrad.F90:gradmoa computes the horizontal pressure gradients in px and py with i outside j:

do k=1,l
  do i=1,np
 do j=1,mp
      py(i,j,k)=...
      px(i,j,k)=...

The arrays are indexed (i,j,k), so Fortran stores the i direction contiguously. This loop
therefore advances the innermost index through noncontiguous memory. gradmoa is called from
small_implicit_forcings, so the loop is on the small-step path.

Swap the i and j loops so i is innermost. The two gradient assignments are independent for each cell,
so this changes memory traversal only and does not change the stencil or its arithmetic.

--- a/higrad.F90
+++ b/higrad.F90
@@
 do k=1,l
- do i=1,np
- do j=1,mp
+ do j=1,mp
+ do i=1,np
         py(i,j,k)=0.5_wp*(pr(i,j+1,k)-pr(i,j-1,k))*dyi
         px(i,j,k)=0.5_wp*(pr(i+1,j,k)-pr(i-1,j,k))*dxi

This is the specific gradmoa instance of the broader loop-order optimization described in note 05; it is
called out separately because it is on the repeated MOA small-step path.

Git evidence: ae1a78e (2026-08-18, speedups part 2).
Gradient/large-scale PGF loops in higrad.F90 and largeScalePGF.F90 were reordered for cleaner memory
traversal.

BUG-2026-08-042: VEGETATION-004: solarHeating mixes local
MPI indices with global AZ geometry

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Vegetation/VEGETATION-004.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ solarHeat_veg.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
   ,→ rinit_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ definearray_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/metric.F90

Radiation allocates the AZ geometry over the global domain:

allocate(zCartEdgeAZGlobal(4,n,m,0:l+nfuel))

rinitrad fills it with global ia,ja indices:

ia=(iprocx-1)*np+i
ja=(jprocy-1)*mp+j
zCartEdgeAZGlobal(it,ia,ja,k)=zCartEdgeAZTmp(i,j,k,iproc)

solarHeating later reads that global array with local subdomain indices:

zlayer=(sum(zCartEdgeAZGlobal(:,i,j,k)- &
  zCartEdgeAZGlobal(:,i,j,k-1)))/4.0_wp
...
i1=i
j1=j
xf=dx*(i-0.5_wp)
yf=dy*(j-0.5_wp)
zf=(sum(zCartEdgeAZGlobal(:,i,j,k)+ &
  zCartEdgeAZGlobal(:,i,j,k-1)))/8.0_wp

During the global ray walk, it also passes global ray indices into zcart:

do while(i1.ge.1.and.i1.le.n.and.j1.ge.1.and.j1.le.m.and. &
  k1.ge.1.and.k1.le.lfuel)
...
sumShade(i,j,k)=sumShade(i,j,k)+ &
  t/(zcart(zedge(k1),i1,j1)+zcart(zedge(k1+1),i1,j1))/2.0_wp* &
  LAIall(i1,j1,k1)/DeepShadeLAI

But zcart indexes local zs(i,j):

z=gdeform*(zb-zs(i,j))/zb+zs(i,j)

 711

Problem
In a decomposed MPI run, local i,j are not the same as global ia,ja except on the first process
tile. Each rank seeds shade rays as if it owned global cells 1:np,1:mp, so the solar path and starting
coordinates are shifted to the wrong part of the domain.
Once a ray walks outside the local tile, i1,j1 can exceed the local bounds expected by zcart, which
reads zs(i1,j1). That is an out-of-bounds access on ranks where the ray reaches global indices beyond
the local halo.
The result is rank-dependent shade: every MPI tile can trace shadows from the wrong global location,
and some runs can crash or read invalid terrain while computing the path length.

Convert local cell indices to global coordinates before reading global AZ arrays, and avoid calling local
zcart for a global ray cell. Use the global AZ geometry for the ray-cell height instead.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Vegetation/solarHeat_veg.F90

@@

- i1=i
- j1=j
+          ia=(npos-1)*np+i
+          ja=(mpos-1)*mp+j

+ j1=ja

-            zCartEdgeAZGlobal(:,i,j,k-1)))/8.0_wp

BUG-2026-08-043: VEGETATION-005: fuelDragCorrection uses one
array as both sorted fuel list and inverse rank map

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Vegetation/VEGETATION-005.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
   ,→ drag_veg.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ convection_veg.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ evaporation_veg.F90

fuelDragCorrection sorts fuel types by actualFuelDepth:

integer :: it
integer :: itfindex(nfuel)
...
afdtmp=afd(:)
do it=1,nfuel
  itfindex(minloc(afdtmp,dim=1))=it
  afdtmp(minloc(afdtmp,dim=1))=maxval(afd)+1
enddo

It then uses itfindex as though itfindex(rank) gives the fuel type at that sorted rank:

layer_ht(1) = afd(itfindex(1))
...
layer_ht(it)=afd(itfindex(it))-afd(itfindex(it-1))
layer_ms(it)= &
  sum(rhoWater(itfindex(it:nfuel))+rhoFuel(itfindex(it:nfuel))) &
  *layer_ht(it)
...
rinterp=(afd(itfindex(nfuel))-zla2)/(zla3-zla2)

At the end, the same array is used in the inverse direction, as though itfindex(fuel_type) gives the
sorted rank of that fuel:

do it=1,nfuel
  u_corr(it)= &
 sum(u_fuel_layer(1:itfindex(it))*layer_ht(1:itfindex(it)))/afd(it)

Problem
The sort assignment stores itfindex(fuel_type)=rank, not itfindex(rank)=fuel_type.
For two fuel types, the inverse mapping can accidentally look correct. For three or more fuel types it
breaks. Example depths [30, 10, 20] produce:

 715

itfindex = [3, 1, 2]

That means fuel 1 has rank 3, fuel 2 has rank 1, and fuel 3 has rank 2. But the layer-height code reads
itfindex(1) as fuel type 3 for the first layer, when the shallowest fuel is fuel type 2.
fuelDragCorrection is called by convection and bulk evaporation to compute in-canopy velocities, so this
corrupts convective heat exchange and slow moisture exchange for multi-fuel cases with unsorted fuel
depths.

Keep both maps explicitly: fuelAtRank(rank) and rankOfFuel(fuel_type).

diff --git a/CODE-dev/Vegetation/drag_veg.F90 b/CODE-dev/Vegetation/drag_veg.F90
--- a/CODE-dev/Vegetation/drag_veg.F90
+++ b/CODE-dev/Vegetation/drag_veg.F90
@@
- integer :: it
- integer :: itfindex(nfuel)
+ integer :: it,ift
+ integer :: fuelAtRank(nfuel),rankOfFuel(nfuel)
@@
 afdtmp=afd(:)
 do it=1,nfuel
- itfindex(minloc(afdtmp,dim=1))=it
- afdtmp(minloc(afdtmp,dim=1))=maxval(afd)+1
+ ift=minloc(afdtmp,dim=1)
+ fuelAtRank(it)=ift
+ rankOfFuel(ift)=it
+ afdtmp(ift)=maxval(afd)+1
 enddo
@@
- layer_ht(1) = afd(itfindex(1))
+ layer_ht(1) = afd(fuelAtRank(1))
@@
- layer_ht(it)=afd(itfindex(it))-afd(itfindex(it-1))
+ layer_ht(it)=afd(fuelAtRank(it))-afd(fuelAtRank(it-1))
 layer_ms(it)= &
- sum(rhoWater(itfindex(it:nfuel))+rhoFuel(itfindex(it:nfuel))) &
+ sum(rhoWater(fuelAtRank(it:nfuel))+rhoFuel(fuelAtRank(it:nfuel))) &
 *layer_ht(it)
@@
- rinterp=(afd(itfindex(nfuel))-zla2)/(zla3-zla2)
+ rinterp=(afd(fuelAtRank(nfuel))-zla2)/(zla3-zla2)
@@
 do it=1,nfuel
     u_corr(it)= &
- sum(u_fuel_layer(1:itfindex(it))*layer_ht(1:itfindex(it)))/afd(it)
+ sum(u_fuel_layer(1:rankOfFuel(it))*layer_ht(1:rankOfFuel(it)))/afd(it)
     v_corr(it)= &
- sum(v_fuel_layer(1:itfindex(it))*layer_ht(1:itfindex(it)))/afd(it)
+ sum(v_fuel_layer(1:rankOfFuel(it))*layer_ht(1:rankOfFuel(it)))/afd(it)
     w_corr(it)= &
- sum(w_fuel_layer(1:itfindex(it))*layer_ht(1:itfindex(it)))/afd(it)
+ sum(w_fuel_layer(1:rankOfFuel(it))*layer_ht(1:rankOfFuel(it)))/afd(it)

BUG-2026-08-044: VEGETATION-006: Dry fuels do not cast solar
shade

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Vegetation/VEGETATION-006.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ solarHeat_veg.F90

solarHeating only traces shade rays for a target AZ cell if there is water mass in that fuel/gas cell:

do k=1,lfuel+nfuel
  if(k.lt.nfuel+1)then
 kcell=1
  else
 kcell=k-nfuel
  endif
  do j=1,mp
 do i=1,np
 if(any(rhoWater(:,i,j,kcell).gt.tolerance))then
 i1=i
 j1=j
 k1=k
 ...
 sumShade(i,j,k)=sumShade(i,j,k)+ ...
 endif
 enddo
  enddo
enddo

But leaf area itself is computed from dry fuel density:

LAIlocal(i,j,k)=sum(rhoFuel(kfindex(i,j,k:nfuel),i,j,1)/ &
  sizeScale(kfindex(i,j,k:nfuel),i,j,1)*zlayer/rhoMicro)

The final heating term is also applied to dry fuel mass:

av=2.0_wp*(rhoFuel(it,i,j,k)/rhoMicro)/sizeScale(it,i,j,k)
force_sies(it,i,j,k)=force_sies(it,i,j,k) &
  +(QswIN+QlwIN-QlwOUT)*av &
  /(rhoFuel(it,i,j,k)+rhoWater(it,i,j,k))

Problem
Canopy shading depends on leaf/fuel area, not on how much water the fuel currently contains.
If a dry fuel bed has rhoWater == 0 but nonzero rhoFuel, solarHeating skips the ray tracing and leaves
sumShade at zero. That makes dry canopies heat as if they were unshaded, while moist canopies cast
shade.

 720

This is especially backwards for a moisture model: as fuels dry out, the code progressively removes
their ability to shade themselves and other fuels.

Use solid fuel presence, or total solid plus water mass, to decide whether a cell participates in shade
tracing.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Vegetation/solarHeat_veg.F90
@@
- if(any(rhoWater(:,i,j,kcell).gt.tolerance))then
+ if(any((rhoFuel(:,i,j,kcell)+rhoWater(:,i,j,kcell)).gt.tolerance))then
 i1=i
 j1=j

If min_rhoFuel is only a numerical floor and should not cast shade, use a vegetation-specific threshold
larger than that floor instead of checking water mass.

Git evidence: 798df8b (2026-08-18, vegetation bug-list pass); 9ce10f9 (2026-08-13, radiation bug-list
pass); dea57a5 (2026-06-30, solar-heating fixes).

force.F90 passes the conserved H2O field:

The ambient emission initialization stores H2O as density, not mass fraction:

  xe(:,:,:,irho)

Problem
xvtmp(:,:,:,iH2O) is a conserved density field. solarHeating treats the value it receives as a mass fraction
and multiplies it by pressure for the Brunt longwave emissivity term.
That makes the emissivity depend on grid-cell density as well as humidity. In denser near-surface
cells, the vapor term is too large; in lower-density cells it is too small. The same H2O representation
is handled correctly elsewhere by using the density-normalized xvrho(:,:,:,iH2O) field, so this call is
inconsistent with the model’s mass-fraction convention.

misuse.

BUG-2026-08-046: VEGETATION-017: sun_position reduces solar
mean longitude modulo 90 degrees

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/Vegetation/VEGETATION-017.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ solarHeat_veg.F90

sun_position computes the apparent solar longitude from a mean longitude L0, an anomaly M, and an
equation-of-center correction:

L0 = mod(REAL(unixT/5022440.0_wp-183.6045_wp,KIND=wp),pi/2.0_wp) ! Mean longitude (geom. not reduced,
 ,→ radians)
M = REAL(unixT/5022680.0_wp-182.2505_wp,KIND=wp)             ! Mean anomaly (radians)
C = 0.03342_wp*sin(M) ! Equation of center (radians)
lambda = L0+C ! True Longitude (radians)
delta=asin(sin(eps)*sin(lambda)) ! Declination (radians)

Problem
Solar ecliptic longitude is an annual angle and should be reduced over a full circle, 2*pi, not over pi/2.
The current mod(..., pi/2) folds the year into four identical 90-degree longitude ranges. As a result,
the declination calculation cannot represent the normal annual cycle correctly. Since L0 is restricted to
roughly 0..pi/2, sin(lambda) is almost always nonnegative, so the computed solar declination is biased
toward spring/summer-like values and cannot produce a proper winter negative declination.
This is separate from the already filed call-order and zenith/elevation bugs: even if latitude/longitude
and GHI zenith handling are fixed, this modulo still corrupts the sun angle.

Reduce the solar mean longitude over 2*pi. It is also safer to reduce M before taking trig functions, and
to use modulo so the result is nonnegative for old dates.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Vegetation/solarHeat_veg.F90
@@
- L0 = mod(REAL(unixT/5022440.0_wp-183.6045_wp,KIND=wp),pi/2.0_wp) ! Mean longitude (geom. not
 ,→ reduced, radians)
- M = REAL(unixT/5022680.0_wp-182.2505_wp,KIND=wp)              ! Mean anomaly (radians)
+ L0 = modulo(REAL(unixT/5022440.0_wp-183.6045_wp,KIND=wp), &
+ 2.0_wp*pi) ! Mean longitude reduced to [0,2*pi)
+ M = modulo(REAL(unixT/5022680.0_wp-182.2505_wp,KIND=wp), &
+ 2.0_wp*pi) ! Mean anomaly reduced to [0,2*pi)

 728

A more complete cleanup would replace the hard-coded epoch constants with a standard Julian-
day/J2000 solar-position calculation, but the modulo base is a direct correctness bug in the current
formula.

Git evidence: 798df8b (2026-08-18, vegetation bug-list pass); 9ce10f9 (2026-08-13, radiation bug-list
pass); dea57a5 (2026-06-30, solar-heating fixes).

BUG-2026-08-047: BUG-June24-advectionScheme-001: ibctopopen
cannot produce advective top outflow because vertical top flux is
hard-coded closed

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/advectionScheme/aa-easy_advectionScheme_Bug1.md

variables.F90 defines ibctopopen as an open-outlet/free-slip top option, and input.F90 reads it from the
gridlist. But advectionScheme.F90 never checks that flag. The vertical face velocity at the top face is
always set to zero, and the MPDATA vertical flux through the top face is always set to zero.
That makes the vertical advection boundary a closed lid even when ibctopopen.ne.0. Top damping/re-
laxation can still occur elsewhere, but transported mass, momentum, heat, smoke, and species cannot
advect out through k=l+1 in this MPDATA path.
Current problematic code:

! advectionScheme.F90, setAdvectiveVelocities
do j=1,mp
  do i=1,np
    u3(i,j,1)=0.0_wp
    u3(i,j,l+1)=0.0_wp
  enddo
enddo

! advectionScheme.F90, mpdata
do j=1,mp
  do i=1,np
    f3(i,j, 1,kv)=0.0_wp
    f3(i,j,n3,kv)=0.0_wp
  enddo
enddo

Minimal suggested diff, assuming ibctopopen.ne.0 is intended to allow upward advective outflow and
prevent top inflow:

BUG-2026-08-049: METRIC-004: Turbulence wall-length correction
uses the wrong metric height

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/metricF90/METRIC-004.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/metric.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb
   ,→ /rinit_turb.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/subGridTurb
 ,→ /variables_turb.F90

zcart returns physical height using the terrain height in zs(i,j):

z=gdeform*(zb-zs(i,j))/zb+zs(i,j)

The turbulence length-scale initialization uses that absolute physical height in the near-wall correction:

elseif(isa.eq.4)then ! similar to isa=2 with a correction in the lower part of the domain
  saxy(i,j,k)=(dx*dy*(zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)- &
    zcart(zedge(k),i,j)))**(1.0_wp/3.0_wp)
  saxy(i,j,k)=saxy(i,j,k)/ &
    sqrt(1.0_wp+(saxy(i,j,k)/(0.4_wp/0.23_wp*zcart(z(k),i,j)))**2.0_wp)
  saz(i,j,k)=saxy(i,j,k)
elseif(isa.eq.5)then ! similar to isa=3 with a correction in the lower part of the domain
  saxy(i,j,k)=(dx*dy)**0.5_wp/ &
    sqrt(1.0_wp+(saxy(i,j,k)/(0.4_wp/0.23_wp*zcart(z(k),i,j)))**2.0_wp)
  saz(i,j,k)=zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j)/ &
    sqrt(1.0_wp+(saxy(i,j,k)/(0.4_wp/0.23_wp*zcart(z(k),i,j)))**2.0_wp)
endif

The same file has non-corrected branches that compute the cell height as the full difference between
upper and lower zcart faces:

saz(i,j,k)=zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j)

Problem
The correction denominator is supposed to use distance from the ground, but zcart(z(k),i,j) is an
absolute elevation. Over topography, a first-layer cell on a ridge can have a large absolute zcart value
even though it is still very close to the local ground. That makes the near-wall correction depend on
terrain elevation instead of local height above ground.
The isa=5 branch also has two local expression bugs:

• saxy(i,j,k) is used on the right-hand side before being assigned in that branch.
• saz divides only the lower-face height because / binds before -:

 738

zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j)/sqrt(...)

That is not the corrected cell height. The intended expression is the full cell height divided by the
correction factor.
For isa=4 or isa=5 over terrain, this can make sa, saxy, and saz decomposition- and terrain-elevation
dependent, and isa=5 can additionally produce stale or nonsensical length scales.

Use local height above ground for the wall distance, define the uncorrected length before applying the
correction, and parenthesize the vertical cell-height correction.

BUG-2026-08-050: METRIC-005: Radiation east-flux update indexes
gas heights as if they were Monte Carlo AZ levels

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/metricF90/METRIC-005.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/metric.F90

Radiation allocates Monte Carlo AZ arrays over l+nfuel levels, but eastFlux only over the gas grid:

allocate(eastFlux(np,mp,l)); eastFlux=0.0_wp

source_defs sets lmc from the active Monte Carlo AZ levels and allows it to reach l+nfuel:

lmc=5+nfuel
do k=1,l+nfuel
  do j=1,m
 do i=1,n

 (EAZ(i,j,k)/Etot*nphotbatch).ge.1) then
 lmc = MAX(k,lmc)
 endif
 enddo
  enddo
enddo

updateRadArrays loops over k=1,lmc. It maps AZ levels to gas levels with kcell, but the east-flux code still
writes eastFlux(i,j,k), reads nphotonEastFlux(...,k+nfuel), and evaluates gas-cell height with zedge(k+1):

do k=1,lmc !FPAZ

 kcell=1
  else

  endif

    (dy*(zcart(zedge(k+1),i,j)-zcart(zedge(k),i,j)))

zedge is only allocated over 1:l+1:

 741

allocate(zedge(l+1))

Problem
The loop variable k in updateRadArrays is an AZ-level index, not always a gas-cell index. For iradeastflux
,→ =1, the current code mixes those two coordinate systems.
When lmc > l, the east-flux statement writes past eastFlux(:,:,l) and reads zedge(k+1) past zedge(l+1).
When k+nfuel > l+nfuel, it also reads beyond nphotonEastFlux. Even before those hard bounds failures,
low k values represent fuel/AZ layers, so using zedge(k) as a gas-grid metric height is inconsistent with
the kcell mapping used by the rest of the routine.
The result is that enabling east-flux output can corrupt memory or crash in terrain-height calculations
when the active Monte Carlo domain extends above the gas-grid index assumed by this statement.

Only write eastFlux for AZ levels that correspond to gas cells, map the AZ level to kcell, and use the
same AZ level when reading nphotonEastFlux.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Radiation/monteCarlo_rad.F90

BUG-2026-08-051: READGRIDLIST-002: Assignment parsing
depends on spaces around =

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/readgridlistF90/READGRIDLIST-002.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/readgridlist
 ,→ .F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/input.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/TOOLS/Basic_Run/
 ,→ gridlist
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/TOOLS/TestCases/50
 ,→ x50x20_heatsource_rect/gridlist

Each query routine first reads the first blank-delimited token into word, then checks that token against
the requested variable name:

! readgridlist.F90
  read(text,*) word

 read(text,*) word,equal,variable
 exit
  endif

For scalar queries, equal is only one character and is not validated:

! readgridlist.F90
  character(len=1) :: equal
  character(len=20) :: word
  character(len=1000) :: text

The gridlist files look namelist-like. TOOLS/Basic_Run/gridlist even wraps the inputs with a namelist
header and terminator:

&compresslist
 irst = 0
 restartfile = ’./comp/comp.out.12400’
 nt = 10000
...
/

Problem
The parser only recognizes assignments when the key and = are separated by whitespace, such as:

nt = 10000

 744

A normal namelist-style spelling without spaces is not recognized:

nt=10000

For nt=10000, the first list-directed token read into word is the whole token nt=10000, not nt, so the
query never matches the requested key. Combined with intent(out) from READGRIDLIST-001, that
can invalidate the caller’s default; even after fixing intent(out), it silently ignores a valid-looking user
override.
The second read also accepts malformed separators because equal is never checked. A typo like
nt : 10000 can be parsed as if it were a valid assignment.

Parse assignments by locating the first = in the line, comparing the trimmed left-hand side to the
requested variable name, and reading only the right-hand side. This accepts both key = value and
key=value, rejects missing =, and avoids the unused equal token.

+++ b/CODE-dev/readgridlist.F90
@@

- character(len=1) :: equal
- character(len=20) :: word
+ integer :: eqpos
+ character(len=1000) :: key
+ character(len=1000) :: valueText
 character(len=1000) :: text
@@
-    if(text/=’’)then
- read(text,*) word
- if(word.eq.variableName)then
- read(text,*) word,equal,variable
- exit

- endif
+    if(text/=’’)then
+ eqpos = index(text,’=’)
+ if(eqpos.gt.0)then
+ key = adjustl(text(:eqpos-1))
+ if(trim(key).eq.trim(variableName))then
+ valueText = text(eqpos+1:)
+ read(valueText,*,iostat=ierror) variable
+ if(ierror.ne.0)then
+ print*,’ERROR reading gridlist value for ’,trim(variableName)
+ STOP
+ endif
+ exit
+ endif
+ endif
+ endif

Apply the same eqpos/key/valueText pattern to QueryGridlist_real, QueryGridlist_string, QueryGridlist_string_array
,→ , and QueryGridlist_real_array. For array queries, combine this with the continuation-aware fix in
READGRIDLIST-003 so long arrays are not forced onto one line.

no longer require spaces around the equals sign.

 748

Problem
The vapor pressure formula returns hPa, while pressground is Pa. At 300 K and 50% RH, the code uses
about 17.7 as if it were Pa instead of converting to about 1770 Pa. That makes water vapor roughly
100x too small.
There is also a naming/usage mismatch: 0.62199 * pw / (p - pw) is a humidity mixing ratio, but the
code stores it in specificHumidity and then treats it as a mass fraction for gas composition and emissions.
The difference is smaller than the hPa/Pa error, but it compounds the same initialization path.

store an actual mass fraction in specificHumidity.

 752

Problem
iperturb=2 assumes rank zero has at least a 6 x 6 x 10 local subdomain. Smaller processor blocks or
vertical domains will read/write out of bounds. It also defines the perturbation in rank-local coordinates,
so changing the MPI decomposition moves the perturbation in global space.
iperturb=3 is closer because it chooses a global target, but if the target lands on the first local row
or column, the i-1 or j-1 updates write a halo cell. With ih=0 that is out of bounds; with halos, the
perturbation can be lost when halos are updated because the owning physical cell is on a neighboring
rank.

Apply perturbations by global cell coordinates and add each target only on the rank that owns it. This
removes the dependency on rank-zero local dimensions and handles pinwheels that cross subdomain
boundaries. Use an MPI reduction for the sampled perturbation magnitude so every rank applies the
same value.

+++ b/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
@@
- use msga_variables, only : mpi_rank,npos,mpos
+ use msga_variables, only : mpi_rank,npos,mpos,mpi_comm_world,ierror, &
+ mpi_sum,mpi_wp
@@
 real(wp) :: rndNum
 real(wp) :: rfluctuation
+ real(wp) :: localMagnitude,globalMagnitude
@@
 elseif(iperturb.eq.2)then ! INRA Pinwheel initialization
 kpert=10
 ipert=5
 jpert=5
- if(mpi_rank.eq.0) then
- rfluctuation=0.05_wp*sqrt(xe(ipert,jpert,kpert,1)**2 &
-        +xe(ipert,jpert,kpert,2)**2)
+ if(kpert.gt.l)then
+ if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’WARNING: iperturb=2 kpert exceeds l; skipping pinwheel’
+ return
+ endif
+ localMagnitude=0.0_wp
+ call sampleLocalMagnitude(ipert,jpert,kpert,localMagnitude)
+ call mpi_allreduce(localMagnitude,globalMagnitude,1,mpi_wp,mpi_sum, &
+ mpi_comm_world,ierror)
+ rfluctuation=0.05_wp*globalMagnitude
+ if(mpi_rank.eq.0) then
 write(6,*) ’pinwheel on proc ’, mpi_rank
 write(6,*) ’pinwheel i,j,k,height’, ipert,jpert,kpert, &
         zcart(z(kpert),1,1)
-      write(6,*) ’pinwheel magnitude’, zcart(z(10),1,1)

Problem
If a user selects a constant-wind setup such as uswitch=0 and vswitch=0, the outer if(uswitch.eq.2.or.

unless the other component happens to request the canopy profile.

profile when switch 2 is active. Then run the wind-assignment loops unconditionally.

+ deallocate(uprofile)

This preserves the existing canopy behavior while making uswitch=0 and vswitch=0 work even when no
component asks for a canopy-normalized profile.

BUG-2026-08-055: RINIT-008: Ramped wind switches update xe

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/rinitF90/RINIT-008.md

! rinit.F90

The actual ramped-wind update for ixevariation=1 happens later in explicit_domain_updates:

! domainUpdates.F90

172    xe(1:np,1:mp,:,:),1,np,1,mp,l,nv)

Problem
For uswitch=1 or vswitch=1, the initial transported field is copied from xe before the ramped wind profile
has ever been applied. rinitXeVariation does not initialize case 1, and xevariation is not called until the

profile is only updated later. That first large step can initialize turbulence, pressure-gradient targeting,
diagnostics, and the transported flow from the wrong wind state.

For restarts, update only the environmental state and keep the restarted xv.

BUG-2026-08-056: RMAXMIN-001: Non-root ranks read undefined
MPI_Reduce receive values

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/rmaxminF90/RMAXMIN-001.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rmaxmin.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/compress.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/MOA.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Firebrands/
 ,→ firebrand_fb.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
   ,→ rinit_veg.F90

compress.F90, MOA.F90, firebrands, radiation, and vegetation diagnostics call the shared min/max helpers:

call rmaxmin_3D(xvrho(:,:,1:l,kv),xv_list(kv), &
  1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,1,l)

call rmaxmin_1D(xvbrand(:,kv),xvbrand_list(kv),1,numBrands)

Both helpers reduce local extrema to rank zero, but then copy the receive buffer on every rank:

rmax=maxval(array)
rmin=minval(array)
call mpi_reduce(rmax,xmax,1,mpi_wp,mpi_max,0, &

call mpi_reduce(rmin,xmin,1,mpi_wp,mpi_min,0, &

xmaxprint = xmax
xminprint = xmin
if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’␣RMAXMIN␣for␣’,string, &
  ’␣:␣max␣=␣’,xmaxprint,’␣,min␣=␣’,xminprint

rmaxmin_3D has the same pattern:

rmax=maxval(array(:,:,:))
rmin=minval(array(:,:,:))
call mpi_reduce(rmax,xmax,1,mpi_wp,mpi_max,0, &

call mpi_reduce(rmin,xmin,1,mpi_wp,mpi_min,0, &

xmaxprint = xmax
xminprint = xmin
if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’␣RMAXMIN␣for␣’,string, &

 765

  ’␣:␣max␣=␣’,xmaxprint,’␣,min␣=␣’,xminprint

Problem
For MPI_Reduce, the receive buffer is meaningful only on the root rank. In these calls, xmax and xmin
are defined on mpi_rank == 0; on all other ranks, MPI does not write valid global extrema into those
variables.
The helpers still execute:

xmaxprint = xmax
xminprint = xmin

on every rank, so non-root processes read undefined local variables. The printed result usually appears
correct because only rank zero prints, but the non-root undefined reads can still produce invalid-
floating-point behavior under debugging/sanitizer builds, make compiler diagnostics harder to trust,
and leave the routine relying on behavior MPI does not provide.
This affects every caller because the helper runs collectively across all ranks whenever diagnostics are
printed.

Only consume the MPI_Reduce receive values on rank zero. If future code needs every rank to receive the
global extrema, switch these calls to MPI_Allreduce instead.

+++ b/CODE-dev/rmaxmin.F90
@@
 call mpi_reduce(rmax,xmax,1,mpi_wp,mpi_max,0, &

 call mpi_reduce(rmin,xmin,1,mpi_wp,mpi_min,0, &

- xmaxprint = xmax
- xminprint = xmin
- if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’ RMAXMIN for ’,string, &
- ’ : max = ’,xmaxprint,’ ,min = ’,xminprint
+ if(mpi_rank.eq.0) then
+ xmaxprint = xmax
+ xminprint = xmin
+ print*,’ RMAXMIN for ’,string, &
+ ’ : max = ’,xmaxprint,’ ,min = ’,xminprint
+ endif
@@
 call mpi_reduce(rmax,xmax,1,mpi_wp,mpi_max,0, &

 call mpi_reduce(rmin,xmin,1,mpi_wp,mpi_min,0, &

- xmaxprint = xmax
- xminprint = xmin
- if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’ RMAXMIN for ’,string, &
- ’ : max = ’,xmaxprint,’ ,min = ’,xminprint
+ if(mpi_rank.eq.0) then
+ xmaxprint = xmax
+ xminprint = xmin

 766

+ print*,’ RMAXMIN for ’,string, &
+ ’ : max = ’,xmaxprint,’ ,min = ’,xminprint
+ endif

 end subroutine rmaxmin_3D

BUG-2026-08-057: RMAXMIN-002: Fuel-depth diagnostic passes a
2D slice to the 3D helper

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/rmaxminF90/RMAXMIN-002.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rmaxmin.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
   ,→ rinit_veg.F90

rmaxmin_3D declares its diagnostic array as rank 3:

subroutine rmaxmin_3D(array,string,il,iu,jl,ju,kl,ku)
  ...
  integer,intent(in) :: il,iu,jl,ju,kl,ku
  real(wp),intent(in) :: array(il:iu,jl:ju,kl:ku)
  character(*) :: string

Most vegetation diagnostics pass rank-3 sections:

call rmaxmin_3D(xvfuel(ift,:,:,:,irhof),’rhoFuel’,1,np,1,mp,1,lfuel)
call rmaxmin_3D(sizeScale(ift,:,:,:),’szsc’,1,np,1,mp,1,lfuel)
call rmaxmin_3D(rmoist(ift,:,:,:),’moist’,1,np,1,mp,1,lfuel)

The fuel-depth diagnostic passes only a rank-2 section, while telling rmaxmin_3D that the third dimension
is 1:1:

call rmaxmin_3D(fuelDepth(ift,:,:,1),’afd’,1,np,1,mp,1,1)

Problem
fuelDepth(ift,:,:,1) has shape (np,mp), but rmaxmin_3D expects shape (np,mp,1). The call compiles
because rmaxmin_3D is an external procedure with no explicit interface at the call site, so the compiler
cannot enforce the helper’s rank contract.
That makes the diagnostic depend on fragile sequence/temporary association instead of a matching
argument shape. A warning build with GNU Fortran reports an array temporary for this call, and
adding a proper module/interface for rmaxmin_3D would expose the rank mismatch as an interface error.
The current call happens to request only one vertical plane, so it is easy for this to appear harmless.
But it leaves the code one refactor away from a compile failure, and one bounds-argument edit away
from reading past the actual 2D slice.

Pass a rank-3 one-plane section to match the rmaxmin_3D interface. This keeps the current output
behavior but makes the call shape honest.

 769

+++ b/CODE-dev/Vegetation/rinit_veg.F90
@@
-      call rmaxmin_3D(fuelDepth(ift,:,:,1),’afd’,1,np,1,mp,1,1)
+      call rmaxmin_3D(fuelDepth(ift,:,:,1:1),’afd’,1,np,1,mp,1,1)

A broader cleanup would move the rmaxmin helpers into a module and provide explicit rmaxmin_1D,
rmaxmin_2D, and rmaxmin_3D interfaces. Then this diagnostic could call a true 2D helper instead of
representing a 2D field as a one-layer 3D field.

BUG-2026-08-058: RMAXMIN-003: Fuel min/max diagnostics
allocate hidden temporaries every timestep

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/rmaxminF90/RMAXMIN-003.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rmaxmin.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/compress.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Vegetation/
 ,→ definearray_veg.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ monteCarlo_rad.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Radiation/
 ,→ definearray_rad.F90

Fuel state is stored with fuel type as the first, fastest-varying dimension:

allocate(xvfuel(nfuel,np,mp,lfuel,nvfuel))

The main timestep loop prints min/max diagnostics by fixing that first dimension:

do ift=1,nfuel
  if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,’Fuel␣Type’,ift
  do kv=1,nvfuel
 call rmaxmin_3D(xvfuel(ift,:,:,:,kv),xvfuel_list(kv), &
      1,np,1,mp,1,lfuel)
  enddo
enddo

rmaxmin_3D takes an explicit-shape 3D dummy:

subroutine rmaxmin_3D(array,string,il,iu,jl,ju,kl,ku)
  ...
  real(wp),intent(in) :: array(il:iu,jl:ju,kl:ku)

Radiation has the same first-index slice pattern:

allocate(fsiesrad(nfuel,np,mp,lfuel)); fsiesrad=0.0_wp
...
call rmaxmin_3D(fsiesrad(ift,:,:,:),’fsiesrad_’//iftname, &
  il,iu,jl,ju,1,lfuel)

Problem
Fortran arrays are column-major, so the first index is contiguous. A section such as:

 772

xvfuel(ift,:,:,:,kv)

fixes the fastest-varying dimension and leaves a strided 3D view. Because rmaxmin_3D is an external
explicit-shape routine, the compiler must pass a contiguous sequence to the dummy argument. In
practice, that means packing the strided section into a hidden temporary before entering rmaxmin_3D.
A focused GNU Fortran warning build reports this at the hot timestep call:

compress.F90:51:24:
Warning: Creating array temporary at (1) for argument ’_formal_14’ [-Warray-temporaries]

This is a performance and scalability bug. The diagnostic runs inside the main timestep loop for every
fuel type and every fuel variable, so large vegetation runs can repeatedly allocate, fill, and discard full
local fuel-field temporaries just to compute extrema. The radiation diagnostic has the same shape issue
for fsiesrad(ift,:,:,:).

Avoid passing strided first-index slices to the generic 3D helper in hot paths. One conservative fix is to
add a fuel-specific helper that receives the full contiguous 5D fuel array and loops over the requested
fuel type and variable directly.

+++ b/CODE-dev/rmaxmin.F90
@@
 end subroutine rmaxmin_3D
+
+!-----------------------------------------------------------------------

stressrij has the safer split that diffuse is missing: km1 is clamped to 1:l for turbulence coefficient
arrays, while k0 is allowed to reach the field’s k=0 ground layer:

! subGridTurb/stressrij_turb.F90

 776

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log August 2026

254   do k=1,lls+1
255 ! km1 is for arrays defined only on 1:lls.
256 ! k0 is for fields intentionally defined on 0:lls, including bottom ghost/subground values.
257     km1 = max(k-1,1)
258     k0 = max(k-1,0)
259     kk = min(k,lls)
...
293         ux = 0.5_wp*(xvrho(i+1,j,kk,iuvel)-xvrho(i-1,j,kk,iuvel)+ &
294           xvrho(i+1,j,k0,iuvel)-xvrho(i-1,j,k0,iuvel))*hdxi
...
299         uy = 0.5_wp*(xvrho(i,j+1,kk,iuvel)-xvrho(i,j-1,kk,iuvel)+ &
300           xvrho(i,j+1,k0,iuvel)-xvrho(i,j-1,k0,iuvel))*hdyi

Problem
At the bottom face of a cell, k=1, diffuse sets:

km1 = max(1,k-1) = 1
kk = min(k,lls) = 1

So the horizontal derivatives used in the vertical contravariant scalar flux are averaged from level 1
twice:

px_bottom = 0.5 * (dphi_dx(k=1) + dphi_dx(k=1))
py_bottom = 0.5 * (dphi_dy(k=1) + dphi_dy(k=1))

But the scalar field phi is explicitly declared on 0:lls, and domainUpdates.F90 constructs a meaningful
xvrho(:,:,0,:) bottom state for these turbulence stencils. The vertical derivative in the same block
already uses phi(i,j,k-1), which is phi(i,j,0) at the bottom face.
This makes the bottom-face flux internally inconsistent on terrain-following grids:

• the normal-gradient part of hzc uses the ground ghost layer through pz;
• the terrain cross terms sqrtG_KG31a * px and sqrtG_KG32a * py ignore the ground ghost layer and
  reuse level 1;
• the Reynolds-stress routine avoids the same mistake by using a separate k0 field index.

On flat terrain, c13 and c23 are zero, so the mistake is mostly hidden. On sloped terrain, the vertical
scalar flux includes horizontal-gradient cross terms, so ignoring the reconstructed ground layer can
produce the wrong near-ground turbulent diffusion of theta, TKE, emissions, water vapor, oxygen, or
any other scalar passed through calcForceTurb.

Use separate vertical indices in diffuse: keep km1 for arrays that only exist on 1:lls, but use k0=max(k-1,0)
for the scalar field declared on 0:lls.

BUG-2026-08-060: SUBGRIDTURB-010: calcForceTurb ignores its

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/subGridTurb/SUBGRIDTURB-010.md

calcForceTurb accepts caller-provided array bounds and a caller-provided vertical extent:

subroutine calcForceTurb(xv,force_xv,il,iu,jl,ju,lls,nv)

  ...

But every turbulence kernel is called with the module-global l, not the dummy argument lls:

        call diffuse(force_xv(:,:,:,kv),xvrho(:,:,:,kv), &
          1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,one)

The current top-level caller happens to pass the global l:

! force.F90
if(iturb.eq.2) call calcForceTurb(xv,forceSE_xv, &
  1-ih,np+ih,1-ih,mp+ih,l,nv)

stressrij also allocates its work arrays with global l, even though its loops use the passed lls:

subroutine stressrij(fx,fy,fz,il,iu,jl,ju,lls)
  use gridlist_variables, only : l,wp
  ...
  integer,intent(in) :: il,iu,jl,ju,lls
  real(wp),intent(inout) :: fx(il:iu,jl:ju,lls)
  ...

 781

    allocate(AB21c(np+1,mp,l),AB22c(np,mp+1,l),AB23c(np,mp,l+1))
    allocate(AB31c(np+1,mp,l),AB32c(np,mp+1,l),AB33c(np,mp,l+1))
    allocate(Ci(np+1,mp,l),Cj(np,mp+1,l),Ck(np,mp,l+1))
 ...
 do k=1,lls
 ...
    do k=1,lls+1

Problem
The subroutine interface says the caller controls the vertical extent through lls, but the implementation
silently overrides that with the module-global l.
If a future caller passes a shorter test array, partial column, or nested vertical extent with lls < l, the
downstream kernels receive l and can read or write beyond the actual xv(:,:,:,kv) / force_xv(:,:,:,kv)
sections. If a caller passes lls > l, the wrapper still sends only l layers to the kernels, so the extra
layers are never forced.
stressrij has the same contract problem at the kernel level: a direct call with lls > l would run loops
to lls using work arrays that were only allocated to l.
The current production call is safe only because force.F90 passes lls=l. The routine is not safe as a
reusable calcForceTurb(...,lls,...) API, and the implicit external procedure style makes this hard for
the compiler to catch.

Minimal no-behavior-change fix: make the full-column requirement explicit and fail before any kernel
receives mismatched array bounds.

BUG-2026-08-061: SUBGRIDTURB-012: Scalar diffusion top face
can leak horizontal gradients as vertical flux

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/subGridTurb/SUBGRIDTURB-012.md

 785

The terrain metric factor gmul is stored at cell centers:

! metric.F90
22 do k=1,l
23     gdeform=aa3*z(k)**3+aa2*z(k)**2+aa1*z(k)
24     gdeform1=3*aa3*z(k)**2+2*aa2*z(k)+aa1
25 gmul(k)=(zb-gdeform)/gdeform1

At the physical top face, the mapping reaches gdeform = zb, so the corresponding face value of this
terrain metric factor should be zero. But diffuse has no face metric and reuses the top cell-center value
gmul(lls).

Problem
At the top face, k=lls+1, the code sets:

kk = lls
km1 = lls
pz = (phi(i,j,lls)-phi(i,j,lls))*dzi = 0

That zeroes the normal scalar gradient, which is the intended hard-coded top boundary behavior.
However, the same top-face flux still includes:

hzc_top = sqrtG_KG31a * dphi_dx_top + sqrtG_KG32a * dphi_dy_top

because sqrtG_KG31a and sqrtG_KG32a are computed from c13/c23 * gmul(lls), not from the metric at the
actual top face.
On flat terrain, c13 and c23 are zero, so the bug is hidden. On sloped terrain, any horizontal scalar
gradient in the top cell can generate a nonzero vertical flux through the top boundary even though
the code is trying to impose a zero-gradient/no-flux top condition. This can spuriously add or remove
theta, TKE, emissions species, water vapor, oxygen, mixture fraction, or any other scalar diffused by
calcForceTurb.
This is distinct from SUBGRIDTURB-008: that report covers the bottom face ignoring the ground ghost
layer; this one covers the top face using interior terrain cross metrics after the normal top gradient has
been clamped to zero.

If the intended top boundary is zero normal scalar flux, explicitly leave the top vertical face flux at
zero. The arrays are initialized to zero, so the loop can skip k=lls+1:

+++ b/CODE-dev/subGridTurb/diffuse_turb.F90
@@
 ! compute contravariant component z-flux at i,j,k-1/2 hzc (sqrtg burried in) top boundary
 ,→ condition on phi, rvtxy, rvtya is burried here (kk=l when k=l+1)
   do k=1,lls+1
+ if(k.eq.lls+1) cycle
     km1=max(1,k-1)
 kk=min(k,lls)

 786

If the top boundary is meant to support a nonzero specified flux instead, then the safer fix is to compute
true vertical-face metric factors, using zero terrain cross terms at zedge(lls+1), rather than reusing
gmul(lls) from the top cell center.

Git evidence: 27c7afa (2026-08-17, subgrid turbulence and thermodynamics bug-list pass); 44f9732
(2026-08-25, subgrid diffusion cleanup and small bug fix).
The scalar diffusion top-face loop now stops at the real top face and avoids leaking horizontal-gradient
terms into the vertical flux through an extra top level.

BUG-2026-08-062: THERMODYNAMICS-001: Gas mixture
molecular weight is averaged with the wrong weights

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/thermodynamicsF90/THERMODYNAMICS-001.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/thermodynamics
 ,→ .F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/domainUpdates
 ,→ .F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/rinit.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/higrad.F90

domainUpdates.F90 passes emitted species divided by gas density into updateGasThermProps, so yEmit is
being used as a mass fraction vector:

call updateGasThermProps( &
  xv(i,j,k,iEmitStart:iEmitStop)/xv(i,j,k,irho), &
  cpEmit,mwEmit,nEmit,xv(i,j,k,itheta)/xv(i,j,k,irho), &
  xv(i,j,k,irho),cp_gas(i,j,k),cv_gas(i,j,k),mw_gas(i,j,k), &
  pr(i,j,k),tempg(i,j,k))

thermodynamics.F90 correctly mass-weights cp_gas, but it also mass-weights molecular weight directly:

cp_gas=sum(cpEmit*yEmit)+cp_N2*(1.0_wp-sum(yEmit))
mw_gas=sum(mwEmit*yEmit)+MW_N2*(1.0_wp-sum(yEmit))
cv_gas=cp_gas-Rgas/mw_gas

The initial ambient profile in rinit.F90 uses the same direct molecular-weight average:

yH2O=specificHumidity
yO2 =0.233_wp/(specificHumidity+1.0_wp)
yN2 =1.0_wp-yH2O-yO2
cpGas=yH2O*1996.0_wp+yO2*918.0_wp+yN2*1040.0_wp
mwGas=yH2O*18.015_wp+yO2*31.998_wp+yN2*28.014_wp

Problem
For mass fractions Y_i, mixture heat capacity can be computed as sum(Y_i * cp_i), but mixture molecular
weight must be computed from the reciprocal relation:

1 / MW_mix = sum(Y_i / MW_i)

The current code instead computes MW_mix = sum(Y_i * MW_i), which is the mole-fraction style average
applied to mass fractions. That gives the wrong specific gas constant Rgas / mw_gas, which then feeds
cv_gas, pressure, temperature, and the pressure-gradient calculation in higrad.F90.

 789

Because setRhoThetaP uses the same arithmetic molecular-weight average, fixing only thermodynamics.F90
would make the runtime update more correct but leave initialization on the old equation. Both places
should use the reciprocal mass-fraction formula.

Use a reciprocal molecular-weight sum wherever the species composition is represented by mass
fractions.

diff --git a/CODE-dev/thermodynamics.F90 b/CODE-dev/thermodynamics.F90

@@
- cp_gas=sum(cpEmit*yEmit)+cp_N2*(1.0_wp-sum(yEmit))
- mw_gas=sum(mwEmit*yEmit)+MW_N2*(1.0_wp-sum(yEmit))

+ cp_gas=sum(cpEmit*yEmit)+cp_N2*yN2
+ inv_mw_gas=sum(yEmit/mwEmit)+yN2/MW_N2

BUG-2026-08-063: TINIT-001: Exponential top absorber is strongest
at the bottom of the sponge

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/tinitF90/TINIT-001.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/tinit.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/boundary.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.
 ,→ F90

tinit.F90 computes the top absorber only above zab. For iab=2, it uses the distance upward from the
bottom of the absorber:

    t1=max(0.0_wp,zl-zab)

 case(2)
        relaxxv(i,j,k,:)=0.05_wp*exp(-t1/(-(zb-zab)/log(tow**(-2.0_wp))))

The relaxation coefficient is later applied as a force toward the environmental field:

force(i,j,k,kv)=force(i,j,k,kv)+relaxxv(i,j,k,min(kv,4))* &
  (xe(i,j,k,kv)-xv(i,j,k,kv))/dt

The default value of tow is greater than 1:

real(wp) :: tow = 10.0_wp ! Magnitude parameter for top relaxation

Problem
With the default tow=10, the denominator in the iab=2 expression is positive. Since t1 is zero at the
bottom of the top sponge and grows upward, the coefficient is largest at zab:

at zl = zab: relaxxv = 0.05
near zl = zb: relaxxv approaches 0.05 / tow**2

That is reversed for a top sponge layer. The strongest damping should be near the top boundary and
should decay inward toward the bottom of the absorber. The other top absorber shapes in the same
routine increase upward, while this exponential option decreases upward.
This makes iab=2 damp interior flow at the entrance to the sponge more strongly than the top boundary
itself, increasing the chance of artificial reflections and leaving the actual outlet weakly controlled.

 792

Use distance from the top boundary for the exponential decay, rather than distance from the bottom
of the absorber.

+++ b/CODE-dev/tinit.F90
@@
 case(2)
-                relaxxv(i,j,k,:)=0.05_wp*exp(-t1/(-(zb-zab)/log(tow**(-2.0_wp))))
+                relaxxv(i,j,k,:)=0.05_wp*exp(-max(0.0_wp,zb-zl)/ &
+                  (-(zb-zab)/log(tow**(-2.0_wp))))

This keeps the same endpoint ratio but puts the maximum coefficient at the top of the domain and the
minimum coefficient near zab.

The top-absorber exponential profile in CODE-dev/tinit.F90 now uses the corrected denominator/sign
convention and validates unsupported absorber modes.

BUG-2026-08-064: VARIABLES-001: namefile builds invalid names
when the base has no trailing blank

Source report: Completed_Bugs/aa-Aug14/variablesF90/VARIABLES-001.md

• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/variables.
 ,→ F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/io.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Firebrands/
   ,→ io_fb.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/xeVariation
 ,→ /windfield.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/HeatSource/
 ,→ rinit_heat.F90
• /Users/colbyfronk/Downloads/FIRETEC_versions/version_151_June26/higrad-firetec/CODE-dev/Sensors/
 ,→ rinit_sense.F90

variables.F90 provides a shared filename helper:

subroutine namefile(itn,fnamein,fnameout)
  ...

  character(len=10) :: fend

  write(fend,"(i0)") itn
  indx=index(fnamein,’␣’)
  fnameout=fnamein(1:indx-1)//’.’//fend
end subroutine namefile

io.F90 has the same whitespace-based pattern inline:

write(fend,"(i0)") ittot
it=index(outname,’␣’)
fname=outname(1:it-1)//’.’//fend

Several callers rely on namefile for windfield, firebrand, heat-source, sensor, and xe-variation input/out-
put names.

Problem
The helper assumes the first blank marks the end of the input path. That is brittle for fixed-length
strings and wrong for valid paths:

• if fnamein has no blank because it exactly fills its declared length, index(fnamein,’ ’) returns 0, so
  fnamein(1:indx-1) becomes an invalid substring;
• if a valid path contains an embedded blank, the filename is truncated at that blank;

 795

• fend is only 10 characters, so a larger iteration value can overflow the internal write before the
  filename is built;
• fnameout length is not checked, so long base paths can be silently truncated.

The outname path in io.F90 has the same failure mode, while other output paths go through namefile.

Use len_trim rather than searching for a blank, make the suffix buffer large enough for ordinary integer
formats, and fail before truncating the output name. Then use the shared helper in io.F90 so all
generated filenames follow the same rules.

+++ b/CODE-dev/variables.F90
@@
 subroutine namefile(itn,fnamein,fnameout)

@@
- character(*),intent(inout) :: fnameout
+ character(*),intent(out) :: fnameout

- integer :: indx
- character(len=10) :: fend
+ integer :: base_len,out_len
+ character(len=32) :: fend

 ! Executable Code
 write(fend,"(i0)") itn
- indx=index(fnamein,’ ’)
- fnameout=fnamein(1:indx-1)//’.’//fend
+ base_len=len_trim(fnamein)
+ if(base_len.le.0) stop ’namefile: empty base filename’
+ out_len=base_len+1+len_trim(fend)
+ if(out_len.gt.len(fnameout)) stop ’namefile: output filename is too short’
+ fnameout=fnamein(1:base_len)//’.’//trim(fend)

 end subroutine namefile

+++ b/CODE-dev/io.F90
@@
- integer :: it,ift
- character(len=10) :: fend
+ integer :: it,ift
 character(len=257) :: fname

 ! Executable Code
- write(fend,"(i0)") ittot
- it=index(outname,’ ’)
-   fname=outname(1:it-1)//’.’//fend
+ call namefile(ittot,outname,fname)
 if(mpi_rank.eq.0) print*,trim(fname)

 796

namefile now uses len_trim and a longer suffix buffer so filenames are valid even when the base name

  real(wp),allocatable :: xvfuelLim(:,:) ! limits on non-advected field

The live limiter array is the one from forcings. It is allocated in Vegetation/definearray_veg.F90:

  xvfuelLim

It is then configured and consumed through forcings:

array, but it is never allocated or initialized in the current tree.

from xvall and leave the current live owner, forcings, unchanged.

BUG-2026-09-001: Firebrands landing exactly on upper/right edges
skip boundary handling

Firebrands/bug_001_exact_domain_edges_not_handled.md
Disposition: Completed report; refreshed September 2 develop source still has no implementation
evidence for this exact-edge fix

• CODE-dev/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90

Problem
The report identifies a regression in evolveFB: right and top lateral boundary checks use strict outside-
domain tests. A brand at exactly x == n*dx or y == m*dy remains active, then updateFB can map it to
processor coordinate nprocx or nprocy, one past the valid decomposition.

Impact
Exact-edge coordinates can index sndBrands out of bounds or attempt to send a brand to an invalid
owning rank. This is a multi-rank correctness and stability risk for firebrand transport.

The report recommends restoring inclusive upper-edge handling by changing the right/top tests to .ge.
before rank ownership is computed.

Restore inclusive handling for the upper/right global edges that otherwise map past the valid processor
range.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
@@
- else if(xvbrand(it,ix).gt.(n*dx))then ! Outside x domain on right
+ else if(xvbrand(it,ix).ge.(n*dx))then ! Outside x domain on right
@@
- else if(xvbrand(it,iy).gt.m*dy)then ! Outside y domain on top
+ else if(xvbrand(it,iy).ge.m*dy)then ! Outside y domain on top

Git evidence: Refreshed develop was checked through 1f27c62 (2026-09-02, firebrand bugs fixed).
The newer firebrand commit changes evolve_fb.F90, but it does not change the right/top exact-edge
boundary comparisons.
The latest checked dev source still contains the strict comparisons:

 805

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log September 2026

else if(xvbrand(it,ix).gt.(n*dx))then ! Outside x domain on right
...
else if(xvbrand(it,iy).gt.m*dy)then ! Outside y domain on top
...
npos=floor(xvbrand(it,ix)/dx/np)
mpos=floor(xvbrand(it,iy)/dy/mp)

BUG-2026-09-002: updateFB sends strided firebrand records as
contiguous data

Firebrands/bug_002_updatefb_alltoallv_sends_strided_brand_records_as_contiguous.md

• CODE-dev/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90

Problem
updateFB packed destination records into xvsndBrands(mxbrand,nvbrand,numprocs) as xvsndBrands(row,:,dest
,→ ), then tried to send sndBrands(dest)*nvbrand contiguous values with mpi_alltoallv. In Fortran
column-major storage, those active rows are strided unless the destination plane is completely full.

Impact
Transferred firebrands could receive gaps, stale values, or shifted attributes for position, velocity, size,
temperature, density, and related fields when brands migrate across MPI ranks.

Either repack into a truly contiguous exchange buffer or restore fixed-size per-destination transfers
with the existing plane layout.

Restore fixed-size per-destination transfers with the existing contiguous plane layout while keeping the
mpi_wp datatype cleanup.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
@@
- call mpi_alltoallv(xvsndBrands,sndBrands*nvbrand,sndDispls,mpi_wp, &
- xvrcvBrands,rcvBrands*nvbrand,rcvDispls,mpi_wp,mpi_comm_world, &
- ierror)
+ call mpi_alltoall(xvsndBrands,nsize,mpi_wp,xvrcvBrands,nsize,mpi_wp, &
+ mpi_comm_world,ierror)

A lower-volume alternative would repack into a truly contiguous one-dimensional send buffer or change
the array layout so each destination’s complete records are contiguous.

The committed fix removes the displacement arrays and replaces the variable-count collective with a
fixed-size mpi_alltoall over each full destination plane.

BUG-2026-09-003: writeio_fb gathers firebrand arrays into the
wrong 2D layout

Firebrands/bug_003_writeio_gatherv_scrambles_multirank_output_layout.md

• CODE-dev/Firebrands/io_fb.F90

Problem
writeio_fb replaced one mpi_gatherv per firebrand variable with one gather over the whole xvbrand(
,→ numBrands,nvbrand) array. That assumes each rank’s row block is contiguous in the root xvtotBrands(
,→ totalBrands,nvbrand) array, but Fortran stores the columns separately.

Impact
Multi-rank firebrand output files could mix or shift brand attributes between columns. Serial output
and some trivial rank layouts could appear correct, masking the bug.

Restore column-wise gathers, or use derived MPI datatypes that describe strided firebrand records
correctly.

Suggested fixes
The smallest correctness fix is to restore per-column gathering while keeping mpi_wp.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Firebrands/io_fb.F90
@@
- call mpi_gatherv(xvbrand,numBrands*nvbrand,mpi_wp, &
- xvtotBrands,totNumBrands*nvbrand,displs*nvbrand,mpi_wp,0, &

+ do it=1,nvbrand
+ call mpi_gatherv(xvbrand(:,it),numBrands,mpi_wp, &
+ xvtotBrands(:,it),totNumBrands,displs,mpi_wp,0, &
+ mpi_comm_world,ierror)
+ enddo

The raw report also describes a higher-effort single-collective version using derived row datatypes so
xvbrand(brand,1:nvbrand) records are sent and received into strided row slices without reverting to a
per-column loop.

The committed fix restores the per-variable gather loop while retaining mpi_wp.

BUG-2026-09-004: writeio_fb uses an unallocated receive buffer on
non-root ranks

Firebrands/bug_004_writeio_deallocates_unallocated_buffer_on_nonroot.md

• CODE-dev/Firebrands/io_fb.F90

Problem
xvtotBrands was allocated only on rank 0, but all ranks passed it to mpi_gatherv and reached the later
deallocation. Non-root ranks therefore supplied and deallocated an unallocated allocatable buffer.

Impact
Multi-process firebrand output could abort at output time or pass an invalid actual argument through
the Fortran MPI interface on non-root ranks.

Ensure all ranks have a defined receive buffer and gather metadata, then deallocate only allocated
storage.

Allocate a harmless zero-row receive buffer and define receive metadata on non-root ranks, then guard
the deallocation.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Firebrands/io_fb.F90
@@

 allocate(xvtotBrands(sum(totNumBrands),nvbrand))
 displs(1) = 0 ! compute displacements
@@
 enddo
 endif
+ else

BUG-2026-09-006: Aerosol Stokes drag divides by zero at the ground

forceF90/bug_002_aerosol_stokes_drag_ground_divide_by_zero.md

• CODE-dev/force.F90
• CODE-dev/Emissions/stokesDrag_ems.F90

Problem
The new aerosol-settling call in force.F90 made stokesDrag active for aerosol-enabled runs. Its ground
branch divided by zcart(zedge(1),i,j)-zs(i,j); because zedge(1) is zero, that denominator is exactly
the ground height minus itself.

Impact
Runs with iemissions > 0 and aerosol moments could generate infinite or NaN aerosol forcing in the
first vertical level.

Use a nonzero near-ground distance in the deposition term instead of the ground edge-to-ground
difference.

Minimal suggested fix
The source report recommended correcting the ground deposition formula before enabling stokesDrag
broadly. The underlying issue was the denominator zcart(zedge(1),i,j)-zs(i,j), which is identically
zero because zedge(1)=0.

! Bad ground denominator from the raw report
forcingAero(i,j,1,nMAero*(it-1)+r)= &
  forcingAero(i,j,1,nMAero*(it-1)+r)+w_set* &
  ((iMp-iM)/(zcart(zedge(2),i,j)-zcart(zedge(1),i,j))- &
    iM/(zcart(zedge(1),i,j)-zs(i,j)))

A minimal physical correction is to use a nonzero ground-to-cell distance or first-cell thickness for the
deposition term, with a defensive call-site option if settling is not ready for all aerosol modes.

Git evidence: 89b4563 (2026-09-02, emissions fixes).
The committed fix uses distances involving zedge(2) and zedge(3), avoiding the zero-height denominator
at zedge(1).

BUG-2026-09-017: iab=2 top absorber exponential has the wrong sign

• CODE-dev/tinit.F90

BUG-2026-09-018: Firebrand halo-padded arrays are remapped with
interior-only bounds

FIREBRANDS-003.md

• CODE-dev/Firebrands/firebrand_fb.F90
• CODE-dev/Firebrands/generation_fb.F90
• CODE-dev/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90

firebrand receives halo-padded gas and fuel-temperature arrays and passes them into lower firebrand
routines:

real(wp),intent(in) :: rhog(ilh:iuh,jlh:juh,lls)
real(wp),intent(in) :: tempg(ilh:iuh,jlh:juh,lls)
real(wp),intent(in) :: temps(nfuel,ilh:iuh,jlh:juh,lfuel)

The raw report noted that launchFB and evolveFB redeclared some of those same arrays with interior-only
dummy bounds:

real(wp),intent(in) :: rhog(il:iu,jl:ju,lls)
real(wp),intent(in) :: temps(nfuel,il:iu,jl:ju,lfuel)
real(wp),intent(in) :: tempg(il:iu,jl:ju,lls)

Problem
These are explicit-shape dummy arrays, not assumed-shape arrays. When a halo-padded actual array
is passed to a callee with different lower bounds and extents, the callee’s first declared interior element
is associated with the first stored element of the actual array, not the same physical cell. With the
normal halo layout, launchFB and evolveFB could therefore read shifted halo or neighbor values for rhog,
temps, and tempg.

Impact
The shifted reads can alter launch decisions, initial firebrand temperature, kinematic viscosity, burning
rates, and trajectory updates. The error is especially dangerous because the arrays are still in bounds
locally; the physics is wrong without necessarily crashing.

Keep halo-padded bounds in lower routines for arrays received from halo-padded callers.

BUG-2026-09-019: GetWind reverses lower-side interpolation weights

FIREBRANDS-007.md

• CODE-dev/Firebrands/functions_fb.F90

GetWind stored an absolute distance from the current cell center and then reused the same endpoint-weight
order on both sides of the center:

if(x_p.gt.x_c)then
  ip=i+1
  im=i
  xd=(x_p-x_c)/dx
else
  ip=i
  im=i-1
  xd=(x_c-x_p)/dx
endif

The y and z branches followed the same pattern, then the interpolation used (1-xd), xd, (1-yd), yd,
(1-zd), and zd as if the chosen lower endpoint were always the lower-weight side.

Problem
When a point lies on the low side of a cell center, the weights are reversed. At x_p == x_c, for example,
the lower-side branch chooses im=i-1, ip=i, and xd=0; the interpolated value should be cell i, but the
shared weighting order selects the lower neighbor. The same reversal applies in y and z.

Impact
Firebrands could sample winds from the wrong side of the cell center and see discontinuous wind
changes when crossing center planes. That perturbation feeds directly into velocity and trajectory
integration.

Compute endpoint weights when the endpoints are chosen, then reuse those weights in all three
interpolation blocks.

diff --git a/CODE-dev/Firebrands/functions_fb.F90 b/CODE-dev/Firebrands/functions_fb.F90

+ real(wp) :: wxm,wxp,wym,wyp,wzm,wzp

+   wxm=1._wp-wxp
@@
-   xd=(x_c-x_p)/dx
+   wxm=(x_c-x_p)/dx
+   wxp=1._wp-wxm
@@
- u00=u_c(im,jm,km)*(1-xd)+u_c(ip,jm,km)*xd
+ u00=u_c(im,jm,km)*wxm+u_c(ip,jm,km)*wxp

The raw report applies the same wxm/wxp, wym/wyp, and wzm/wzp replacement to the u_c, v_c, and w_c
trilinear interpolation blocks.

The committed change replaces the scalar distances with signed endpoint weights and uses those
weights throughout the u, v, and w interpolation blocks.

FIRETEC Bug Resolution Log September 2026

BUG-2026-09-024: Firebrand drag acceleration omits mass and uses
ambient velocity direction

FIREBRANDS-017.md
Disposition: Completed with a residual implementation note

• CODE-dev/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90

evolveFB computed particle-air velocity differences and a slip-speed magnitude:

w_bx=(xvbrand(it,iuvel)-xvu)**2
w_by=(xvbrand(it,ivvel)-xvv)**2
w_bz=(xvbrand(it,iwvel)-xvw)**2
w_absz=sqrt(w_bx+w_by+w_bz)

The drag scale omitted firebrand mass, then the update accelerated in the direction of the ambient
velocity:

A_ek=0.5_wp*Ac*rhog(i,j,k)

xvbrand(it,iuvel)=xvbrand(it,iuvel)+xvu*A_ek*w_abs*dt
xvbrand(it,ivvel)=xvbrand(it,ivvel)+xvv*A_ek*w_abs*dt
xvbrand(it,iwvel)=xvbrand(it,iwvel)-g*dt+xvw*A_ek*w_absz*dt

Problem
A_ek had force-like scaling but was applied directly to velocity without division by firebrand mass. The
direction was also based on absolute ambient velocity rather than signed slip velocity (air velocity -
,→ particle velocity). With zero ambient wind, a moving firebrand received no horizontal drag; with a
tailwind, a firebrand already faster than the wind could still be accelerated in the wind direction.

Impact
The velocity increment was dimensionally inconsistent and could push particles in the wrong direction
relative to the surrounding air, changing firebrand travel distance and residence time.

Compute firebrand mass from shape and apply drag along signed slip velocity.

+++ b/CODE-dev/Firebrands/evolve_fb.F90
@@

+ real(wp) :: A_ek,massFB
+ real(wp) :: du,dv,dw

+ case(3)
+ massFB=xvbrand(it,irho)*4.0_wp/3.0_wp*pi*xvbrand(it,irad)**3
+ end select
+    A_ek=0.5_wp*Ac*rhog(i,j,k)/massFB
+ du=xvu-xvbrand(it,iuvel)

- xvbrand(it,ivvel)=xvbrand(it,ivvel)+xvv*A_ek*w_abs*dt
